text_mt: taking a fearsome skull-staff in her hand, sprinkling [blood], terrible like a receptacle of black collyrium, / her limbs withered, her body drenched in blood, wearing a garland of kingly human heads.

sanskrit_iast:
kāṃścit khaḍgena ciccheda khaṭvāṅgena parān raṇe /
nyaṣūdayad bhṛśaṃ kruddhā saratāśvagajān ripūn //
meaning:
कांश्चित् खड्गेन चिच्छेद खट्वाङ्गेन परान् रणे /
न्यषूदयद् भृशं क्रुद्धा सरताश्वगजान् रिपून् //
text_mt: Some she cut down with her sword, others she slew with her skull-staff in battle; / furiously enraged, she slaughtered the enemies with their chariots, horses, and elephants.

sanskrit_iast:
carmāṅkuśaṃ mudgaraṃ ca sadhanuṣkaṃ saghaṇṭikam /
kuñjaraṃ saha yantreṇa pratikṣepa muke 'mbikā //
meaning:
चर्माङ्कुशं मुद्गरं च सधनुष्कं सघण्टिकम् /
कुञ्जरं सह यन्त्रेण प्रतिक्षेप मुके ऽम्बिका //
text_mt: The shield, the elephant-goad, the club, the bow, and the bell, / and the elephant along with its machine, Ambikā cast into her mouth.

sanskrit_iast:
sacakrakūbararathaṃ sasārathituraṅgamam /
samaṃ yodhena vadane kṣipya carvayate 'mbikā //
meaning:
सचक्रकूबररथं ससारथितुरङ्गमम् /
समं योधेन वदने क्षिप्य चर्वयते ऽम्बिका //
text_mt: The chariot with its wheels and axle-pole, along with the charioteer and the horses, / casting [all] together with the warrior into her mouth, Ambikā chewed them up.

sanskrit_iast:
ekaṃ jagrāha keśeṣu grīvāyamaparaṃ tathā /
pādenākramya caivānyaṃ preṣayāmāsa mṛtyave //
meaning:
एकं जग्राह केशेषु ग्रीवायमपरं तथा /
पादेनाक्रम्य चैवान्यं प्रेषयामास मृत्यवे //
text_mt: One she seized by the hair, another likewise by the neck; / and trampling yet another with her foot, she dispatched them to death.

sanskrit_iast:
tatastu tad balaṃ devyā bhakṣitaṃ sabalādhipam /
rururdṛṣṭvā pradudrāva taṃ caṇḍi dadṛśe svayam //
meaning:
ततस्तु तद् बलं देव्या भक्षितं सबलाधिपम् /
रुरुर्दृष्ट्वा प्रदुद्राव तं चण्डि ददृशे स्वयम् //
text_mt: Then, seeing that army along with its commanders devoured by the goddess, / Ruru fled away; and Caṇḍikā saw him herself.

sanskrit_iast:
ājaghānātha śirasi khaṭvāṅgena mahāsuram /
sa papāta hato bhūmyāṃ chinnamūla iva drumaḥ //
meaning:
आजघानाथ शिरसि खट्वाङ्गेन महासुरम् /
स पपात हतो भूम्यां छिन्नमूल इव द्रुमः //
text_mt: Then she struck the great asura upon his head with her skull-staff; / slain, he fell to the ground like a tree cut down at its roots.

sanskrit_iast:
tatastaṃ patitaṃ dṛṣṭvā paśoriva vibhāvarī /
kośamutkartayāmāsa karṇādicaraṇāntikam //
meaning:
ततस्तं पतितं दृष्ट्वा पशोरिव विभावरी /
कोशमुत्कर्तयामास कर्णादिचरणान्तिकम् //
text_mt: Then, seeing him fallen like a sacrificial beast, the dark night-like goddess / flayed off his skin from his ears down to his feet.

sanskrit_iast:
sā ca kośaṃ samādāya vabandha vimalā jaṭāḥ /
ekā na bandhamagamat tāmutpāṭyākṣipad bhuvi //
meaning:
सा च कोशं समादाय वबन्ध विमला जटाः /
एका न बन्धमगमत् तामुत्पाट्याक्षिपद् भुवि //
text_mt: Taking the skin, she bound up her spotless matted locks; / one [lock] could not be bound, so tearing it out she cast it upon the earth.

sanskrit_iast:
sā jātā sutarāṃ raudrī tailābhyaktaśiroruhā /
kuṣṇārdhamardhaśuklaṃ ca dhārayantī svakaṃ vapuḥ //
meaning:
सा जाता सुतरां रौद्री तैलाभ्यक्तशिरोरुहा /
कुष्णार्धमर्धशुक्लं च धारयन्ती स्वकं वपुः //
text_mt: She became exceedingly fierce, her hair smeared with oil, / bearing her body half-black and half-white.

sanskrit_iast:
sābravīdaṃ varamekaṃ tu mārayāmi mahāsuram /
tasyā nāma tadā cakre caṇḍamārīti viśrutam //
meaning:
साब्रवीदं वरमेकं तु मारयामि महासुरम् /
तस्या नाम तदा चक्रे चण्डमारीति विश्रुतम् //
text_mt: She said: “Granted this one boon, I will slay the great asura.” / Then her name was made famed as Caṇḍamārī.

sanskrit_iast:
prāha gacchasva subhage caṇḍamuṇḍāvihānaya /
svayaṃ hi mārayiṣyāmi tāvānetuṃ tvamarhasi //
meaning:
प्राह गच्छस्व सुभगे चण्डमुण्डाविहानय /
स्वयं हि मारयिष्यामि तावानेतुं त्वमर्हसि //
text_mt: [The goddess] said: “Go, auspicious one, and bring Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa here; / for I myself shall slay them; you ought to fetch the two.”

sanskrit_iast:
śrutvaivaṃ vacanaṃ devyāḥ sābhyadravat tāvubhau /
pradudruvaturbhayārttau diśamāśritya dakṣiṇām //
meaning:
श्रुत्वैवं वचनं देव्याः साभ्यद्रवत् तावुभौ /
प्रदुद्रुवतुर्भयार्त्तौ दिशमाश्रित्य दक्षिणाम् //
text_mt: Having heard this speech of the goddess, she rushed at the two; / afflicted with fear, they fled towards the southern quarter.

sanskrit_iast:
tatastāvapi vegena prādhāvat tyaktavāsasau /
sādhiruhya mahāvegaṃ rāsabhaṃ garuḍopamam //
meaning:
ततस्तावपि वेगेन प्राधावत् त्यक्तवाससौ /
साधिरुह्य महावेगं रासभं गरुडोपमम् //
text_mt: Then, casting off their clothes, they two ran with great speed; / and mounting a donkey of immense speed resembling Garuḍa,

sanskrit_iast:
yato gatau ca tau dautyau tatraivānuyayau śivā /
sā dadarśa tadā pauṇḍraṃ mahiṣaṃ vai masya ca //
meaning:
यतो गतौ च तौ दौत्यौ तत्रैवानुययौ शिवा /
सा ददर्श तदा पौण्ड्रं महिषं वै मस्य च //
text_mt: wherever those two Daityas went, there Śivā followed behind them. / She then saw a Pauṇḍra buffalo of [great] size,

sanskrit_iast:
sā tasyotpāṭayāmāsa viṣāṇaṃ bhujagākṛtim /
taṃ pragṛhya kareṇaiva dānavāvanvagājjavāt //
meaning:
सा तस्योत्पाटयामास विषाणं भुजगाकृतिम् /
तं प्रगृह्य करेणैव दानवावन्वगाज्जवात् //
text_mt: and she wrenched out its horn shaped like a serpent. / Seizing that in her hand, she pursued the two Dānavas with speed.

sanskrit_iast:
tau cāpi bhūmiṃ saṃtyajya jagmaturgaganaṃ tadā /
vegenābisṛtā sā ca rāsabhena maheśvarī //
meaning:
तौ चापि भूमिं संत्यज्य जग्मतुर्गगनं तदा /
वेगेनाबिसृता सा च रासभेन महेश्वरी //
text_mt: And leaving the earth, the two went into the sky at that time; / and the supreme goddess rushed after them with speed on the donkey.

sanskrit_iast:
tato dadarśa garuḍaṃ pannagendraṃ ciṣādiṣuma /
karkoṭakaṃ sa dṛṣṭvā ūrdhvaromā vyajāyata //
meaning:
ततो ददर्श गरुडं पन्नगेन्द्रं चिषादिषुम /
कर्कोटकं स दृष्ट्वा ऊर्ध्वरोमा व्यजायत //
text_mt: Then Garuḍa saw the lord of serpents eager to devour him; / seeing Karkoṭaka, his hair stood on end.

sanskrit_iast:
bhayānmāryaśca garuḍo māṃsapiṇḍopamo babhau /
nyapataṃstasya patrāṇi raudrāṇi hi patattriṇaḥ //
meaning:
भयान्मार्यश्च गरुडो मांसपिण्डोपमो बभौ /
न्यपतंस्तस्य पत्राणि रौद्राणि हि पतत्त्रिणः //
text_mt: From fear of the goddess Mārī, Garuḍa looked like a lump of flesh; / the dreadful feathers of that bird fell off.

sanskrit_iast:
khagendrapatrāṇyādāya nāgaṃ karkoṭakaṃ tathā /
vegenānusarad devī caṇḍamuṇḍau bhayāturau //
meaning:
खगेन्द्रपत्राण्यादाय नागं कर्कोटकं तथा /
वेगेनानुसरद् देवी चण्डमुण्डौ भयातुरौ //
text_mt: Taking the feathers of the king of birds and the serpent Karkoṭaka, / the goddess swiftly pursued Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, who were stricken with fear.

sanskrit_iast:
saṃprāptau ca tadā devyā caṇḍamuṇḍau mahāsurau /
baddhau karkoṭakenaiva baddhvā vindhyamupāgamat //
meaning:
संप्राप्तौ च तदा देव्या चण्डमुण्डौ महासुरौ /
बद्धौ कर्कोटकेनैव बद्ध्वा विन्ध्यमुपागमत् //
text_mt: Then the two great asuras, Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, were caught by the goddess; / bound with Karkoṭaka alone, having bound them, she approached the Vindhya mountain.

sanskrit_iast:
nivedayitvā kauśikyai kośamādāya bheravam /
śirobhirdānavendrāṇāṃ tārkṣyapatraiśca śobhanaiḥ //
meaning:
निवेदयित्वा कौशिक्यै कोशमादाय भेरवम् /
शिरोभिर्दानवेन्द्राणां तार्क्ष्यपत्रैश्च शोभनैः //
text_mt: Having announced [them] to Kauśikī, taking the terrible skin, / with the heads of the Dānava lords and the splendid feathers of Tārkṣya,

sanskrit_iast:
kṛtvā srajamanaupamyāṃ caṇḍikāyai nyavedayat /
ghargharāṃ ca mṛgendrasya carmaṇaḥ sā samārpayat //
meaning:
कृत्वा स्रजमनौपम्यां चण्डिकायै न्यवेदयत् /
घर्घरां च मृगेन्द्रस्य चर्मणः सा समार्पयत् //
text_mt: having made an incomparable garland, she offered it to Caṇḍikā; / and she presented a rattle made from the lion's skin.

sanskrit_iast:
srajamanyaiḥ khagendrasya patrairmūrghni nibadhya ca /
ātmanā sā papau pānaṃ rudhiraṃ dānaveṣvapi //
meaning:
स्रजमन्यैः खगेन्द्रस्य पत्रैर्मूर्घ्नि निबध्य च /
आत्मना सा पपौ पानं रुधिरं दानवेष्वपि //
text_mt: Having tied a garland with other feathers of the king of birds upon her head, / she herself drank the drink, blood among the Dānavas.

sanskrit_iast:
caṇḍā tvādāya caṇḍaṃ ca muṇḍaṃ cāsuranāyakam /
cakāra kupitā durgā viśiraskau mahāsurau //
meaning:
चण्डा त्वादाय चण्डं च मुण्डं चासुरनायकम् /
चकार कुपिता दुर्गा विशिरस्कौ महासुरौ //
text_mt: Seizing Caṇḍa, and Muṇḍa the leader of the asuras, / the enraged Durgā rendered the two great asuras headless.

sanskrit_iast:
tayorevāhinā devī śekharaṃ suṣkarevatī /
kṛtvā jagāma kauśikyāḥ sakāśaṃ māryayā saha //
meaning:
तयोरेवाहिना देवी शेखरं सुष्करेवती /
कृत्वा जगाम कौशिक्याः सकाशं मार्यया सह //
text_mt: With their [heads] the beautiful goddess, having made a crest-garland with the serpent, / went to the presence of Kauśikī along with Mārī.

sanskrit_iast:
sametya sābravīd devi gṛhyatāṃ śekharottamaḥ /
grathito daityaśīrṣābhyāṃ nāgarājena veṣṭitaḥ //
meaning:
समेत्य साब्रवीद् देवि गृह्यतां शेखरोत्तमः /
ग्रथितो दैत्यशीर्षाभ्यां नागराजेन वेष्टितः //
text_mt: Approaching, she said: “O goddess, take this excellent crest, / strung with the two Daitya heads and entwined by the king of serpents.”

sanskrit_iast:
taṃ śekharaṃ śivā gṛhya caṇḍāyā mūrdhni vistṛtam /
babandha prāha caivaināṃ kṛtaṃ karma sudāruṇam //
meaning:
तं शेखरं शिवा गृह्य चण्डाया मूर्ध्नि विस्तृतम् /
बबन्ध प्राह चैवैनां कृतं कर्म सुदारुणम् //
text_mt: Taking that crest, Śivā bound it broad upon the head of Caṇḍā / and spoke to her: “You have performed a very dreadful deed.

sanskrit_iast:
śekharaṃ caṇḍamuṇḍābhyāṃ yasmād dhārayase śubham /
tasmālloke tava khyātiścāmuṇḍeti bhaviṣyati //
meaning:
शेखरं चण्डमुण्डाभ्यां यस्माद् धारयसे शुभम् /
तस्माल्लोके तव ख्यातिश्चामुण्डेति भविष्यति //
text_mt: Since you wear this auspicious crest from Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, / therefore your fame in the world shall be Cāmuṇḍā.”

sanskrit_iast:
ityevamuktvā vacanaṃ trinetrā mā caṇḍamuṇḍasrajadhāriṇīṃ vai /
digvāsasaṃ cābhyavadat pratītā niṣūdaya khāribalānyamūni //
meaning:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा वचनं त्रिनेत्रा मा चण्डमुण्डस्रजधारिणीं वै /
दिग्वाससं चाभ्यवदत् प्रतीता निषूदय खारिबलान्यमूनि //
text_mt: Having spoken this word, the three-eyed goddess, pleased, said to that sky-clad one wearing the garland of Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa: / “Destroy these hostile forces!”

sanskrit_iast:
sā tvevamuktātha viṣāṇakoṭyā suvegayuktena ca rāsabhena /
niṣūdayantī ripusainyamugraṃ cacāra cānyānasurāṃścakhāda //
meaning:
सा त्वेवमुक्ताथ विषाणकोट्या सुवेगयुक्तेन च रासभेन /
निषूदयन्ती रिपुसैन्यमुग्रं चचार चान्यानसुरांश्चखाद //
text_mt: Thus addressed, she, destroying the fierce enemy army with the tip of the horn / and with her swift donkey, roamed about and devoured the other asuras.

sanskrit_iast:
tato 'mbikāyāstvatha carmamuṇḍayā māryā ca siṃhena ca bhūtasaṃghaiḥ /
nipātyamānā danupuṅgavāste kakudminaṃ śumbhamupāśrayanta //
iti śrīvāmanapurāṇe ekonatriṃśodhyāyaḥ
meaning:
ततो ऽम्बिकायास्त्वथ चर्ममुण्डया मार्या च सिंहेन च भूतसंघैः /
निपात्यमाना दनुपुङ्गवास्ते ककुद्मिनं शुम्भमुपाश्रयन्त //
इति श्रीवामनपुराणे एकोनत्रिंशोध्यायः
text_mt:
Then, being struck down by Ambikā, by Carmamuṇḍā, / by Mārī, by the lion, and by the hosts of spirits, those bulls among the Danus took refuge with the hump-backed Śumbha.

Thus ends the twenty-ninth chapter in the glorious Vāmana Purāṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
pulastya uvāca /
caṇḍamuṇḍau ca nihatau sainyaṃ ca vidrutam /
samādideśātibalaṃ raktabījaṃ mahāsuram /
akṣauhiṇīnāṃ triṃśadbhiḥ koṭibhiḥ parivāritam //
meaning:
पुलस्त्य उवाच /
चण्डमुण्डौ च निहतौ सैन्यं च विद्रुतम् /
समादिदेशातिबलं रक्तबीजं महासुरम् /
अक्षौहिणीनां त्रिंशद्भिः कोटिभिः परिवारितम् //
text_mt: Pulastya said: / [Seeing] Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa slain and the army put to flight, / [Śumbha] commanded the mighty great asura Raktabīja, / surrounded by thirty crores of akṣauhiṇīs.

sanskrit_iast:
tamāpatantaṃ daityānāṃ balaṃ dṛṣṭvaiva caṇḍikā /
mumoca siṃhanādaṃ vai tābhyāṃ saha maheśvarī //
meaning:
तमापतन्तं दैत्यानां बलं दृष्ट्वैव चण्डिका /
मुमोच सिंहनादं वै ताभ्यां सह महेश्वरी //
text_mt: Seeing that army of Daityas rushing forward, Caṇḍikā, / the supreme goddess, let loose a lion-roar along with those two.

sanskrit_iast:
ninadantyāstato devyā brahmāṇī mukhato 'bhavat /
haṃsayuktavimānasthā sākṣasūtrakamaṇḍaluḥ //
meaning:
निनदन्त्यास्ततो देव्या ब्रह्माणी मुखतो ऽभवत् /
हंसयुक्तविमानस्था साक्षसूत्रकमण्डलुः //
text_mt: Then, from the roaring goddess, Brahmāṇī came forth from her mouth, / seated upon an aerial chariot drawn by swans, with a rosary and a water-pot.

sanskrit_iast:
māheśvarī trinetrā ca vṛṣārūḍhā triśūlinī /
mahāhivalayā raudrā jātā kuṇḍalinī kṣaṇāt //
meaning:
माहेश्वरी त्रिनेत्रा च वृषारूढा त्रिशूलिनी /
महाहिवलया रौद्रा जाता कुण्डलिनी क्षणात् //
text_mt: And Māheśvarī, three-eyed, mounted upon a bull, holding a trident, / with great serpents as bracelets, terrible, wearing earrings, arose in an instant.

sanskrit_iast:
kaṇṭhādatha ca kaumārī barhipatrā ca śaktinī /
samudbhūtā ca devarṣe mayūravaravāhanā //
meaning:
कण्ठादथ च कौमारी बर्हिपत्रा च शक्तिनी /
समुद्भूता च देवर्षे मयूरवरवाहना //
text_mt: Then from her neck arose Kaumārī, with peacock feathers, holding a spear, / mounted on an excellent peacock as her vehicle, O divine sage.

sanskrit_iast:
bāhubhyāṃ garuḍārūḍhā śaṅkhacakragadāsinī /
śārṅgabāṇadharā jātā vaiṣṇavī rūpaśālinī //
meaning:
बाहुभ्यां गरुडारूढा शङ्खचक्रगदासिनी /
शार्ङ्गबाणधरा जाता वैष्णवी रूपशालिनी //
text_mt: From her two arms arose the beauteous Vaiṣṇavī, mounted upon Garuḍa, / holding a conch, discus, mace, and sword, bearing the bow Śārṅga and arrows.

sanskrit_iast:
mahogramuśalā raudrā daṃṣṭrollikhitabhūtalā /
vārāhī pṛṣṭhato jātā śeṣanāgopari śthitā //
meaning:
महोग्रमुशला रौद्रा दंष्ट्रोल्लिखितभूतला /
वाराही पृष्ठतो जाता शेषनागोपरि श्थिता //
text_mt: From her back arose the fierce Vārāhī with a terrible pestle, / tearing up the earth with her tusks, standing atop the serpent Śeṣa.

sanskrit_iast:
vajrāṅkuśodyatakarā nānālaṅkārabhūṣitā /
jātā gajendrapaṣṭhasthā māhendrī stanamaṇḍalāt //
meaning:
वज्राङ्कुशोद्यतकरा नानालङ्कारभूषिता /
जाता गजेन्द्रपष्ठस्था माहेन्द्री स्तनमण्डलात् //
text_mt: Holding a thunderbolt and an elephant-goad raised in hand, adorned with various ornaments, / Māhendrī arose from her breast-circle, mounted on the back of an elephant lord.

sanskrit_iast:
vikṣipantī saṭākṣepairgrahanakṣatratārakāḥ /
nakhinī hṛdayājjātā nārasiṃhī sudāruṇā //
meaning:
विक्षिपन्ती सटाक्षेपैर्ग्रहनक्षत्रतारकाः /
नखिनी हृदयाज्जाता नारसिंही सुदारुणा //
text_mt: Tossing the planets, constellations, and stars by the shaking of her mane, / the terribly fierce, clawed Nārasiṃhī arose from her heart.

sanskrit_iast:
tābhirnipātyamānaṃ tu nirīkṣya balamāsuram /
nanāda bhūyo nādān vai caṇḍikā nirbhayā ripūn /
tanninādaṃ mahacchrutvā trailokyapratipūrakam //
meaning:
ताभिर्निपात्यमानं तु निरीक्ष्य बलमासुरम् /
ननाद भूयो नादान् वै चण्डिका निर्भया रिपून् /
तन्निनादं महच्छ्रुत्वा त्रैलोक्यप्रतिपूरकम् //
text_mt: Beholding the asura army being struck down by them, / fearless Caṇḍikā roared repeatedly at the enemies. / Hearing that great roar, which filled the three worlds,

sanskrit_iast:
samājagāma deveśaḥ śūlapāṇistrilocanaḥ /
abhyetya vandya caivaināṃ prāha vākyaṃ tadāmbikaṃ //
meaning:
समाजगाम देवेशः शूलपाणिस्त्रिलोचनः /
अभ्येत्य वन्द्य चैवैनां प्राह वाक्यं तदाम्बिकं //
text_mt: the lord of the gods, spear in hand, the three-eyed one, arrived. / Approaching and bowing to her, he then addressed these words to Ambikā:

sanskrit_iast:
samāyāto 'smi vai durge dehyājñāṃ kiṃ karomi te /
tadvākyasamakālaṃ ca devyā dehodbhavā śivā //
meaning:
समायातो ऽस्मि वै दुर्गे देह्याज्ञां किं करोमि ते /
तद्वाक्यसमकालं च देव्या देहोद्भवा शिवा //
text_mt: “I have arrived indeed, O Durgā; give your command, what shall I do for you?” / Simultaneous with his words, from the goddess’s body Śivā arose,

sanskrit_iast:
jātā sā cāha deveśaṃ gaccha dautyena śaṅkara /
brūhi śumbhaṃ niśumbhaṃ ca yadi jīvitumicchatha //
meaning:
जाता सा चाह देवेशं गच्छ दौत्येन शङ्कर /
ब्रूहि शुम्भं निशुम्भं च यदि जीवितुमिच्छथ //
text_mt: She was born and said to the lord of gods: “Go on an embassy, Śaṅkara! / Tell Śumbha and Niśumbha: ‘If you desire to live,

sanskrit_iast:
tad gacchadhvaṃ durācārāḥ saptamaṃ hi rasātalam /
vāsavo labhatāṃ svargaṃ devāḥ santu gatavyathā //
meaning:
तद् गच्छध्वं दुराचाराः सप्तमं हि रसातलम् /
वासवो लभतां स्वर्गं देवाः सन्तु गतव्यथा //
text_mt: then go, you wicked ones, to the seventh Rasātala! / Let Vāsava obtain heaven, and let the gods be freed from distress!

sanskrit_iast:
yajantu brāhmaṇādyāmī varṇā yajñāṃśca sāmpratam /
noced balāvalepena bhavanto yoddhumicchatha //
meaning:
यजन्तु ब्राह्मणाद्यामी वर्णा यज्ञांश्च साम्प्रतम् /
नोचेद् बलावलेपेन भवन्तो योद्धुमिच्छथ //
text_mt: Let these castes, beginning with the Brahmins, offer their sacrifices now! / If not, and arrogant with strength you desire to fight,

sanskrit_iast:
tadāgacchadhvamavyagrā eṣāhaṃ viniṣūdaye /
yatastu sā śivaṃ dautye nyayojayat nārada //
meaning:
तदागच्छध्वमव्यग्रा एषाहं विनिषूदये /
यतस्तु सा शिवं दौत्ये न्ययोजयत् नारद //
text_mt: then come without delay; here I stand to slay you!’” / Because she dispatched Śiva on an embassy, O Nārada,

sanskrit_iast:
tato nāma mahādevyāḥ śivadūtītyajāyata /
te cāpi śaṅkaravacaḥ śrutvā garvasamanvitam/ /
huṅkṛtvābhyadravan sarve yatra kātyāyanī sthitā //
meaning:
ततो नाम महादेव्याः शिवदूतीत्यजायत /
ते चापि शङ्करवचः श्रुत्वा गर्वसमन्वितम्/ /
हुङ्कृत्वाभ्यद्रवन् सर्वे यत्र कात्यायनी स्थिता //
text_mt: the great goddess came to be known by the name Śivadūtī. / Having heard Śaṅkara’s words full of pride, / they all uttered a roar and rushed to where Kātyāyanī stood.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ śaraiḥ śaktibhiraṅkurvaraiḥ paraśvadhaiḥ śūlabhuśuṇḍipaṭṭiśaiḥ /
prāsaiḥ sunīkṣṇaiḥ parighaiśca vistṛtairvavarṣatudaityavarau sureśvarīm //
meaning:
ततः शरैः शक्तिभिरङ्कुर्वरैः परश्वधैः शूलभुशुण्डिपट्टिशैः /
प्रासैः सुनीक्ष्णैः परिघैश्च विस्तृतैर्ववर्षतुदैत्यवरौ सुरेश्वरीम् //
text_mt: Then with arrows, spears, excellent hooks, battle-axes, tridents, bhuśuṇḍis, and paṭṭiśas, / with sharp darts and broad iron bludgeons, the two excellent Daityas rained down upon the queen of gods.

sanskrit_iast:
sā cāpi bāṇairvarakāmukacyutaiś ciccheda śastrāṇyatha bāhubhiḥ saha /
jaghāna cānyāt raṇacaṇḍavikramā mahāsurān bāṇaśatairmaheśvarī //
meaning:
सा चापि बाणैर्वरकामुकच्युतैश् चिच्छेद शस्त्राण्यथ बाहुभिः सह /
जघान चान्यात् रणचण्डविक्रमा महासुरान् बाणशतैर्महेश्वरी //
text_mt: And with arrows shot from her excellent bow, Maheśvarī cut down their weapons along with their arms; / and fierce in prowess in battle, she struck down other great asuras with hundreds of arrows.

sanskrit_iast:
mārī triśūlena jaghāna cānyān khaṭvāṅgapātairaparāṃśca kauśikī /
mahājalakṣepahataprabhāvān brāhmī tathānyānasurāṃścakāra //
meaning:
मारी त्रिशूलेन जघान चान्यान् खट्वाङ्गपातैरपरांश्च कौशिकी /
महाजलक्षेपहतप्रभावान् ब्राह्मी तथान्यानसुरांश्चकार //
text_mt: Mārī struck down others with her trident, and Kauśikī felled others with blows of her khaṭvāṅga; / and Brāhmī rendered other asuras bereft of power by casting great floods of water.

sanskrit_iast:
māheśvarī śūlavidāritorasaś cakāra dagdhānaparāṃśca vaiṣṇavī /
śaktyā kumārī kuliśena caindrī tuṇḍena cakreṇa varāharūpiṇī //
meaning:
माहेश्वरी शूलविदारितोरसश् चकार दग्धानपरांश्च वैष्णवी /
शक्त्या कुमारी कुलिशेन चैन्द्री तुण्डेन चक्रेण वराहरूपिणी //
text_mt: Māheśvarī tore open chests with her trident, and Vaiṣṇavī burned others; / Kumārī struck with her spear, Aindrī with her thunderbolt, and the one possessing the form of a boar with snout and discus.

sanskrit_iast:
nakhairvibhinnānapi nālasiṃhī aṭṭāṭṭahāsaipi rudradutī /
rudrastriśūlena tathaiva cānyān vināyakaścāpi paraśvadhena //
meaning:
नखैर्विभिन्नानपि नालसिंही अट्टाट्टहासैपि रुद्रदुती /
रुद्रस्त्रिशूलेन तथैव चान्यान् विनायकश्चापि परश्वधेन //
text_mt: Nālasiṃhī tore them apart with her claws, Rudradūtī with loud bursts of laughter, / Rudra likewise with his trident, and Vināyaka with his battle-axe.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ hi devyā vividhaistu rūpairnipātyamānā danupugavāste /
petuḥ pṛthivyāṃ bhuvi cāpi bhūtaiste bhakṣyamāṇāḥ pralayaṃ prajagmuḥ //
meaning:
एवं हि देव्या विविधैस्तु रूपैर्निपात्यमाना दनुपुगवास्ते /
पेतुः पृथिव्यां भुवि चापि भूतैस्ते भक्ष्यमाणाः प्रलयं प्रजग्मुः //
text_mt: Thus struck down by the various forms of the goddess, those bulls among the Danus / fell to the earth, and devoured by the bhūtas upon the ground, they met destruction.

sanskrit_iast:
te vadhyamānāstvatha devatābhirmahāsurā mātṛbhirākulāśca /
vimuktakeśāstaralekṣaṇā bhayāt te raktabījaṃ śaraṇaṃ hi jagmuḥ //
meaning:
ते वध्यमानास्त्वथ देवताभिर्महासुरा मातृभिराकुलाश्च /
विमुक्तकेशास्तरलेक्षणा भयात् ते रक्तबीजं शरणं हि जग्मुः //
text_mt: Slain by the deities and confounded by the Mothers, / with disheveled hair and trembling eyes from fear, the great asuras fled to Raktabīja for refuge.

sanskrit_iast:
sa raktabījaḥ sahasābhyupetya varāstramādāya ca mātṛmaṇḍatam /
vidrāvayan bhūtagaṇān samantād viveśa kopāt sphuritādharaśca //
meaning:
स रक्तबीजः सहसाभ्युपेत्य वरास्त्रमादाय च मातृमण्डतम् /
विद्रावयन् भूतगणान् समन्ताद् विवेश कोपात् स्फुरिताधरश्च //
text_mt: That Raktabīja approached suddenly, took up an excellent weapon, / and putting the hosts of bhūtas to flight all around, entered into the circle of Mothers, his lip quivering with rage.

sanskrit_iast:
tamāpatantaṃ prasamīkṣya mātaraḥ śastraiḥ śitāgrairditajaṃ vavarṣuḥ /
yo raktabindurnyapatat pṛthivyāṃ sa tatpramāṇastvasuro 'pi jajñe //
meaning:
तमापतन्तं प्रसमीक्ष्य मातरः शस्त्रैः शिताग्रैर्दितजं ववर्षुः /
यो रक्तबिन्दुर्न्यपतत् पृथिव्यां स तत्प्रमाणस्त्वसुरो ऽपि जज्ञे //
text_mt: Seeing that son of Diti rushing forward, the Mothers showered him with sharp-pointed weapons; / but whatever drop of blood fell upon the earth, an asura of equal measure arose from it.

sanskrit_iast:
tatastadāścaryamayaṃ nirīkṣya sā kauśikī keśinimabhyuvāca /
pibasva caṇḍe rudhiraṃ tvarātervitatya vaktraṃ vaḍavānalābham //
meaning:
ततस्तदाश्चर्यमयं निरीक्ष्य सा कौशिकी केशिनिमभ्युवाच /
पिबस्व चण्डे रुधिरं त्वरातेर्वितत्य वक्त्रं वडवानलाभम् //
text_mt: Then, beholding that wonder, Kauśikī said to Keśinī: / “O fierce one, opening wide your mouth like the submarine fire, quickly drink the enemy's blood!”

sanskrit_iast:
sā tvevamuktā varadāmbikā hi vitatya vaktraṃ vikarālamugram /
oṣṭhaṃ nabhaspṛk pṛthivīṃ spūśantaṃ kṛtvādharaṃ tiṣṭhati carmamuṇḍā //
meaning:
सा त्वेवमुक्ता वरदाम्बिका हि वितत्य वक्त्रं विकरालमुग्रम् /
ओष्ठं नभस्पृक् पृथिवीं स्पूशन्तं कृत्वाधरं तिष्ठति चर्ममुण्डा //
text_mt: Thus addressed, the boon-giving Ambikā opened wide her dread, hideous mouth; / making her upper lip touch the sky and her lower lip touch the earth, Carmamuṇḍā stood.

sanskrit_iast:
tato 'mbikā keśavikarṣaṇākulaṃ kṛtvā ripuṃ prākṣipata svavaktre /
bibheda śūlena tathāpyurastaḥ kṣatodbhavānye nyapataṃśca vaktre //
meaning:
ततो ऽम्बिका केशविकर्षणाकुलं कृत्वा रिपुं प्राक्षिपत स्ववक्त्रे /
बिभेद शूलेन तथाप्युरस्तः क्षतोद्भवान्ये न्यपतंश्च वक्त्रे //
text_mt: Then Ambikā, throwing the enemy into confusion by dragging him by his hair, cast him into her mouth; / she pierced his chest with her trident, and the others born of his wounds fell right into her mouth.

sanskrit_iast:
tatastu śoṣaṃ prajagāma raktaṃ raktakṣaye hīnabalo babhūva /
taṃ hīnavīryaṃ śatadhā cakāra cakreṇa cāmīkarabhūṣitena //
meaning:
ततस्तु शोषं प्रजगाम रक्तं रक्तक्षये हीनबलो बभूव /
तं हीनवीर्यं शतधा चकार चक्रेण चामीकरभूषितेन //
text_mt: Then his blood dried up, and with the loss of blood his strength waned; / when his valor was spent, she cut him into a hundred pieces with her gold-adorned discus.

sanskrit_iast:
tasmin viśaste danusainyanāte te dānavā dīnataraṃ vineduḥ /
hā tāta ha bhrātariti bruvantaḥ kta yāsi tiṣṭhasva muhūrttamehi //
meaning:
तस्मिन् विशस्ते दनुसैन्यनाते ते दानवा दीनतरं विनेदुः /
हा तात ह भ्रातरिति ब्रुवन्तः क्त यासि तिष्ठस्व मुहूर्त्तमेहि //
text_mt: When that leader of the Danu army was slain, the Dānavas wailed most wretchedly, / crying: “Alas, father! Alas, brother! Where are you going? Stay! Come for a moment!”

sanskrit_iast:
tathāpare vilulitakeśapāśā viśīrṇavarmābharaṇā digambarāḥ /
nipātitā dharaṇitale mṛḍānyā pradudruvurgirivaramuhya daityāḥ //
meaning:
तथापरे विलुलितकेशपाशा विशीर्णवर्माभरणा दिगम्बराः /
निपातिता धरणितले मृडान्या प्रदुद्रुवुर्गिरिवरमुह्य दैत्याः //
text_mt: And other Daityas, their braids of hair loosened, their armor and ornaments shattered, naked, / struck down upon the surface of the earth by Mṛḍānī, fled in bewilderment toward the excellent mountain.

sanskrit_iast:
viśīrṇavarmāyudhabhūṣaṇaṃ tat balaṃ nirīkṣyaiva hi dānavendraḥ /
viśīrmacakrākṣaratho niśumbhaḥ krodhānmṛḍānīṃ samupājagāma //
meaning:
विशीर्णवर्मायुधभूषणं तत् बलं निरीक्ष्यैव हि दानवेन्द्रः /
विशीर्मचक्राक्षरथो निशुम्भः क्रोधान्मृडानीं समुपाजगाम //
text_mt: Seeing that army whose armor, weapons, and ornaments were shattered, the Dānava lord Niśumbha, / his chariot wheels and axles broken, approached Mṛḍānī in wrath.

sanskrit_iast:
khaḍgaṃ samādāya ca carma bhāsvaraṃ dhunvan śiraḥ prekṣya ca rūpamasyāḥ /
saṃstambhamohajvarapīḍite 'tha citre yathāsau likhito babhūva //
meaning:
खड्गं समादाय च चर्म भास्वरं धुन्वन् शिरः प्रेक्ष्य च रूपमस्याः /
संस्तम्भमोहज्वरपीडिते ऽथ चित्रे यथासौ लिखितो बभूव //
text_mt: Taking a sword and a gleaming shield, shaking his head and gazing upon her form, / he was seized by the fever of petrifaction and delusion, and stood as though painted in a picture.

sanskrit_iast:
taṃ stambhitaṃ vīkṣya surāmagre provāca devī vacanaṃ vihasya /
anena vīryeṇa surāstvayā jitā anena māṃ prārthayase balena //
meaning:
तं स्तम्भितं वीक्ष्य सुरामग्रे प्रोवाच देवी वचनं विहस्य /
अनेन वीर्येण सुरास्त्वया जिता अनेन मां प्रार्थयसे बलेन //
text_mt: Seeing him immobilized in front of the gods, the goddess laughed and said: / “By such valor the gods were conquered by you? With such strength do you desire me?”

sanskrit_iast:
śrutvā tu vākyaṃ kauśikyā dānavaḥ sucirādiva /
provāca cintayitvātha vacanaṃ vadatāṃ varaḥ //
meaning:
श्रुत्वा तु वाक्यं कौशिक्या दानवः सुचिरादिव /
प्रोवाच चिन्तयित्वाथ वचनं वदतां वरः //
text_mt: Hearing the words of Kauśikī, the Dānava, best among eloquent speakers, / reflected for a long while and said:

sanskrit_iast:
sukumārarīro 'thaṃ macchastrapatanādapi /
śatadhā yāsyate bhīru āmapātramivāmbhasi //
meaning:
सुकुमाररीरो ऽथं मच्छस्त्रपतनादपि /
शतधा यास्यते भीरु आमपात्रमिवाम्भसि //
text_mt: “This body is delicate; even from the fall of my weapon, / O timid one, it will shatter into a hundred pieces, like an unbaked jar in water.

sanskrit_iast:
etad vicintayannartha tvāṃ praharttu na sundari /
karomi buddhi tasmāt tvaṃ māṃ bhajasvāyatekṣaṇe //
meaning:
एतद् विचिन्तयन्नर्थ त्वां प्रहर्त्तु न सुन्दरि /
करोमि बुद्धि तस्मात् त्वं मां भजस्वायतेक्षणे //
text_mt: Considering this reason, O beautiful woman, I do not make up my mind to strike you; / therefore, resort to me, O large-eyed one!

sanskrit_iast:
mama khaṅganipātaṃ hi nendro dhārayituṃ kṣamaḥ /
nivarttaya matiṃ yuddhād bhāryā me bhava sāmpratam //
meaning:
मम खङ्गनिपातं हि नेन्द्रो धारयितुं क्षमः /
निवर्त्तय मतिं युद्धाद् भार्या मे भव साम्प्रतम् //
text_mt: Even Indra is unable to bear the blow of my sword; / turn your mind away from battle and become my wife now!”

sanskrit_iast:
itthaṃ niśumbhavacanaṃ śrutvā yogīśvarī mune /
vihasya bhāvagambhīraṃ niśumbhaṃ vākyamabravīt //
meaning:
इत्थं निशुम्भवचनं श्रुत्वा योगीश्वरी मुने /
विहस्य भावगम्भीरं निशुम्भं वाक्यमब्रवीत् //
text_mt: Hearing Niśumbha’s words thus, the queen of yogins, O sage, / laughed and spoke words full of deep intent to Niśumbha:

sanskrit_iast:
nājitāhaṃ raṇe vīra bhave bhāryā hi kasyacit /
bhavān yadiha bhāryārtho tato māṃ jaya saṃyuge //
meaning:
नाजिताहं रणे वीर भवे भार्या हि कस्यचित् /
भवान् यदिह भार्यार्थो ततो मां जय संयुगे //
text_mt: “I do not become the wife of anyone unless I am conquered in battle, O hero; / if you desire me here as your wife, then conquer me in combat!”

sanskrit_iast:
ityevamukte vacane khaṅgamudyamya dānavaḥ /
pracikṣepa tadā vegāt kauśikīṃ prati nārada //
meaning:
इत्येवमुक्ते वचने खङ्गमुद्यम्य दानवः /
प्रचिक्षेप तदा वेगात् कौशिकीं प्रति नारद //
text_mt: When these words were spoken, the Dānava raised his sword / and swiftly hurled it at Kauśikī, O Nārada.

sanskrit_iast:
tamāpatantaṃ nistriṃśaṃ ṣaḍbhirbarhiṇarājitaiḥ /
ciccheda carmaṇā sārddha tadadbhutamivābhavat //
meaning:
तमापतन्तं निस्त्रिंशं षड्भिर्बर्हिणराजितैः /
चिच्छेद चर्मणा सार्द्ध तदद्भुतमिवाभवत् //
text_mt: With six [arrows] adorned with peacock feathers she cut that onrushing sword along with his shield; / that seemed wondrous indeed.

sanskrit_iast:
khaḍge sacarmaṇi chinne gadāṃ gṛhya mahāsuraḥ /
samādravat kośabhavāṃ vāyuvegasamo jave //
meaning:
खड्गे सचर्मणि छिन्ने गदां गृह्य महासुरः /
समाद्रवत् कोशभवां वायुवेगसमो जवे //
text_mt: When his sword and shield were severed, the great asura seized a club / and rushed at the sheaths-born goddess, matching the speed of the wind in swiftness.

sanskrit_iast:
tasyāpatata evāśu karau śliṣṭau samau dṛḍhau /
gadayā saha ciccheda kṣurepreṇa raṇe 'mbikā //
meaning:
तस्यापतत एवाशु करौ श्लिष्टौ समौ दृढौ /
गदया सह चिच्छेद क्षुरेप्रेण रणे ऽम्बिका //
text_mt: Even as he rushed forward, Ambikā swiftly cut off both his clasped, matched, strong arms / along with the club using a sharp-edged arrow in the battle.

sanskrit_iast:
tasminnapatite raudre suraśatrau bhayaṅkare /
caṇḍādya mātaro hṛṣṭāścakruḥ kilakilādhvanim //
meaning:
तस्मिन्नपतिते रौद्रे सुरशत्रौ भयङ्करे /
चण्डाद्य मातरो हृष्टाश्चक्रुः किलकिलाध्वनिम् //
text_mt: When that fierce, terrible enemy of the gods fell, / Caṇḍā and the other Mothers rejoiced and uttered shouts of jubilation.

sanskrit_iast:
gaganasthāstato devāḥ śatakratupurogamāḥ /
jayasva vijayetyūcurhṛṣṭāḥ śatrau nipātite //
meaning:
गगनस्थास्ततो देवाः शतक्रतुपुरोगमाः /
जयस्व विजयेत्यूचुर्हृष्टाः शत्रौ निपातिते //
text_mt: Then the gods standing in the sky, led by Śatakratu, / rejoiced when the enemy was struck down, and said: “Be victorious! Conquer!”

sanskrit_iast:
tatastūryāṇyavādyanta bhūtasaṃghaiḥ samantataḥ /
puṣpavṛṣṭiṃ ca mumucuḥ surāḥ kātyāyanīṃ prati //
meaning:
ततस्तूर्याण्यवाद्यन्त भूतसंघैः समन्ततः /
पुष्पवृष्टिं च मुमुचुः सुराः कात्यायनीं प्रति //
text_mt: Then drums were sounded on all sides by the hosts of bhūtas, / and the gods released a shower of flowers upon Kātyāyanī.

sanskrit_iast:
niśumbhaṃ patitaṃ dṛṣṭvā śumbhaḥ krodhānmahāmune /
vṛndārakaṃ samāruhya pāśapāṇiḥ samabhyagāt //
meaning:
निशुम्भं पतितं दृष्ट्वा शुम्भः क्रोधान्महामुने /
वृन्दारकं समारुह्य पाशपाणिः समभ्यगात् //
text_mt: Seeing Niśumbha fallen, Śumbha, O great sage, / mounted a noble elephant in wrath and advanced with a noose in his hand.

sanskrit_iast:
tamāpatantaṃ dṛṣṭvātha sagajaṃ dānaveśvaram /
jagrā ha caturo vāṇāṃścandrārdhākaravarcasaḥ //
meaning:
तमापतन्तं दृष्ट्वाथ सगजं दानवेश्वरम् /
जग्रा ह चतुरो वाणांश्चन्द्रार्धाकरवर्चसः //
text_mt: Seeing that lord of Dānavas advancing with his elephant, / she grasped four arrows gleaming like the crescent moon.

sanskrit_iast:
kṣuraprābhyāṃ samaṃ pādau dvau ciccheda dvipasya sā /
dvābhyāṃ kumbhe jaghānātha hasantī līlayāmbikā //
meaning:
क्षुरप्राभ्यां समं पादौ द्वौ चिच्छेद द्विपस्य सा /
द्वाभ्यां कुम्भे जघानाथ हसन्ती लीलयाम्बिका //
text_mt: With two crescent-shaped arrows she cut off both feet of the elephant at once, / and with two, laughing sportively, Ambikā struck its frontal globes.

sanskrit_iast:
nikṛttābhyāṃ gajaḥ padmyāṃ nipapāta tathecchayā /
śakravajrasamākrāntaṃ śailarājaśiro yathā //
meaning:
निकृत्ताभ्यां गजः पद्म्यां निपपात तथेच्छया /
शक्रवज्रसमाक्रान्तं शैलराजशिरो यथा //
text_mt: With both its feet severed, the elephant fell headlong, / like the peak of the king of mountains struck by the thunderbolt of Śakra.

sanskrit_iast:
tasyāvarjitanāgasya śumbhasyāpyutpatiṣyataḥ /
śiraściccheda bāṇena kuṇḍalālaṅkṛtaṃ śivā //
meaning:
तस्यावर्जितनागस्य शुम्भस्याप्युत्पतिष्यतः /
शिरश्चिच्छेद बाणेन कुण्डलालङ्कृतं शिवा //
text_mt: As his elephant was felled and Śumbha was about to leap up, / Śivā cut off his earring-adorned head with an arrow.

sanskrit_iast:
chinne śirasi daityendro nipapāta sakuñjaraḥ /
yathā samahiṣaḥ kroñco mahāsenasamāhataḥ //
meaning:
छिन्ने शिरसि दैत्येन्द्रो निपपात सकुञ्जरः /
यथा समहिषः क्रोञ्चो महासेनसमाहतः //
text_mt: When his head was severed, the lord of the Daityas fell down along with his elephant, / like Mount Krauñca together with the buffalo when struck down by Mahāsena.

sanskrit_iast:
śrutvā surāḥ suraripu nihatau mṛḍānyā sendrāḥ sasūryamarudaśvivasupradhānāḥ /
āgatya taṃ girivaraṃ vinayāvanamrā devyāstadā stutipadaṃ tvidamīrayantaḥ //
meaning:
श्रुत्वा सुराः सुररिपु निहतौ मृडान्या सेन्द्राः ससूर्यमरुदश्विवसुप्रधानाः /
आगत्य तं गिरिवरं विनयावनम्रा देव्यास्तदा स्तुतिपदं त्विदमीरयन्तः //
text_mt: Hearing that the enemy of the gods had been slain by Mṛḍānī, the gods, headed by Indra, the Sun, the Maruts, the Aśvins, and the Vasus, / came to that best of mountains, bowed low with modesty, and recited this hymn of praise to the Goddess:

sanskrit_iast:
devā ūcuḥ/ /
namo 'stu te bhagavati pāpanāśini namo 'stu te suraripudarpaśātani /
namo 'stu te harihararājyadāyini namo 'stu te makhabhujakāryakāriṇi //
meaning:
देवा ऊचुः/ /
नमो ऽस्तु ते भगवति पापनाशिनि नमो ऽस्तु ते सुररिपुदर्पशातनि /
नमो ऽस्तु ते हरिहरराज्यदायिनि नमो ऽस्तु ते मखभुजकार्यकारिणि //
text_mt: The gods said: / Homage to you, O Goddess, destroyer of sins! Homage to you, destroyer of the pride of the enemies of the gods! / Homage to you, granter of the kingdoms of Hari and Hara! Homage to you, accomplisher of the tasks of the consumers of sacrifices!

sanskrit_iast:
namo 'stu te tridaśaripukṣayaṅkari namo 'stu te śatamakhapādapūjite /
namo 'stu te mahiṣavināsakāriṇi namo 'stu te hariharabhāskarastute //
meaning:
नमो ऽस्तु ते त्रिदशरिपुक्षयङ्करि नमो ऽस्तु ते शतमखपादपूजिते /
नमो ऽस्तु ते महिषविनासकारिणि नमो ऽस्तु ते हरिहरभास्करस्तुते //
text_mt: Homage to you, destroyer of the enemies of the thirty [gods]! Homage to you, whose feet are worshipped by the performer of a hundred sacrifices! / Homage to you, slayer of Mahiṣa! Homage to you, praised by Hari, Hara, and the Sun!

sanskrit_iast:
namo 'stu te 'ṣṭādaśabāhuśālini namo 'stu te śumbhaniśumbhaghātini /
namo 'stu lokārttihare triśūlini namo 'stu nārāyaṇi cakradhāriṇi //
meaning:
नमो ऽस्तु ते ऽष्टादशबाहुशालिनि नमो ऽस्तु ते शुम्भनिशुम्भघातिनि /
नमो ऽस्तु लोकार्त्तिहरे त्रिशूलिनि नमो ऽस्तु नारायणि चक्रधारिणि //
text_mt: Homage to you, who possess eighteen arms! Homage to you, slayer of Śumbha and Niśumbha! / Homage to you, remover of the world's afflictions, bearer of the trident! Homage to you, Nārāyaṇī, wielder of the discus!

sanskrit_iast:
namo 'stu vārāhi sadā dharādhare tvāṃ nārasiṃhi praṇatā namo 'suta te /
namo 'stu nārasiṃhi praṇatā namo 'stu te /
namo 'stu te vajradhare gajadhvaje namo 'suta kaumāri mayūravāhini //
meaning:
नमो ऽस्तु वाराहि सदा धराधरे त्वां नारसिंहि प्रणता नमो ऽसुत ते /
नमो ऽस्तु नारसिंहि प्रणता नमो ऽस्तु ते /
नमो ऽस्तु ते वज्रधरे गजध्वजे नमो ऽसुत कौमारि मयूरवाहिनि //
text_mt: Homage to Vārāhī, who always sustains the earth! Bowed before you, O Nārasiṃhī, homage to you! / Homage to Nārasiṃhī, bowed [to you], homage to you! / Homage to you, bearer of the thunderbolt, whose banner is an elephant! Homage to you, O Kaumārī, rider of the peacock!

sanskrit_iast:
namo 'stu paitāmahahaṃsavāhane namo 'stu mālāvikaṭe sukeśini /
nama'stu mālāvikaṭe sukeśini /
namo 'stu te rāsabhapṛṣṭhavāhini namo 'stu sarvārttihare jaganmaye //
meaning:
नमो ऽस्तु पैतामहहंसवाहने नमो ऽस्तु मालाविकटे सुकेशिनि /
नमऽस्तु मालाविकटे सुकेशिनि /
नमो ऽस्तु ते रासभपृष्ठवाहिनि नमो ऽस्तु सर्वार्त्तिहरे जगन्मये //
text_mt: Homage to the swan-riding [consort] of the Grandfather! Homage to the fearsome one with garlands, having beautiful hair! / Homage to the fearsome one with garlands, having beautiful hair! / Homage to you, rider on the back of an ass! Homage to the remover of all afflictions, who embodies the world!

sanskrit_iast:
namo 'stu viśveśvari pāhi viśvaṃ niṣūdayārīn dvijadevatānām /
namo 'stu te sarvamayi trinetre namo namaste varade prasīda //
meaning:
नमो ऽस्तु विश्वेश्वरि पाहि विश्वं निषूदयारीन् द्विजदेवतानाम् /
नमो ऽस्तु ते सर्वमयि त्रिनेत्रे नमो नमस्ते वरदे प्रसीद //
text_mt: Homage to you, O Mistress of the universe! Protect the universe! Slay the enemies of the twice-born and the gods! / Homage to you, who embody everything, three-eyed one! Homage, homage to you, giver of boons, be gracious!

sanskrit_iast:
brahmāṇī tvaṃ mṛḍānī varaśikhigamanā śaktihastā kumārī vārāhī tvaṃ suvaktrā khagapatigamanā vaiṣṇavī tvaṃ saśārṅgo /
durdṛśyā nārasiṃhī ghuraghuritaravā tvaṃ tathaindrī savajrā tvaṃ mārī carmamuṇḍāśavagamanaratā yoginī yogasiddhā //
meaning:
ब्रह्माणी त्वं मृडानी वरशिखिगमना शक्तिहस्ता कुमारी वाराही त्वं सुवक्त्रा खगपतिगमना वैष्णवी त्वं सशार्ङ्गो /
दुर्दृश्या नारसिंही घुरघुरितरवा त्वं तथैन्द्री सवज्रा त्वं मारी चर्ममुण्डाशवगमनरता योगिनी योगसिद्धा //
text_mt: You are Brahmāṇī, you are Mṛḍānī; Kumārī riding the excellent peacock, holding the spear; you are Vārāhī with a fair face; you are Vaiṣṇavī riding the lord of birds, carrying the Śārṅga bow; / you are the terrible Nārasiṃhī with a deep roaring sound; likewise you are Aindrī with the thunderbolt; you are the pestilential Yoginī, Carmamuṇḍā delighting in walking among corpses, perfected in yoga!

sanskrit_iast:
namaste trinetre bhagavati tavacaraṇānuṣitā ye aharaharvinataśiraso 'vanatāḥ /
nahi nahi paribhavamastyaśubhaṃ ca stutibalikusumakarāḥ satataṃ ye //
meaning:
नमस्ते त्रिनेत्रे भगवति तवचरणानुषिता ये अहरहर्विनतशिरसो ऽवनताः /
नहि नहि परिभवमस्त्यशुभं च स्तुतिबलिकुसुमकराः सततं ये //
text_mt: Homage to you, O three-eyed Goddess! Those who adhere to your feet, bowing their heads in devotion day after day, / and whose hands are always filled with praises, offerings, and flowers, never meet with defeat or misfortune.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ stutā suravaraiḥ suraśatrunāśinī prāha prahasya surasiddhamaharṣivaryān /
prāpto mayād bhutatamo bhavatāṃ prasādāt saṃgrāmamūrdhvi suraśatrujayaḥ pramardāt //
meaning:
एवं स्तुता सुरवरैः सुरशत्रुनाशिनी प्राह प्रहस्य सुरसिद्धमहर्षिवर्यान् /
प्राप्तो मयाद् भुततमो भवतां प्रसादात् संग्राममूर्ध्वि सुरशत्रुजयः प्रमर्दात् //
text_mt: Thus praised by the best of the gods, the destroyer of the gods' enemies laughed and said to the excellent gods, Siddhas, and great sages: / “By your grace, the most wondrous victory over the enemy of the gods by crushing them on the battlefield has been attained by me.

sanskrit_iast:
imāṃ stutiṃ bhaktiparā narottamā bhavadbhiruktāmanukīrttayanti /
duḥsvapnanāśo bhavitā na saṃśayo varastathānyo vriyatāmabhīpsitaḥ //
meaning:
इमां स्तुतिं भक्तिपरा नरोत्तमा भवद्भिरुक्तामनुकीर्त्तयन्ति /
दुःस्वप्ननाशो भविता न संशयो वरस्तथान्यो व्रियतामभीप्सितः //
text_mt: When the best of men, devoted in faith, recite this hymn uttered by you, / their bad dreams will undoubtedly be destroyed. Choose also another boon that you desire.”

sanskrit_iast:
devā ūcuḥ /
yadi varadā bhavatī tridaśānāṃ dvijaśiśugoṣu yatasva hitāya /
punarapi devaripūnaparāṃstvaṃ pradaha hutāśanatulyaśarīre //
meaning:
देवा ऊचुः /
यदि वरदा भवती त्रिदशानां द्विजशिशुगोषु यतस्व हिताय /
पुनरपि देवरिपूनपरांस्त्वं प्रदह हुताशनतुल्यशरीरे //
text_mt: The gods said: / “If you are willing to grant a boon to the thirty [gods], strive for the welfare of the twice-born, children, and cows; / furthermore, burn the other enemies of the gods, O you whose body is like fire!”

sanskrit_iast:
devyuvāca/ /
bhūyo bhaviṣyāmyasṛgukṣitānanā harānanasvedajalodbhavā surāḥ /
andhāsurasyāpratipoṣaṇe ratā nāmnā prasiddhā bhuvaneṣu carcikā //
meaning:
देव्युवाच/ /
भूयो भविष्याम्यसृगुक्षितानना हराननस्वेदजलोद्भवा सुराः /
अन्धासुरस्याप्रतिपोषणे रता नाम्ना प्रसिद्धा भुवनेषु चर्चिका //
text_mt: The Goddess said: / “I shall appear again with a face sprinkled with blood, born from the sweat on Hara's face, O gods; / devoted to starving the asura Andhaka, I will be renowned in the worlds by the name of Carcikā.

sanskrit_iast:
bhūyo vadhiṣyāmi surārimuttamaṃ saṃbhūya nandasya gṛhe yaśodayā /
taṃ vipracittiṃ lavaṇaṃ tathāparau śumbhaṃ niśumbhaṃ daśanaprahārimī //
meaning:
भूयो वधिष्यामि सुरारिमुत्तमं संभूय नन्दस्य गृहे यशोदया /
तं विप्रचित्तिं लवणं तथापरौ शुम्भं निशुम्भं दशनप्रहारिमी //
text_mt: Again, born in the house of Nanda through Yaśodā, I shall slay the foremost enemy of the gods— / that Vipracitti, and Lavaṇa, and also the other two, Śumbha and Niśumbha, striking them with my teeth.

sanskrit_iast:
bhūyaḥ surāstiṣyayuge nirāśinī nirīkṣya mārī ca gṛhe śatakratoḥ /
saṃbhūya devyāmitasatyadhāmayā surā bhariṣyāmi ca śākambharī vai //
meaning:
भूयः सुरास्तिष्ययुगे निराशिनी निरीक्ष्य मारी च गृहे शतक्रतोः /
संभूय देव्यामितसत्यधामया सुरा भरिष्यामि च शाकम्भरी वै //
text_mt: Again, O gods, seeing that in the Kali age the world is foodless and plague-ridden, in the realm of Indra / I shall be born as a goddess of boundless truth and splendor, and I shall sustain the gods as Śākambharī.

sanskrit_iast:
bhūyo vipakṣakṣapaṇāya devā vindhye bhaviṣyamyṛṣirakṣaṇārtham /
durvṛttaceṣṭān vinihatya daityān bhūyaḥ sameṣyāmi surālayaṃ hi //
meaning:
भूयो विपक्षक्षपणाय देवा विन्ध्ये भविष्यम्यृषिरक्षणार्थम् /
दुर्वृत्तचेष्टान् विनिहत्य दैत्यान् भूयः समेष्यामि सुरालयं हि //
text_mt: Again, to destroy adversaries and protect the sages, O gods, I will be born on the Vindhya [mountains]; / having slain the Daityas of wicked deeds, I will surely return again to the abode of the gods.

sanskrit_iast:
yadāruṇākṣo bhavitā mahāsuraḥ tadā bhaviṣyāmi hitāya devātāḥ /
mahālirūpeṇa vinaṣṭajīvitaṃ kṛtvā samaṣyāmi punastriviṣṭapam //
meaning:
यदारुणाक्षो भविता महासुरः तदा भविष्यामि हिताय देवाताः /
महालिरूपेण विनष्टजीवितं कृत्वा समष्यामि पुनस्त्रिविष्टपम् //
text_mt: When the great asura Aruṇākṣa arises, then I will appear for the welfare of the gods; / having deprived him of life in the form of a great bee, I will return once again to heaven.”

sanskrit_iast:
pulastya uvāca /
ityevamuktvā varadā surāṇāṃ kṛtvā praṇāmaṃ divajapuṅgavānām /
visṛjya bhūtāni jagāma devī khaṃ siddhasaṃghairanugamyamānā //
meaning:
पुलस्त्य उवाच /
इत्येवमुक्त्वा वरदा सुराणां कृत्वा प्रणामं दिवजपुङ्गवानाम् /
विसृज्य भूतानि जगाम देवी खं सिद्धसंघैरनुगम्यमाना //
text_mt: Pulastya said: / Having spoken thus, the giver of boons to the gods bowed to the foremost among the heaven-born, / dismissed the spirits, and departed into the sky, accompanied by multitudes of Siddhas.

sanskrit_iast:
idaṃ purāṇaṃ paramaṃ pavitraṃ devyā jayaṃ maṅgaladāyi puṃsām /
śrotavyametanniyataiḥ sadaiva rakṣoghnametadbhagavānuvāca //
iti śrīvāmanapurāṇe triṃśodhyāyaḥ
meaning:
इदं पुराणं परमं पवित्रं देव्या जयं मङ्गलदायि पुंसाम् /
श्रोतव्यमेतन्नियतैः सदैव रक्षोघ्नमेतद्भगवानुवाच //
इति श्रीवामनपुराणे त्रिंशोध्यायः
text_mt:
This ancient story is supremely pure; it brings victory for the Goddess and bestows auspiciousness on men. / It should always be heard by self-controlled people; the Blessed One said that it destroys demons.

Thus ends the thirtieth chapter in the glorious Vāmana Purāṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
nārada uvāca /
kathaṃ samahiṣaḥ kroñco bhinnaḥ skandena suvrata /
etanme vistarād brahman kathayasvāmitadyute //
meaning:
नारद उवाच /
कथं समहिषः क्रोञ्चो भिन्नः स्कन्देन सुव्रत /
एतन्मे विस्तराद् ब्रह्मन् कथयस्वामितद्युते //
text_mt: Nārada said: / “How was Mount Krauñca, together with the buffalo, pierced by Skanda, O observer of good vows? / Tell me this in detail, O Brahmin of boundless splendor!”

sanskrit_iast:
pulasatya uvāca/ /
śṛṇuṣva kathayiṣyāmi kathāṃ puṇyāṃ purātanīm /
yaśovṛddhiṃ kumārasya kārtikeyasya nārada //
meaning:
पुलसत्य उवाच/ /
शृणुष्व कथयिष्यामि कथां पुण्यां पुरातनीम् /
यशोवृद्धिं कुमारस्य कार्तिकेयस्य नारद //
text_mt: Pulastya said: / “Listen, I will tell the ancient and meritorious story / that enhances the renown of the youth Kārtikeya, O Nārada.

sanskrit_iast:
yattatpītaṃ hutāśena skannaṃ śukraṃ pinākinaḥ /
tenākrānto 'bhavad brahman mandatejā hutāśanaḥ //
meaning:
यत्तत्पीतं हुताशेन स्कन्नं शुक्रं पिनाकिनः /
तेनाक्रान्तो ऽभवद् ब्रह्मन् मन्दतेजा हुताशनः //
text_mt: When that spilled seed of the wielder of the Pināka bow was swallowed by the Fire, / the Fire became overcome by it, O Brahmin, and his luster diminished.

sanskrit_iast:
tato jagāma devānāṃ sakāśamamitadyutiḥ /
taiścāpi prahitastūrṇaṃ brahmalokaṃ jagāma ha //
meaning:
ततो जगाम देवानां सकाशममितद्युतिः /
तैश्चापि प्रहितस्तूर्णं ब्रह्मलोकं जगाम ह //
text_mt: Then, of boundless brilliance, he went to the presence of the gods; / and sent swiftly by them, he went to Brahmaloka.

sanskrit_iast:
sa gacchan kuṭulāṃ devīṃ dadarśa pathi pāvakaḥ /
tāṃ dṛṣṭvā prāha kuṭile teja etatsudurddharam //
meaning:
स गच्छन् कुटुलां देवीं ददर्श पथि पावकः /
तां दृष्ट्वा प्राह कुटिले तेज एतत्सुदुर्द्धरम् //
text_mt: As he was going, the fire Pāvaka saw the goddess Kuṭilā on the path. / Seeing her, he said: ‘O Kuṭilā, this splendor is very difficult to bear;

sanskrit_iast:
maheśvareṇa saṃtyaktaṃ nirdahed bhuvanānyapi /
tasmāt pratīccha putro 'yaṃ tava dhanyo bhaviṣyati //
meaning:
महेश्वरेण संत्यक्तं निर्दहेद् भुवनान्यपि /
तस्मात् प्रतीच्छ पुत्रो ऽयं तव धन्यो भविष्यति //
text_mt: cast out by Maheśvara, it could burn even the worlds. / Therefore, accept it; this son of yours will be fortunate.’

sanskrit_iast:
ityagninā sā kuṭilā smṛtvā kvamatamuttamam /
prakṣipasvāmbhasi mama prāha vahniṃ mahāpagā //
meaning:
इत्यग्निना सा कुटिला स्मृत्वा क्वमतमुत्तमम् /
प्रक्षिपस्वाम्भसि मम प्राह वह्निं महापगा //
text_mt: Being addressed thus by Fire, Kuṭilā, considering that excellent counsel, / that great river said to the Fire: ‘Cast it into my waters.’

sanskrit_iast:
tatastvadhārayaddevī śārvaṃ tejastvapūpuṣat /
hutāśano/pi bhagavān kāmacārī paribhraman //
meaning:
ततस्त्वधारयद्देवी शार्वं तेजस्त्वपूपुषत् /
हुताशनो/पि भगवान् कामचारी परिभ्रमन् //
text_mt: Then the goddess bore Śarva's splendor and nourished it. / The blessed consumer of oblations too, roaming about freely as he wished,

sanskrit_iast:
pañcavarṣasahasrāṇi dhṛtavān havyabhuk tataḥ /
māṃsamasthīni rudhiraṃ medontraretasī tvacaḥ //
meaning:
पञ्चवर्षसहस्राणि धृतवान् हव्यभुक् ततः /
मांसमस्थीनि रुधिरं मेदोन्त्ररेतसी त्वचः //
text_mt: for five thousand years, the eater of oblations bore [the rest of it]. Then / his flesh, bones, blood, fat, intestines, seed, skin,

sanskrit_iast:
romaśmaśvrakṣikeśādyāḥ sarve jātā hiraṇmayāḥ /
hiraṇyaretā lokeṣu tena gītaśca pāvakaḥ //
meaning:
रोमश्मश्व्रक्षिकेशाद्याः सर्वे जाता हिरण्मयाः /
हिरण्यरेता लोकेषु तेन गीतश्च पावकः //
text_mt: body hair, beard, eyes, hair of the head, and all else became golden; / because of that, Pāvaka is sung in the worlds as Hiraṇyaretas.

sanskrit_iast:
pañcavarṣasahasrāṇi kuṭulā jvalanopamam /
dhārayantī tadā garbhaṃ brahmaṇaḥ sthānamāgatā //
meaning:
पञ्चवर्षसहस्राणि कुटुला ज्वलनोपमम् /
धारयन्ती तदा गर्भं ब्रह्मणः स्थानमागता //
text_mt: For five thousand years Kuṭilā bore that embryo resembling fire, / and then came to the abode of Brahmā.

sanskrit_iast:
tāṃ dṛṣṭāvān padmajanmā saṃtapyantīṃ mahāpagām /
dṛṣṭvā papraccha genāyaṃ tava garbhaḥ samāhitaḥ //
meaning:
तां दृष्टावान् पद्मजन्मा संतप्यन्तीं महापगाम् /
दृष्ट्वा पप्रच्छ गेनायं तव गर्भः समाहितः //
text_mt: The lotus-born [Brahmā] saw that great river burning in agony, / and seeing her, he asked: ‘By whom has this embryo been placed in you?’

sanskrit_iast:
sā cāha śaṅkaraṃ yattacchrukraṃ pītaṃ hi vahninā /
tadaśaktena tenādya nikṣiptaṃ mayi sattama //
meaning:
सा चाह शङ्करं यत्तच्छ्रुक्रं पीतं हि वह्निना /
तदशक्तेन तेनाद्य निक्षिप्तं मयि सत्तम //
text_mt: And she said: ‘That semen of Śaṅkara which was swallowed by Fire / was deposited today in me by him when he was unable [to bear it], O best of beings.

sanskrit_iast:
pañjavarṣa sahasrāṇi dhārayantyāḥ pitāmaha /
garbhasya varttate kālo na papāta ca karhicit //
meaning:
पञ्जवर्ष सहस्राणि धारयन्त्याः पितामह /
गर्भस्य वर्त्तते कालो न पपात च कर्हिचित् //
text_mt: Five thousand years have passed while I have been carrying it, O Grandfather; / the term of the embryo is long overdue, yet it has never fallen out.’

sanskrit_iast:
tacchrutvā bhagavānāha gaccha tvamudayaṃ girim /
tatrāsti yojanaśataṃ raudraṃ śaravaṇaṃ mahat //
meaning:
तच्छ्रुत्वा भगवानाह गच्छ त्वमुदयं गिरिम् /
तत्रास्ति योजनशतं रौद्रं शरवणं महत् //
text_mt: Hearing that, the Blessed One said: ‘Go to the mountain of the rising sun; / there lies a great and dreadful forest of reeds covering a hundred yojanas.

sanskrit_iast:
tatraiva kṣipa suśreṇi vistīrṇe girisānuni /
daśavarṣasahasrānte tato bālo bhaviṣyati //
meaning:
तत्रैव क्षिप सुश्रेणि विस्तीर्णे गिरिसानुनि /
दशवर्षसहस्रान्ते ततो बालो भविष्यति //
text_mt:
Right there cast [it], O fair-hipped one, upon the wide mountain ridge;
after ten thousand years, a boy will then be born."

sanskrit_iast:
sā śrutvā brahmaṇo vākyaṃ rūpiṇī girimāgatā /
āgatya garbhaṃ tatyāja sukhenaivādrinandinī //
meaning:
सा श्रुत्वा ब्रह्मणो वाक्यं रूपिणी गिरिमागता /
आगत्य गर्भं तत्याज सुखेनैवाद्रिनन्दिनी //
text_mt:
Having heard the word of Brahmā, she assumed a bodily form and came to the mountain;
having arrived, the mountain’s daughter easily gave up the embryo.

sanskrit_iast:
sā tu saṃtyajya taṃ bālaṃ brahmāṇaṃ sahasāgamat /
āpomayī mantravaśāt saṃjātā-kuṭilā satī //
meaning:
सा तु संत्यज्य तं बालं ब्रह्माणं सहसागमत् /
आपोमयी मन्त्रवशात् संजाता-कुटिला सती //
text_mt:
Having abandoned that boy, she immediately went to Brahmā;
by the power of the mantra she turned into water, being the virtuous Kuṭilā.

sanskrit_iast:
tejasā cāpi śārveṇa raukmaṃ śaravaṇaṃ mahat /
tannivāsaratāścānye pādapā mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ //
meaning:
तेजसा चापि शार्वेण रौक्मं शरवणं महत् /
तन्निवासरताश्चान्ये पादपा मृगपक्षिणः //
text_mt:
And by the splendor of Śiva, that great reed-bed became golden,
as did the trees, beasts, and birds dwelling there with delight.

sanskrit_iast:
tato daśasu pūrṇeṣu śaraddaśaśateṣvatha /
bālārkadīptiḥ saṃjāto bālaḥ kamalalocanaḥ //
meaning:
ततो दशसु पूर्णेषु शरद्दशशतेष्वथ /
बालार्कदीप्तिः संजातो बालः कमललोचनः //
text_mt:
Then, when ten hundred autumns were fully complete,
a boy was born, radiant as the morning sun, with eyes like lotuses.

sanskrit_iast:
uttānaśāyī bhagavān divye śaravaṇe sthitaḥ /
mukhe 'ṅguṣṭhaṃ samākṣipya ruroda ghanarāḍiva //
meaning:
उत्तानशायी भगवान् दिव्ये शरवणे स्थितः /
मुखे ऽङ्गुष्ठं समाक्षिप्य रुरोद घनराडिव //
text_mt:
Lying on his back, the blessed one, staying in the divine reed-bed,
putting his thumb into his mouth, wept like the lord of clouds.

sanskrit_iast:
etasminnantare devyaḥ kṛttikāḥ ṣaṭ sutejasaḥ /
dadṛśuḥ svecchayā yāntyo bālaṃ śaravaṇe sthitam //
meaning:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे देव्यः कृत्तिकाः षट् सुतेजसः /
ददृशुः स्वेच्छया यान्त्यो बालं शरवणे स्थितम् //
text_mt:
At that moment, the six Kṛttikā goddesses of great splendor,
wandering at will, saw the boy situated in the reed-bed.

sanskrit_iast:
kṛpāyuktāḥ samājagmuḥ yatra skandaḥ sthito 'bhavat /
ahaṃ pūrvamahaṃ pūrvaṃ tasmai stanye 'bhicukruśuḥ //
meaning:
कृपायुक्ताः समाजग्मुः यत्र स्कन्दः स्थितो ऽभवत् /
अहं पूर्वमहं पूर्वं तस्मै स्तन्ये ऽभिचुक्रुशुः //
text_mt:
Filled with pity, they approached the place where Skanda was;
"I first! I first!" they cried out to him regarding breast-milk.

sanskrit_iast:
vivadantīḥ sa tā dṛṣṭāvā ṣaṇmukhaḥ samajāyata /
abībharaṃśca tāḥ sarvāḥ śiśuṃ snehācca kṛttikāḥ //
meaning:
विवदन्तीः स ता दृष्टावा षण्मुखः समजायत /
अबीभरंश्च ताः सर्वाः शिशुं स्नेहाच्च कृत्तिकाः //
text_mt:
Seeing them disputing, he became six-faced,
and all those Kṛttikās nurtured the child out of love.

sanskrit_iast:
bhriyamāmaḥ sa tābhistu bālo vṛddhimagānmune /
kārttikeyeti vikhyāto jātaḥ sa balināṃ varaḥ //
meaning:
भ्रियमामः स ताभिस्तु बालो वृद्धिमगान्मुने /
कार्त्तिकेयेति विख्यातो जातः स बलिनां वरः //
text_mt:
Being nurtured by them, O sage, the boy grew;
he became known as Kārttikeya, the foremost among the strong.

sanskrit_iast:
etasminnantare brahman pāvakaṃ prāha padmajaḥ /
kiyatpramāṇaḥ putraste varttate sāmprataṃ guhaḥ //
meaning:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे ब्रह्मन् पावकं प्राह पद्मजः /
कियत्प्रमाणः पुत्रस्ते वर्त्तते साम्प्रतं गुहः //
text_mt:
In the meantime, O Brahmin, the lotus-born [Brahmā] said to Fire:
"Of what measure is your son Guha now?"

sanskrit_iast:
sa tadvacanamākarṇya ajānaṃstaṃ harātmajam /
provāca putraṃ deveśa na vedmi katamo guhaḥ //
meaning:
स तद्वचनमाकर्ण्य अजानंस्तं हरात्मजम् /
प्रोवाच पुत्रं देवेश न वेद्मि कतमो गुहः //
text_mt:
Hearing his words, not knowing that son of Hara,
he said: "O Lord of gods, I do not know of a son, which [one is] Guha."

sanskrit_iast:
taṃ prāha bhagavān yattu tejaḥ pītaṃ purā tvayā /
traiyambalaṃ trilokeśa jātaḥ śaravaṇe śiśuḥ //
meaning:
तं प्राह भगवान् यत्तु तेजः पीतं पुरा त्वया /
त्रैयम्बलं त्रिलोकेश जातः शरवणे शिशुः //
text_mt:
The blessed one said to him: "The splendor of the Three-Eyed One that was drunk by you of old,
O lord of the three worlds, has become a child born in the reed-bed."

sanskrit_iast:
śrutvā pitāmahavacaḥ pāvakastvarito 'bhyagāt /
veginaṃ meṣamāruhya kuṭilā taṃ dadarśa ha //
meaning:
श्रुत्वा पितामहवचः पावकस्त्वरितो ऽभ्यगात् /
वेगिनं मेषमारुह्य कुटिला तं ददर्श ह //
text_mt:
Hearing the words of the grandfather, Fire departed in haste,
mounting a swift ram; and Kuṭilā saw him.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ papraccha kuṭilā śīghraṃ kva vrajase kave /
so 'bravīt putraduṣṭyarthaṃ jātaṃ śaravaṇe śiśum //
meaning:
ततः पप्रच्छ कुटिला शीघ्रं क्व व्रजसे कवे /
सो ऽब्रवीत् पुत्रदुष्ट्यर्थं जातं शरवणे शिशुम् //
text_mt:
Then Kuṭilā asked: "Where are you going so quickly, O wise one?"
He said: "To see my son, the child born in the reed-bed."

sanskrit_iast:
sābravīt tanayo mahyaṃ mametyāha ca pāvakaḥ /
vivadantau dadarsātha svecchācārī janārdanaḥ //
meaning:
साब्रवीत् तनयो मह्यं ममेत्याह च पावकः /
विवदन्तौ ददर्साथ स्वेच्छाचारी जनार्दनः //
text_mt:
She said, "He is my son," and Fire said, "He is mine."
Then Janārdana, wandering at will, saw the two disputing.

sanskrit_iast:
tau papraccha kimarthaṃ vā vivādamiha cakrathaḥ /
tāvūcatuḥ vutraheto rudraśukrodbhavāya hi //
meaning:
तौ पप्रच्छ किमर्थं वा विवादमिह चक्रथः /
तावूचतुः वुत्रहेतो रुद्रशुक्रोद्भवाय हि //
text_mt:
He asked the two: "For what reason are you two arguing here?"
The two said: "For the sake of the son born from the seed of Rudra."

sanskrit_iast:
tāvuvāca harirdevo gaccha taṃ tripurāntakam /
sa yadā vakṣyati deveśastatkurudhvamasaṃśayam //
meaning:
तावुवाच हरिर्देवो गच्छ तं त्रिपुरान्तकम् /
स यदा वक्ष्यति देवेशस्तत्कुरुध्वमसंशयम् //
text_mt:
Lord Hari said to the two: "Go to the destroyer of Tripura;
whatever that lord of gods shall say, do that without a doubt."

sanskrit_iast:
ityuktau vāsudevena kuṭilāgnī harāntikam /
sambhyetyocatustathyaṃ kasya putreti nārada //
meaning:
इत्युक्तौ वासुदेवेन कुटिलाग्नी हरान्तिकम् /
सम्भ्येत्योचतुस्तथ्यं कस्य पुत्रेति नारद //
text_mt:
Thus addressed by Vāsudeva, Kuṭilā and Fire, having approached Hara,
said truly: "Whose son is he, O Nārada?"

sanskrit_iast:
rudrastadvākyamākarṇya harṣanirbharamānasaḥ /
diṣṭyā diṣṭyeti girijāṃ prodbhūtapulako 'bravīt //
meaning:
रुद्रस्तद्वाक्यमाकर्ण्य हर्षनिर्भरमानसः /
दिष्ट्या दिष्ट्येति गिरिजां प्रोद्भूतपुलको ऽब्रवीत् //
text_mt:
Rudra, hearing their words, his mind brimming with joy,
with bristling hair, said to the mountain's daughter: "By good fortune! By good fortune!"

sanskrit_iast:
tato 'mbikā prāha haraṃ deva gacchāma śiśum /
praṣṭuṃ samāśrayed yaṃ sa tasya putro bhaviṣyati //
meaning:
ततो ऽम्बिका प्राह हरं देव गच्छाम शिशुम् /
प्रष्टुं समाश्रयेद् यं स तस्य पुत्रो भविष्यति //
text_mt:
Then Ambikā said to Hara: "O Lord, let us go to the child
to ask: Whomever he resorts to, he shall be the son of that one."

sanskrit_iast:
bāḍhamityeva bhagavān samuttasthau vṛṣadhvajaḥ /
sahomayā kuṭilayā pāvakena ca dhīmatā //
meaning:
बाढमित्येव भगवान् समुत्तस्थौ वृषध्वजः /
सहोमया कुटिलया पावकेन च धीमता //
text_mt:
"So be it," said the blessed bull-bannered Lord, and set out
together with Umā, Kuṭilā, and the wise Fire.

sanskrit_iast:
saṃprāptāste śaravaṇaṃ harāgnikuṭilāmbikāḥ /
dadṛśuḥ śiśukaṃ taṃ ca kṛttikotsaṅgaśāyinam //
meaning:
संप्राप्तास्ते शरवणं हराग्निकुटिलाम्बिकाः /
ददृशुः शिशुकं तं च कृत्तिकोत्सङ्गशायिनम् //
text_mt:
Arrived at the reed-bed, Hara, Fire, Kuṭilā, and Ambikā
saw that little child lying in the lap of the Kṛttikās.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ sa bālakasteṣāṃ matvā cintitamādarāt /
yogī caturmūrtirabhūt ṣaṇmukhaḥ sa śiśustvapi //
meaning:
ततः स बालकस्तेषां मत्वा चिन्तितमादरात् /
योगी चतुर्मूर्तिरभूत् षण्मुखः स शिशुस्त्वपि //
text_mt:
Then that boy, respectfully perceiving their thought,
that yogin child, though six-faced, assumed four forms.

sanskrit_iast:
kumāraḥ śaṅkaramagād viśākho gaurimāgamat /
kuṭilāmagamacchākho mahāseno 'gnimabhyayāt //
meaning:
कुमारः शङ्करमगाद् विशाखो गौरिमागमत् /
कुटिलामगमच्छाखो महासेनो ऽग्निमभ्ययात् //
text_mt:
Kumāra went to Śaṅkara; Viśākha went to Gaurī;
Śākha went to Kuṭilā; and Mahāsena approached Fire.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ prītiyuto rudra umā ca kuṭilā tathā /
pāvakaścāpi deveśaḥ parāṃ mudamavāpa ca //
meaning:
ततः प्रीतियुतो रुद्र उमा च कुटिला तथा /
पावकश्चापि देवेशः परां मुदमवाप च //
text_mt:
Then Rudra, filled with affection, and Umā, and likewise Kuṭilā,
and Fire, the lord of gods, attained the highest joy.

sanskrit_iast:
tato 'bruvan kṛttikāstāḥ ṣaṇmukhaḥ kiṃ harātmajaḥ /
tā abravīddharaḥ pratītyā vidhivad vacanaṃ mune //
meaning:
ततो ऽब्रुवन् कृत्तिकास्ताः षण्मुखः किं हरात्मजः /
ता अब्रवीद्धरः प्रतीत्या विधिवद् वचनं मुने //
text_mt:
Then those Kṛttikās said: "Is the six-faced one the son of Hara?"
Hara, with conviction, spoke words to them according to rule, O sage:

sanskrit_iast:
nāmnā tu kārttikeyo hi yuṣmākaṃ tanayastvasau /
kuṭulāyāḥ kumāreti putro 'yaṃ bhavitāvyayaḥ //
meaning:
नाम्ना तु कार्त्तिकेयो हि युष्माकं तनयस्त्वसौ /
कुटुलायाः कुमारेति पुत्रो ऽयं भविताव्ययः //
text_mt:
"By the name Kārttikeya, indeed, this one shall be your son;
and as Kumāra, this imperishable one shall be the son of Kuṭilā.

sanskrit_iast:
skanda ityeva vikhyāto gaurīputro bhavatvasau /
guha ityeva nāmnā ca mamāsau tanayaḥ smṛtaḥ //
meaning:
स्कन्द इत्येव विख्यातो गौरीपुत्रो भवत्वसौ /
गुह इत्येव नाम्ना च ममासौ तनयः स्मृतः //
text_mt:
Known as Skanda, let this one be the son of Gaurī;
and by the name Guha, he is considered my son.

sanskrit_iast: māhāsena iti khyāto hutāśasyāstu putrakaḥ śāradvata iti khyātaḥ sutaḥ śaravaṇasya ca //
meaning: माहासेन इति ख्यातो हुताशस्यास्तु पुत्रकः शारद्वत इति ख्यातः सुतः शरवणस्य च //
text_mt:
Known as Mahāsena, let him be the son of the Fire-god;
and known as Śāradvata, he is the son of the reed-bed.

sanskrit_iast:
evameva mahāyogī pṛthivyāṃ khyātimeṣyati /
ṣaḍāsyatvān mahābāhuḥ ṣaṇmukho nāma gīyate //
meaning:
एवमेव महायोगी पृथिव्यां ख्यातिमेष्यति /
षडास्यत्वान् महाबाहुः षण्मुखो नाम गीयते //
text_mt:
In this very way the great yogin shall attain renown upon earth;
because of having six faces, the mighty-armed one is sung by the name Ṣaṇmukha."

sanskrit_iast:
ityevamuktvā bhagavān śūlapāṇiḥ pitāmaham /
sasmāra daivataiḥ sārddha te 'pyājagmustvarānvitāḥ //
meaning:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा भगवान् शूलपाणिः पितामहम् /
सस्मार दैवतैः सार्द्ध ते ऽप्याजग्मुस्त्वरान्विताः //
text_mt:
Having spoken thus, the blessed Lord who holds the trident in his hand
remembered the Grandfather together with the gods; and they too arrived in haste.

sanskrit_iast:
praṇipatya ca kāmārimumāṃ ca girinandinīm /
dṛṣṭvā hutāśanaṃ prītyā kuṭilāṃ kṛttikāstathā //
meaning:
प्रणिपत्य च कामारिमुमां च गिरिनन्दिनीम् /
दृष्ट्वा हुताशनं प्रीत्या कुटिलां कृत्तिकास्तथा //
text_mt:
Bowing to the enemy of Kāma and to Umā, daughter of the mountain,
and looking with joy upon Fire, Kuṭilā, and the Kṛttikās,

sanskrit_iast: dadṛśurbālamatyugraṃ ṣaṇmukhaṃ sūryasaṃnibham muṣṇantamiva cakṣuṃṣi tejasā svena devatāḥ //
meaning: ददृशुर्बालमत्युग्रं षण्मुखं सूर्यसंनिभम् मुष्णन्तमिव चक्षुंषि तेजसा स्वेन देवताः //
text_mt:
the deities beheld the fierce, six-faced child, resembling the sun,
as if stealing their eyes with his own splendor.

sanskrit_iast:
kautukābhivṛtāḥ sarve evamūcuḥ surottamāḥ /
devakāryaṃ tvayā deva kṛtaṃ devyāgninā tathā //
meaning:
कौतुकाभिवृताः सर्वे एवमूचुः सुरोत्तमाः /
देवकार्यं त्वया देव कृतं देव्याग्निना तथा //
text_mt:
Filled with wonder, all the foremost gods spoke thus:
"The task of the gods has been accomplished by you, O Lord, and by the goddess, and by Fire.

sanskrit_iast:
taduttaṣṭha vrajāmo 'dya tīrthamaujasamavyayam /
kurukṣetre sarasvatyāmabhiṣñcāma ṣaṇmukham //
meaning:
तदुत्तष्ठ व्रजामो ऽद्य तीर्थमौजसमव्ययम् /
कुरुक्षेत्रे सरस्वत्यामभिष्ञ्चाम षण्मुखम् //
text_mt:
Therefore arise, let us go today to the imperishable tīrtha Ojas;
let us consecrate the six-faced one on the Sarasvatī in Kurukṣetra.

sanskrit_iast:
senāyāḥ patirastveṣa devagandharvakiṃnarāḥ /
mahiṣaṃ ghātayatveṣa tārakaṃ ca sudāruṇam //
meaning:
सेनायाः पतिरस्त्वेष देवगन्धर्वकिंनराः /
महिषं घातयत्वेष तारकं च सुदारुणम् //
text_mt:
Let him be the commander of the army of gods, Gandharvas, and Kiṃnaras;
let him slay Mahiṣa and the exceedingly dreadful Tāraka."

sanskrit_iast:
bāḍhamityabravīccharvaḥ samuttasthuḥ surāstataḥ /
kumārasahitā jagmuḥ kurukṣetraṃ mahāphalam //
meaning:
बाढमित्यब्रवीच्छर्वः समुत्तस्थुः सुरास्ततः /
कुमारसहिता जग्मुः कुरुक्षेत्रं महाफलम् //
text_mt:
"So be it," Śarva said; then the gods arose.
Accompanied by Kumāra, they went to Kurukṣetra, which bestows great fruit.

sanskrit_iast:
tatraiva devatāḥ sendrā rudrabrahmajanārdanāḥ /
yatnamasyābhiṣekārtaṃ cakrurmunigaṇaiḥ saha //
meaning:
तत्रैव देवताः सेन्द्रा रुद्रब्रह्मजनार्दनाः /
यत्नमस्याभिषेकार्तं चक्रुर्मुनिगणैः सह //
text_mt:
Right there the deities, along with Indra, Rudra, Brahmā, and Janārdana,
made preparations for his consecration together with the hosts of sages.

sanskrit_iast:
tato 'mbunā saptasamudravāhinīnadījalenāpi mahāphalena /
varauṣadhībhiśca sahasramūrttibhistadābhyaṣiñcan gumacyutādyāḥ //
meaning:
ततो ऽम्बुना सप्तसमुद्रवाहिनीनदीजलेनापि महाफलेन /
वरौषधीभिश्च सहस्रमूर्त्तिभिस्तदाभ्यषिञ्चन् गुमच्युताद्याः //
text_mt:
Then with water, with the greatly fruitful waters of rivers flowing to the seven seas,
and with excellent medicinal herbs of a thousand forms, Acyuta and the others consecrated Guha.

sanskrit_iast:
abhiṣiñcati senānyāṃ kumāre divyarūpiṇi /
jagurgandharvapatayo nanṛtuścāpsarogaṇāḥ //
meaning:
अभिषिञ्चति सेनान्यां कुमारे दिव्यरूपिणि /
जगुर्गन्धर्वपतयो ननृतुश्चाप्सरोगणाः //
text_mt:
As Kumāra of divine form was being consecrated as commander of the army,
the lords of Gandharvas sang and the hosts of Apsarases danced.

sanskrit_iast:
abhiṣiktaṃ kumāraṃ ca giriputrī nirīkṣya hi /
snehādutsaṅgagaṃ skandaṃ mūrdhnyajighranmurhurmuhuḥ //
meaning:
अभिषिक्तं कुमारं च गिरिपुत्री निरीक्ष्य हि /
स्नेहादुत्सङ्गगं स्कन्दं मूर्ध्न्यजिघ्रन्मुर्हुर्मुहुः //
text_mt:
Seeing Kumāra consecrated, the mountain's daughter,
out of love, smelled Skanda who was sitting in her lap on his head again and again.

sanskrit_iast:
jighratī kārttikeyasya abhiṣekārdramānanam /
bhātyadrijā yathendrasya devamātāditiḥ purā //
meaning:
जिघ्रती कार्त्तिकेयस्य अभिषेकार्द्रमाननम् /
भात्यद्रिजा यथेन्द्रस्य देवमातादितिः पुरा //
text_mt:
Smelling the face of Kārttikeya wet with the waters of consecration,
the mountain's daughter shone like Aditi of old, the mother of the gods, smelling Indra's.

sanskrit_iast:
tadābhiṣiktaṃ tanayaṃ dṛṣṭvā śarvo mudaṃ yayau /
pāvakaḥ kṛttikāścaiva kuṭilā ca yaśasvinī //
meaning:
तदाभिषिक्तं तनयं दृष्ट्वा शर्वो मुदं ययौ /
पावकः कृत्तिकाश्चैव कुटिला च यशस्विनी //
text_mt:
Seeing his son consecrated, Śarva then rejoiced,
as did Fire, the Kṛttikās, and the renowned Kuṭilā.

sanskrit_iast:
tato 'bhiṣiktāsya haraḥ senāpatye guhasya tu /
pramathāṃścaturaḥ pradācchakratulyaparākramān //
meaning:
ततो ऽभिषिक्तास्य हरः सेनापत्ये गुहस्य तु /
प्रमथांश्चतुरः प्रदाच्छक्रतुल्यपराक्रमान् //
text_mt:
Then, upon the consecration of Guha to the commandership of the army,
Hara gave four Pramathas equal in prowess to Śakra:

sanskrit_iast:
ghaṇṭākarṇa lohitākṣaṃ nandisenaṃ ca dāruṇam /
caturthaṃ balināṃ mukhyaṃ khyātaṃ kumudamālinam //
meaning:
घण्टाकर्ण लोहिताक्षं नन्दिसेनं च दारुणम् /
चतुर्थं बलिनां मुख्यं ख्यातं कुमुदमालिनम् //
text_mt:
Ghaṇṭākarṇa, Lohitākṣa, the fierce Nandisena,
and the fourth, Kumudamālin, celebrated as foremost among the strong.

sanskrit_iast:
haradattān gaṇān dṛṣṭvā devāḥ skandasya nārada /
pradaduḥ pramathān svān svān sarve brahmapurogamāḥ //
meaning:
हरदत्तान् गणान् दृष्ट्वा देवाः स्कन्दस्य नारद /
प्रददुः प्रमथान् स्वान् स्वान् सर्वे ब्रह्मपुरोगमाः //
text_mt:
Seeing the hosts given by Hara, the gods, O Nārada,
led by Brahmā, all gave their own Pramathas to Skanda.

sanskrit_iast:
sthāṇuṃ brahma gaṇaṃ prādād viṣṇuḥ prādād gaṇatrayam /
saṃkramaṃ vikramaṃ caiva tṛtīyaṃ ca parākramam //
meaning:
स्थाणुं ब्रह्म गणं प्रादाद् विष्णुः प्रादाद् गणत्रयम् /
संक्रमं विक्रमं चैव तृतीयं च पराक्रमम् //
text_mt: Brahmā gave the gaṇa Sthāṇu, and Viṣṇu gave a triad of gaṇas: / Saṃkrama, Vikrama, and the third, Parākrama.

sanskrit_iast:
utkesaṃ paṅkajaṃ śakro ravirdaṇḍakapiṅgalau /
candro maṇiṃ vasumaṇimaśvinau vatsanandinau //
meaning:
उत्केसं पङ्कजं शक्रो रविर्दण्डकपिङ्गलौ /
चन्द्रो मणिं वसुमणिमश्विनौ वत्सनन्दिनौ //
text_mt: Indra gave Utkeśa and Paṅkaja; the Sun gave Daṇḍa and Kapiṅgala; / the Moon gave Maṇi and Vasumaṇi; the Aśvins gave Vatsa and Nandin.

sanskrit_iast:
jyotirhutāśanaḥ prādājjavalajjihvaṃ tathāparam /
kundaṃ mukundaṃ kusumaṃ trīn dhātānucarān dadau //
meaning:
ज्योतिर्हुताशनः प्रादाज्जवलज्जिह्वं तथापरम् /
कुन्दं मुकुन्दं कुसुमं त्रीन् धातानुचरान् ददौ //
text_mt: The fire-god gave Jyotis, and another named Jvalajjihva; / Dhātṛ gave three attendants: Kunda, Mukunda, and Kusuma.

sanskrit_iast:
cakrānucakrau tvaṣṭāṃ ca vedhātisthirasusthirau /
pāṇityajaṃ kālakañca prādāt pūṣā mahābalau //
meaning:
चक्रानुचक्रौ त्वष्टां च वेधातिस्थिरसुस्थिरौ /
पाणित्यजं कालकञ्च प्रादात् पूषा महाबलौ //
text_mt: Tvaṣṭṛ gave Cakra and Anucakra; the Creator [gave] Atisthira and Susthira; / Pūṣan gave two of great strength: Pāṇityaja and Kālaka.

sanskrit_iast:
svarṇamālaṃ ghanāhvaṃ ca himavān pramathottamau /
prādādevocchrito vindhyastvatiśṛṅgaṃ ca pārṣadam //
meaning:
स्वर्णमालं घनाह्वं च हिमवान् प्रमथोत्तमौ /
प्रादादेवोच्छ्रितो विन्ध्यस्त्वतिशृङ्गं च पार्षदम् //
text_mt: Himavat gave two supreme pramathas: Svarṇamāla and the one named Ghana; / and the lofty Vindhya gave an attendant named Atiśṛṅga.

sanskrit_iast:
suvarcasaṃ ca varuṇaḥ pradadau cātivarcasam /
saṃgrahaṃ vigrahaṃ cābdhirnāgā jayamahājayau //
meaning:
सुवर्चसं च वरुणः प्रददौ चातिवर्चसम् /
संग्रहं विग्रहं चाब्धिर्नागा जयमहाजयौ //
text_mt: Varuṇa gave Suvarcas and Ativarcas; / the Ocean gave Saṃgraha and Vigraha; the snakes gave Jaya and Mahājaya.

sanskrit_iast:
unmādaṃ śuṅkurṇa ca puṣpadantaṃ tathāmbikā /
ghasaṃ cātighasaṃ vāyuḥ prādādanucarāvubhau //
meaning:
उन्मादं शुङ्कुर्ण च पुष्पदन्तं तथाम्बिका /
घसं चातिघसं वायुः प्रादादनुचरावुभौ //
text_mt: Ambikā gave Unmāda, Śuṅkarṇa, and Puṣpadanta; / the Wind gave both attendants: Ghasa and Atighasa.

sanskrit_iast:
parighaṃ caṭakaṃ bhīmaṃ dahatidahanau tathā /
pradadāvaṃśumān pañca pramathān ṣaṇmukhāya hi //
meaning:
परिघं चटकं भीमं दहतिदहनौ तथा /
प्रददावंशुमान् पञ्च प्रमथान् षण्मुखाय हि //
text_mt: The Sun gave five pramathas to the six-faced god: / Parigha, Caṭaka, Bhīma, and Dahati and Dahana.

sanskrit_iast:
yamaḥ pramāthamunmāthaṃ kālasenaṃ mahāmukham /
tālapatraṃ nāḍijaṅghaṃ ṣaḍevānucarān dadau //
meaning:
यमः प्रमाथमुन्माथं कालसेनं महामुखम् /
तालपत्रं नाडिजङ्घं षडेवानुचरान् ददौ //
text_mt: Yama gave six attendants: / Pramātha, Unmātha, Kālasena, Mahāmukha, Tālapatra, and Nāḍijaṅgha.

sanskrit_iast:
suprabhaṃ ca sukarmāṇaṃ dadau dhātā gaṇeśvarau /
suvrataṃ satyasandhaṃ ca mitraḥ pradāda dvijottama //
meaning:
सुप्रभं च सुकर्माणं ददौ धाता गणेश्वरौ /
सुव्रतं सत्यसन्धं च मित्रः प्रदाद द्विजोत्तम //
text_mt: Dhātṛ gave two lords of gaṇas: Suprabha and Sukarman; / and Mitra gave Suvrata and Satyasandha, O best of the twice-born.

sanskrit_iast:
anantaḥ śaṅkupīṭhaśca nikumbhaḥ kumudo 'mbujaḥ /
ekākṣaḥ kunaṭī cakṣuḥ kirīṭī kalaśodaraḥ //
meaning:
अनन्तः शङ्कुपीठश्च निकुम्भः कुमुदो ऽम्बुजः /
एकाक्षः कुनटी चक्षुः किरीटी कलशोदरः //
text_mt: Ananta, Śaṅkupīṭha, Nikumbha, Kumuda, Ambuja, / Ekākṣa, Kunaṭī, Cakṣus, Kirīṭin, Kalaśodara,

sanskrit_iast:
sūcīvaktraḥ kokanadaḥ prahāsaḥ priyako 'cyutaḥ /
gaṇāḥ pañcadaśaite hi yakṣairdattā guhasya tu //
meaning:
सूचीवक्त्रः कोकनदः प्रहासः प्रियको ऽच्युतः /
गणाः पञ्चदशैते हि यक्षैर्दत्ता गुहस्य तु //
text_mt: Sūcīvaktra, Kokanada, Prahāsa, Priyaka, and Acyuta— / these fifteen gaṇas were given to Guha by the yakṣas.

sanskrit_iast:
kālindyāḥ kālakandaśca narmadāyā raṇotkaṭaḥ /
godāvaryāḥ siddhayātrastamasāyādrikampakaḥ /
31.75 sahasrabāhuḥ sītāyā vañjūlāyāḥ sitodaraḥ /
mandākinyāstathā nando vipāśāyāḥ priyaṅkaraḥ //
meaning:
कालिन्द्याः कालकन्दश्च नर्मदाया रणोत्कटः /
गोदावर्याः सिद्धयात्रस्तमसायाद्रिकम्पकः /
31.75 सहस्रबाहुः सीताया वञ्जूलायाः सितोदरः /
मन्दाकिन्यास्तथा नन्दो विपाशायाः प्रियङ्करः //
text_mt:
Kālakanda of the Kālindī, and Raṇotkaṭa of the Narmadā,
Siddhayātra of the Godāvarī, and Adrikampaka of the Tamasā;

Sahasrabāhu of the Sītā, Sitodara of the Vañjūlā,
and Nanda of the Mandākinī, and Priyaṅkara of the Vipāśā.

sanskrit_iast:
airāvatyāścaturddaṣṭraḥ ṣoḍaśākṣo vitastayā /
mārjāraṃ sauśikī prādāt krathakrauñcau ca gautamī //
meaning:
ऐरावत्याश्चतुर्द्दष्ट्रः षोडशाक्षो वितस्तया /
मार्जारं सौशिकी प्रादात् क्रथक्रौञ्चौ च गौतमी //
text_mt: from Airāvatī, Caturdaṣṭra; by Vitastā, Ṣoḍaśākṣa; / Sauśikī gave Mārjāra; and Gautamī gave Kratha and Krauñca.

sanskrit_iast:
bāhudā śatasīrṣaṃ ca vāhā gonandanandikau /
bhīmaṃ bhīmarathī prādād vegāriṃ sarayūrdadau //
meaning:
बाहुदा शतसीर्षं च वाहा गोनन्दनन्दिकौ /
भीमं भीमरथी प्रादाद् वेगारिं सरयूर्ददौ //
text_mt: Bāhudā gave Śataśīrṣa, and Vāhā gave Gonanda and Nandika; / Bhīmarathī gave Bhīma, and Sarayū gave Vegāri.

sanskrit_iast:
aṣṭabāhuṃ dadau kāśī subāhumapi gaṇḍakī /
mahānadī citradevaṃ citrā citrarathaṃ dadau //
meaning:
अष्टबाहुं ददौ काशी सुबाहुमपि गण्डकी /
महानदी चित्रदेवं चित्रा चित्ररथं ददौ //
text_mt: Kāśī gave Aṣṭabāhu, and Gaṇḍakī gave Subāhu; / Mahānadī gave Citradeva, and Citrā gave Citraratha.

sanskrit_iast:
kuhūḥ kuvalayaṃ prādānmadhuvarṇaṃ madhūdakā /
jambūkaṃ dhūtapāpā ca veṇā śvetānanaṃ dadau //
meaning:
कुहूः कुवलयं प्रादान्मधुवर्णं मधूदका /
जम्बूकं धूतपापा च वेणा श्वेताननं ददौ //
text_mt: Kuhū gave Kuvalaya, and Madhūdakā gave Madhuvarṇa; / Dhūtapāpā gave Jambūka, and Veṇā gave Śvetānana.

sanskrit_iast:
śrutavarma ca parmāsā revā sāgaraveginam /
prabhāvārthaṃ sahaṃ prādāt kāñcanā kanakekṣaṇam //
meaning:
श्रुतवर्म च पर्मासा रेवा सागरवेगिनम् /
प्रभावार्थं सहं प्रादात् काञ्चना कनकेक्षणम् //
text_mt: Parnāsā gave Śrutavarman, and Revā gave Sāgaravegin; / Prabhāvā gave Saha, and Kāñcanā gave Kanakekṣaṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
gṛdhrapatraṃ ca vimalā cāruvaktraṃ manoharā /
dhūtapāpā mahārāvaṃ karṇā vidrumasaṃnibham //
meaning:
गृध्रपत्रं च विमला चारुवक्त्रं मनोहरा /
धूतपापा महारावं कर्णा विद्रुमसंनिभम् //
text_mt: Vimalā gave Gṛdhrapatra, and Manoharā gave Cāruvaktra; / Dhūtapāpā gave Mahārāva, and Karṇā gave one resembling coral.

sanskrit_iast:
suprasādaṃ suveṇuśca jiṣṇumeghavatī dadau /
yajñabāhuṃ viśālā ca sarasvatyo dadurgaṇān //
meaning:
सुप्रसादं सुवेणुश्च जिष्णुमेघवती ददौ /
यज्ञबाहुं विशाला च सरस्वत्यो ददुर्गणान् //
text_mt: Suveṇu gave Suprasāda, and Meghavatī gave Jiṣṇu; / Viśālā and the Sarasvatīs gave Yajñabāhu and gaṇas.

sanskrit_iast:
kuṭilā tanayasyādāda daśa śakrabalān gaṇān /
karālaṃ sitakeśaṃ ca kṛṣṇakeśaṃ jaṭādharam //
meaning:
कुटिला तनयस्यादाद दश शक्रबलान् गणान् /
करालं सितकेशं च कृष्णकेशं जटाधरम् //
text_mt: Kuṭilā gave to her son ten gaṇas with the strength of Indra: / Karāla, Sitakeśa, Kṛṣṇakeśa, Jaṭādhara,

sanskrit_iast:
meghanādaṃ caturddaṣṭraṃ vidyujihvaṃ daśānanam /
somāpyayanamevograṃ devayājinameva ca //
meaning:
मेघनादं चतुर्द्दष्ट्रं विद्युजिह्वं दशाननम् /
सोमाप्ययनमेवोग्रं देवयाजिनमेव च //
text_mt: Meghanāda, Caturdaṣṭra, Vidyujjihva, Daśānana, / Somāpyayana, Ugra, and Devayājin.

sanskrit_iast:
haṃsāsyaṃ kuṇḍajaṭharaṃ bahugrīvaṃ hayānanam /
kūrmagrīvaṃ ca pañcaitān daduḥ putrāya kṛttikāḥ //
meaning:
हंसास्यं कुण्डजठरं बहुग्रीवं हयाननम् /
कूर्मग्रीवं च पञ्चैतान् ददुः पुत्राय कृत्तिकाः //
text_mt: The Kṛttikās gave five to their son: / Haṃsāsya, Kuṇḍajaṭhara, Bahugrīva, Hayānana, and Kūrmagrīva.

sanskrit_iast:
sthāṇujaṅghaṃ kumbhavaktraṃ lohajaṅghaṃ mahānanam /
piṇḍākāraṃ ca pañacaitān daduḥ skandāyaṭa carṣayaḥ //
meaning:
स्थाणुजङ्घं कुम्भवक्त्रं लोहजङ्घं महाननम् /
पिण्डाकारं च पञचैतान् ददुः स्कन्दायट चर्षयः //
text_mt: The sages gave these five to Skanda: / Sthāṇujaṅgha, Kumbhavaktra, Lohajaṅgha, Mahānana, and Piṇḍākāra.

sanskrit_iast:
nāgajihvaṃ candrabhāsaṃ pāṇikūrmaṃ śaśīkṣakam /
cāṣavaktraṃ ca jambūkaṃ dadau tīrthaḥ pṛthūdakaḥ //
meaning:
नागजिह्वं चन्द्रभासं पाणिकूर्मं शशीक्षकम् /
चाषवक्त्रं च जम्बूकं ददौ तीर्थः पृथूदकः //
text_mt: The tīrtha Pṛthūdaka gave Nāgajihva, Candrabhāsa, / Pāṇikūrma, Śaśīkṣaka, Cāṣavaktra, and Jambūka.

sanskrit_iast:
cakratīrthaṃ sucajakrākṣaṃ makarāśraṃ gayāśiraḥ /
gaṇaṃ pañcaśikhaṃ nāma dadau kanakhalaḥ svakam //
meaning:
चक्रतीर्थं सुचजक्राक्षं मकराश्रं गयाशिरः /
गणं पञ्चशिखं नाम ददौ कनखलः स्वकम् //
text_mt: Cakratīrtha gave Sucakrākṣa; Gayāśiras gave Makarāśra; / Kanakhala gave his own gaṇa named Pañcaśikha.

sanskrit_iast:
bandhudattaṃ vājiśiro bāhuśālaṃ ca puṣkaram /
sarvauñjasaṃ māhiṣakaṃ mānasaḥ piṅgalaṃ yathā //
meaning:
बन्धुदत्तं वाजिशिरो बाहुशालं च पुष्करम् /
सर्वौञ्जसं माहिषकं मानसः पिङ्गलं यथा //
text_mt: Puṣkara gave Bandhudatta, Vājiśiras, and Bāhuśāla; / Mānasa likewise gave Sarvojasa, Māhiṣaka, and Piṅgala.

sanskrit_iast:
rudramauśanasaḥ prādāt tato 'nye mātaro daduḥ /
vasudāmāṃ somatīrthaḥ prabhāso nandinīmapi //
meaning:
रुद्रमौशनसः प्रादात् ततो ऽन्ये मातरो ददुः /
वसुदामां सोमतीर्थः प्रभासो नन्दिनीमपि //
text_mt: Auśanasa gave Rudra; then other mothers gave: / Somatīrtha gave Vasudāmā, and Prabhāsa gave Nandinī;

sanskrit_iast:
indratīrthaṃ viśokāṃ ca udapāno ghanasvanām /
saptasārasvataḥ prādānmātaraścaturodbhutāḥ //
meaning:
इन्द्रतीर्थं विशोकां च उदपानो घनस्वनाम् /
सप्तसारस्वतः प्रादान्मातरश्चतुरोद्भुताः //
text_mt: Indratīrtha gave Viśokā, and Udapāna gave Ghanasvanā; / Saptasārasvata gave four wondrous mothers:

sanskrit_iast:
gītapriyāṃ mādhavīṃ ca tīrthanemiṃ smitānanām /
ekacūḍāṃ nāgatīrthaḥ kurukṣetraṃ palāsadām //
meaning:
गीतप्रियां माधवीं च तीर्थनेमिं स्मिताननाम् /
एकचूडां नागतीर्थः कुरुक्षेत्रं पलासदाम् //
text_mt: Gītapriyā, Mādhavī, Tīrthanemi, and Smitānanā; / Nāgatīrtha gave Ekacūḍā, and Kurukṣetra gave Palāsadā;

sanskrit_iast:
brahmayoniścaṇḍaśilāṃ bhadrakālīṃ triviṣṭapaḥ /
cauṇḍīṃ bhaiṇḍīṃ yogabhaiṇḍīṃ prādāccaraṇapāvanaḥ //
meaning:
ब्रह्मयोनिश्चण्डशिलां भद्रकालीं त्रिविष्टपः /
चौण्डीं भैण्डीं योगभैण्डीं प्रादाच्चरणपावनः //
text_mt: Brahmayoni gave Caṇḍaśilā, and Triviṣṭapa gave Bhadrakālī; / Caraṇapāvana gave Cauṇḍī, Bhaiṇḍī, and Yogabhaiṇḍī;

sanskrit_iast:
sopānīyāṃ mahī prādācchālikāṃ mānaso hradaḥ /
śakaghaṇṭāṃ śatānandāṃ tatholūkhalamekhalām //
meaning:
सोपानीयां मही प्रादाच्छालिकां मानसो ह्रदः /
शकघण्टां शतानन्दां तथोलूखलमेखलाम् //
text_mt: the earth gave Sopānīyā, and Lake Mānasa gave Śālikā; / [they also gave] Śakaghaṇṭā, Śatānandā, and Ulūkhalamekhalā.

sanskrit_iast:
padmāvatī mādhavīṃ ca dadau badarikāśramaḥ /
suṣamāmaikacūḍāṃ ca devīṃ dhamadhamāṃ tathā //
meaning:
पद्मावती माधवीं च ददौ बदरिकाश्रमः /
सुषमामैकचूडां च देवीं धमधमां तथा //
text_mt: Badarikāśrama gave Padmāvatī and Mādhavī, / Suṣamā, the goddess Ekacūḍā, and Dhamadhamā.

sanskrit_iast:
utkrāthanīṃ vedamitrāṃ kedāro mātaro dadau /
sunakṣatrāṃ kadrulāṃ ca suprabhātāṃ muṅgalām //
meaning:
उत्क्राथनीं वेदमित्रां केदारो मातरो ददौ /
सुनक्षत्रां कद्रुलां च सुप्रभातां मुङ्गलाम् //
text_mt: Kedāra gave mothers: Utkrāthanī and Vedamitrā, / Sunakṣatrā, Kadrulā, Suprabhātā, and Maṅgalā.

sanskrit_iast:
devamitrāṃ citrasenāṃ dadau rudramahālayaḥ /
koṭarāmūrdhvaṇīṃ ca śrīmatīṃ bahuputrikām //
meaning:
देवमित्रां चित्रसेनां ददौ रुद्रमहालयः /
कोटरामूर्ध्वणीं च श्रीमतीं बहुपुत्रिकाम् //
text_mt: Rudramahālaya gave Devamitrā and Citrasenā, / Koṭarā, Ūrdhvaṇī, the auspicious one, and Bahuputrikā.

sanskrit_iast:
palitāṃ kamalākṣīṃ ca prayāgo mātaro dadau /
sūpalāṃ madhukumbhāṃ ca khyātiṃ dahadahāṃ parām //
meaning:
पलितां कमलाक्षीं च प्रयागो मातरो ददौ /
सूपलां मधुकुम्भां च ख्यातिं दहदहां पराम् //
text_mt: Prayāga gave mothers: Palitā and Kamalākṣī, / Sūpalā, Madhukumbhā, Khyāti, and Dahadahā the supreme.

sanskrit_iast:
prādāt khaṭakaṭāṃ cānyāṃ sarvapāpavimocanaḥ /
saṃtānikāṃ vikalikāṃ kramaścatvaravāsinīm //
meaning:
प्रादात् खटकटां चान्यां सर्वपापविमोचनः /
संतानिकां विकलिकां क्रमश्चत्वरवासिनीम् //
text_mt: Sarvapāpavimocana gave the other one, Khaṭakaṭā, / Saṃtānikā, Vikalikā, and Catvaravāsinī in turn.

sanskrit_iast:
jaleśvarīṃ kukkuṭikāṃ sudāmāṃ lohamekhalām /
vapuṣmatyutmukākṣī ca kokanāmā mahāśanī /
raudrā karkaṭikā tuṇḍā śvetatīrtho dadau tvimāḥ //
meaning:
जलेश्वरीं कुक्कुटिकां सुदामां लोहमेखलाम् /
वपुष्मत्युत्मुकाक्षी च कोकनामा महाशनी /
रौद्रा कर्कटिका तुण्डा श्वेततीर्थो ददौ त्विमाः //
text_mt: Śvetatīrtha gave these: Jaleśvarī, Kukkuṭikā, Sudāmā, Lohamekhalā, / Vapuṣmatī, Ulmukākṣī, Kokanāmā, Mahāśanī, Raudrā, Karkaṭikā, and Tuṇḍā.

sanskrit_iast:
etāni bhūtāni gaṇāṃśca mātaro dṛṣṭvā mahātmā vinatātanūjaḥ /
dadau mayūraṃ svasutaṃ mahājavaṃ tathāruṇastāmracūḍaṃ ca putram //
meaning:
एतानि भूतानि गणांश्च मातरो दृष्ट्वा महात्मा विनतातनूजः /
ददौ मयूरं स्वसुतं महाजवं तथारुणस्ताम्रचूडं च पुत्रम् //
text_mt: Seeing these spirits, gaṇas, and mothers, the great-souled son of Vinatā / gave his own swift-moving son, the peacock, and Aruṇa gave his son, the rooster.

sanskrit_iast:
śakti hutāśo 'drisutā ca vastraṃ daṇḍaṃ guruḥ sā kuṭilā kamaṇḍalum /
mālāṃ hariḥ śūladharaḥ patākāṃ kaṇṭhe ca hāraṃ maghavānurastaḥ //
meaning:
शक्ति हुताशो ऽद्रिसुता च वस्त्रं दण्डं गुरुः सा कुटिला कमण्डलुम् /
मालां हरिः शूलधरः पताकां कण्ठे च हारं मघवानुरस्तः //
text_mt: The Fire gave a spear, the Mountain's daughter gave garments, the Guru gave a staff, that Kuṭilā gave a water-pot, / Hari gave a garland, the trident-bearer gave a banner, and Indra gave a necklace from his own chest for his neck.

sanskrit_iast:
gaṇairvṛto mātṛbiranvayāto mayūrasaṃstho varaśaktipāṇiḥ /
sainyādhipatye sa kṛto bhavena rarāja sūryeva mahāvapuṣmān //
iti śrīvāmanapurāṇe ekatriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
meaning:
गणैर्वृतो मातृबिरन्वयातो मयूरसंस्थो वरशक्तिपाणिः /
सैन्याधिपत्ये स कृतो भवेन रराज सूर्येव महावपुष्मान् //
इति श्रीवामनपुराणे एकत्रिंशो ऽध्यायः
text_mt:
Surrounded by gaṇas, followed by the mothers, mounted on the peacock, with the excellent spear in his hand, / having been appointed to command of the army by Bhava, he shone like the sun, possessed of a mighty body.

Thus ends the thirty-first chapter in the auspicious Vāmana Purāṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
pulastya uvāca /
senāpatye 'bhiṣiktastu kumāro daivatairatha /
praṇipatya bhavaṃ bhaktyā girijāṃ pāvakaṃ śucim //
meaning:
पुलस्त्य उवाच /
सेनापत्ये ऽभिषिक्तस्तु कुमारो दैवतैरथ /
प्रणिपत्य भवं भक्त्या गिरिजां पावकं शुचिम् //
text_mt: Pulastya said: / Then Kumāra, having been consecrated to the generalship by the gods, / bowed down with devotion before Bhava, the Mountain-born goddess, and the pure Fire,

sanskrit_iast:
ṣaṭ kṛttikāśca śirasā praṇamya kuṭilāmapi /
brahmāṇaṃ ca namaskṛtya idaṃ vacanamabravīt //
meaning:
षट् कृत्तिकाश्च शिरसा प्रणम्य कुटिलामपि /
ब्रह्माणं च नमस्कृत्य इदं वचनमब्रवीत् //
text_mt: and having bowed his head before the six Kṛttikās and Kuṭilā, / and having paid homage to Brahmā, spoke these words:

sanskrit_iast:
kumāra uvāca /
namo 'stu bhavatāṃ devā oṃ namo 'stu tapodhanāḥ /
yuṣmatprasādājjeṣyāmi śatrū mahiṣatārakau //
meaning:
कुमार उवाच /
नमो ऽस्तु भवतां देवा ओं नमो ऽस्तु तपोधनाः /
युष्मत्प्रसादाज्जेष्यामि शत्रू महिषतारकौ //
text_mt: Kumāra said: / "Obeisance to you, O gods! Om, obeisance to you, rich in austerity! / By your grace I will conquer the enemies, Mahiṣa and Tāraka."

sanskrit_iast:
śiśurasmi na jānāmi vaktuṃ kiñcana devatāḥ /
dīyatāṃ brahmaṇā sārddhamanujña mama sāmpratam //
meaning:
शिशुरस्मि न जानामि वक्तुं किञ्चन देवताः /
दीयतां ब्रह्मणा सार्द्धमनुज्ञ मम साम्प्रतम् //
text_mt: I am a child, O gods, and know not how to speak at all. / Let permission now be given to me together with Brahmā.
