text_mt: “What is it to you to conquer mortal men, O Daitya? Bring the unconquered under your rule! / If you wish to strike, then turn your hand against the End-maker.

sanskrit_iast:
sa balī śāsanaṃ tubhyaṃ na karoti mahāsura /
tasmiñjite hi vijitaṃ sarvaṃ manyasva bhūtalam //
meaning:
स बली शासनं तुभ्यं न करोति महासुर /
तस्मिञ्जिते हि विजितं सर्वं मन्यस्व भूतलम् //
text_mt: He is mighty, O great asura, and does not obey your command; / indeed, once he is conquered, consider the entire earth conquered!”

sanskrit_iast:
sa tad vasiṣṭhavacanaṃ niśamya danupuṅgavaḥ /
jagāma dharmarājānaṃ vijetuṃ daṇḍapāṇinam //
meaning:
स तद् वसिष्ठवचनं निशम्य दनुपुङ्गवः /
जगाम धर्मराजानं विजेतुं दण्डपाणिनम् //
text_mt: Hearing that speech of Vasiṣṭha, that bull among Danu's sons / went to conquer the King of Dharma, who holds the staff in hand.

sanskrit_iast:
tamāyāntaṃ yamaḥ śrutvā matvāvadhyaṃ ca saṃyuge /
sa samāruhya mahiṣaṃ keśavāntikamāgamat //
meaning:
तमायान्तं यमः श्रुत्वा मत्वावध्यं च संयुगे /
स समारुह्य महिषं केशवान्तिकमागमत् //
text_mt: Hearing that he was coming, and considering him unslayable in battle, / Yama mounted his buffalo and went into the presence of Keśava.

sanskrit_iast:
sametya cābhivādyainaṃ provāca muraceṣṭitam /
sa cāha gaccha māmadya prepayasva mahāsuram //
meaning:
समेत्य चाभिवाद्यैनं प्रोवाच मुरचेष्टितम् /
स चाह गच्छ मामद्य प्रेपयस्व महासुरम् //
text_mt: Approaching and greeting him, he told him of Mura's deeds. / And he said: 'Go, dispatch the great asura to me today.'

sanskrit_iast:
sa vāsudevavacanaṃ śrutvābhyāgāt tvarānvitaḥ /
etasminnantare daityaḥ saṃprāpto nagarīṃ muraḥ //
meaning:
स वासुदेववचनं श्रुत्वाभ्यागात् त्वरान्वितः /
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे दैत्यः संप्राप्तो नगरीं मुरः //
text_mt: Hearing Vāsudeva's words, he returned in haste. / In the meantime, the Daitya Mura arrived at the city.

sanskrit_iast:
tamāgataṃ yamaḥ prāha kiṃ muro karttumicchasi /
vadasva vacanaṃ karttā tvadīyaṃ dānaveśvara //
meaning:
तमागतं यमः प्राह किं मुरो कर्त्तुमिच्छसि /
वदस्व वचनं कर्त्ता त्वदीयं दानवेश्वर //
text_mt: Yama said to him upon his arrival: 'O Mura, what do you wish to do? / Speak your word, O lord of the Dānavas; I will do it.'

sanskrit_iast:
mururuvāca /
yama prajāsaṃyamānannivṛttiṃ karttumarhasi /
no cet tavādya chittvāhaṃ mūrdhānaṃ pātaye bhuvi //
meaning:
मुरुरुवाच /
यम प्रजासंयमानन्निवृत्तिं कर्त्तुमर्हसि /
नो चेत् तवाद्य छित्त्वाहं मूर्धानं पातये भुवि //
text_mt: Mura said: / 'O Yama, you ought to cease restraining living beings; / otherwise, severing your head today, I shall cast it down upon the earth.'

sanskrit_iast:
tamāha dharmarāḍ brahman yadi māṃ saṃyamād bhavān /
gopāyati muro satyaṃ kariṣye vacanaṃ tava/cha /
34.55 murastamāha bhavataḥ kaḥ saṃyantā vadasva māma /
ahamena parājitya vārayāmi na saṃśayaḥ //
meaning:
तमाह धर्मराड् ब्रह्मन् यदि मां संयमाद् भवान् /
गोपायति मुरो सत्यं करिष्ये वचनं तव/छ /
34.55 मुरस्तमाह भवतः कः संयन्ता वदस्व माम /
अहमेन पराजित्य वारयामि न संशयः //
text_mt:
The king of dharma said to him, 'O Brahmin, if you preserve me
from restraint, O Mura, in truth I will do your bidding.'

Mura said to him, 'Tell me who is your restrainer;
having conquered him, I shall ward him off, there is no doubt.'

sanskrit_iast:
yamastaṃ prāhaṃ māṃ viṣṇurdevaścakragadādharaḥ /
śvetadvīpanivāsī yaḥ sa māṃ saṃyamate 'vyayaḥ //
meaning:
यमस्तं प्राहं मां विष्णुर्देवश्चक्रगदाधरः /
श्वेतद्वीपनिवासी यः स मां संयमते ऽव्ययः //
text_mt: Yama said to him: 'Viṣṇu, the imperishable god who holds the discus and mace, / who dwells in Śvetadvīpa—he restrains me.'

sanskrit_iast:
tamāha daityaśārdūlaḥ kvāsau vasati durjayaḥ /
svayaṃ tatra gamiṣyāmi tasya saṃyamanodyataḥ //
meaning:
तमाह दैत्यशार्दूलः क्वासौ वसति दुर्जयः /
स्वयं तत्र गमिष्यामि तस्य संयमनोद्यतः //
text_mt: The tiger among Daityas said to him: 'Where does that invincible one dwell? / I will go there myself, intent upon restraining him.'

sanskrit_iast:
tamuvāca yamo gaccha kṣīrodaṃ nāma sāgaram /
tatrāste bhagavān viṣṇurlokanātho jaganmayaḥ //
meaning:
तमुवाच यमो गच्छ क्षीरोदं नाम सागरम् /
तत्रास्ते भगवान् विष्णुर्लोकनाथो जगन्मयः //
text_mt: Yama said to him: 'Go to the ocean named the Ocean of Milk; / there resides the Lord Viṣṇu, the lord of the worlds, whose essence is the universe.'

sanskrit_iast:
murastadvākyamākarṇya prāha gacchāmi keśavam /
kiṃ tu tvayā na tāvaddhi saṃyamyā dharma mānavāḥ //
meaning:
मुरस्तद्वाक्यमाकर्ण्य प्राह गच्छामि केशवम् /
किं तु त्वया न तावद्धि संयम्या धर्म मानवाः //
text_mt: Hearing his words, Mura said: 'I am going to Keśava; / however, O Dharma, humans must not be restrained by you until then.'

sanskrit_iast:
sa prāha gaccha tvaṃ tāvat pravartiṣye jayaṃ prati /
saṃyanturvā yathā syāddhi tato yuddhaṃ samācara //
meaning:
स प्राह गच्छ त्वं तावत् प्रवर्तिष्ये जयं प्रति /
संयन्तुर्वा यथा स्याद्धि ततो युद्धं समाचर //
text_mt: He said: 'Go for now; I will act according to victory / or whatever becomes of the restrainer; then wage battle.'

sanskrit_iast:
ityevāmuktvā vacanaṃ dugdhābdhimagamanmuraḥ /
yatrāste śeṣaparyaṅke caturmūrtirjanārdanaḥ //
meaning:
इत्येवामुक्त्वा वचनं दुग्धाब्धिमगमन्मुरः /
यत्रास्ते शेषपर्यङ्के चतुर्मूर्तिर्जनार्दनः //
text_mt: Having spoken these words, Mura went to the Ocean of Milk, / where Janārdana of four forms resides on the couch of Śeṣa.

sanskrit_iast:
nārada uvāca /
caturmūrttiḥ kathaṃ viṣṇureka eva nigadyate /
sarvagatvāt kathamapi avyaktatvācca tadvada //
meaning:
नारद उवाच /
चतुर्मूर्त्तिः कथं विष्णुरेक एव निगद्यते /
सर्वगत्वात् कथमपि अव्यक्तत्वाच्च तद्वद //
text_mt: Nārada said: / 'How is Viṣṇu called four-formed, when he is only one? / Tell me how that is, on account of his omnipresence and unmanifest nature.'

sanskrit_iast:
pulastya uvāca /
avyaktaḥ sarvago 'pīha eka eva mahāmune /
caturmūrtirjagannātho yatā brahmaṃstathā śṛṇu //
meaning:
पुलस्त्य उवाच /
अव्यक्तः सर्वगो ऽपीह एक एव महामुने /
चतुर्मूर्तिर्जगन्नाथो यता ब्रह्मंस्तथा शृणु //
text_mt: Pulastya said: / 'Though unmanifest and omnipresent, he is one alone here, O great sage; / hear, O Brahmin, how the Lord of the Universe is four-formed.'

sanskrit_iast:
apratarkyamanirdeśyaṃ śuklaṃ śāntaṃ paraṃ padam /
vāsudevākhyamāvyaktaṃ smṛtaṃ dvādaśapatrakam //
meaning:
अप्रतर्क्यमनिर्देश्यं शुक्लं शान्तं परं पदम् /
वासुदेवाख्यमाव्यक्तं स्मृतं द्वादशपत्रकम् //
text_mt: Inconceivable, indescribable, pure white, tranquil is the supreme state; / known as Vāsudeva, unmanifest, it is handed down as twelve-petaled.

sanskrit_iast:
nārada uvāca /
kathaṃ śuklaṃ kathaṃ śāntamapratarkyamaninditam /
kānyasya dvādaśaivoktā patrakā tāni me vada //
meaning:
नारद उवाच /
कथं शुक्लं कथं शान्तमप्रतर्क्यमनिन्दितम् /
कान्यस्य द्वादशैवोक्ता पत्रका तानि मे वद //
text_mt: Nārada said: / 'How is it white, how tranquil, inconceivable, and blameless? / And what are its twelve petals that are spoken of? Tell me that.'

sanskrit_iast:
pulastya uvāca /
śṛṇuṣva guhyaṃ paramaṃ parameṣṭhiprabhāṣitam /
śrataṃ sanatkumārema tenākhyātaṃ ca tanmama //
meaning:
पुलस्त्य उवाच /
शृणुष्व गुह्यं परमं परमेष्ठिप्रभाषितम् /
श्रतं सनत्कुमारेम तेनाख्यातं च तन्मम //
text_mt: Pulastya said: / 'Listen to the supreme secret uttered by the Supreme Lord, / heard by Sanatkumāra, and told by him to me.'

sanskrit_iast:
nārada uvāca /
ko 'yaṃ sanatkumāreti yasyoktaṃ brahmaṇā svayam /
tavāpi tena gaditaṃ vada māmanupūrvaśaḥ //
meaning:
नारद उवाच /
को ऽयं सनत्कुमारेति यस्योक्तं ब्रह्मणा स्वयम् /
तवापि तेन गदितं वद मामनुपूर्वशः //
text_mt: Nārada said: / 'Who is this Sanatkumāra to whom Brahmā himself spoke, / and by whom it was also told to you? Tell me in order.'

sanskrit_iast:
pulastya uvāca/ /
dharmasya bhāryāhiṃsākhyā tasyāṃ putracatuṣṭayam /
saṃjātaṃ munisārdula yogaśāstravicārakam //
meaning:
पुलस्त्य उवाच/ /
धर्मस्य भार्याहिंसाख्या तस्यां पुत्रचतुष्टयम् /
संजातं मुनिसार्दुल योगशास्त्रविचारकम् //
text_mt: Pulastya said: / 'Dharma's wife was named Ahiṃsā; upon her, O tiger among sages, / four sons were born who were reflective students of the Yoga treatises.'

sanskrit_iast:
jyeṣṭhaḥ sanatkumāro 'bhūd dvitīyaśca sanātanaḥ /
tṛtīyaḥ sanako nāma caturthaśca sanandanaḥ //
meaning:
ज्येष्ठः सनत्कुमारो ऽभूद् द्वितीयश्च सनातनः /
तृतीयः सनको नाम चतुर्थश्च सनन्दनः //
text_mt: The eldest was Sanatkumāra, the second was Sanātana, / the third was named Sanaka, and the fourth was Sanandana.

sanskrit_iast:
sāṃkhyevettāramaparaṃ kapilaṃ voḍhumāsurim /
dṛṣṭvā pañcaśikhaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ yogayuktaṃ taponidhim //
meaning:
सांख्येवेत्तारमपरं कपिलं वोढुमासुरिम् /
दृष्ट्वा पञ्चशिखं श्रेष्ठं योगयुक्तं तपोनिधिम् //
text_mt: Having seen the other knower of Sāṃkhya, Kapila, [as well as] Āsuri and Voḍhu, / [and] the eminent Pañcaśikha, joined in yoga and a treasury of asceticism,

sanskrit_iast:
jñānayogaṃ na te dadyurjyāyāṃso 'pi kanīyasām /
mānamuktaṃ mahāyogaṃ kapilādīnapāsataḥ //
meaning:
ज्ञानयोगं न ते दद्युर्ज्यायांसो ऽपि कनीयसाम् /
मानमुक्तं महायोगं कपिलादीनपासतः //
text_mt: they, though elder, would not give the yoga of knowledge to those who were younger. / Giving up pride, they attended upon Kapila and the others in the great yoga.

sanskrit_iast:
sanatkumāraś cābhyetya brahmāṇaṃ kamalodbhavam /
apṛcchad yogavijñānaṃ tamuvāca prajāpatiḥ //
meaning:
सनत्कुमारश् चाभ्येत्य ब्रह्माणं कमलोद्भवम् /
अपृच्छद् योगविज्ञानं तमुवाच प्रजापतिः //
text_mt: Sanatkumāra, approaching Brahmā born from the lotus, / inquired about the specific knowledge of yoga. Prajāpati said to him:'

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca /
kathayiṣyāmi te sādhya yadi putratvamicchasi /
yasya kasya na vaktavyaṃ tatsatyaṃ nānyatheti hi //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच /
कथयिष्यामि ते साध्य यदि पुत्रत्वमिच्छसि /
यस्य कस्य न वक्तव्यं तत्सत्यं नान्यथेति हि //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / 'I shall tell you, O virtuous one, if you desire the state of a son; / it must not be told to just anyone—that is the truth and not otherwise.'

sanskrit_iast:
sanatkumāra uvāca/ /
putra evāsmi deveśa yataḥ śiṣyo 'smyahaṃ vibho /
na viseṣo 'sti putrasya śiṣyasya ca pitāmaha //
meaning:
सनत्कुमार उवाच/ /
पुत्र एवास्मि देवेश यतः शिष्यो ऽस्म्यहं विभो /
न विसेषो ऽस्ति पुत्रस्य शिष्यस्य च पितामह //
text_mt: Sanatkumāra said: / 'I am indeed a son, O Lord of gods, since I am a disciple, O all-pervading one; / there is no distinction between a son and a disciple, O Grandfather.'

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca /
viśeṣaḥ śiṣyaputrābhyāṃ vidyate dharmanandana /
dharmakarmasamāyoge tathāpi gadataḥ śruṇu //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच /
विशेषः शिष्यपुत्राभ्यां विद्यते धर्मनन्दन /
धर्मकर्मसमायोगे तथापि गदतः श्रुणु //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / 'There is a distinction between a disciple and a son, O delight of Dharma, / in the conjunction of duties and actions. Nevertheless, listen as I speak:'

sanskrit_iast:
punnāmno narakāt trāti putrasteneha gīyate /
seṣapāpaharaḥ śiṣya itīyaṃ vaidikī śrutiḥ //
meaning:
पुन्नाम्नो नरकात् त्राति पुत्रस्तेनेह गीयते /
सेषपापहरः शिष्य इतीयं वैदिकी श्रुतिः //
text_mt: A son protects from the hell named Put, therefore he is praised as such in the world; / a disciple removes the remaining sin—such is this Vedic revelation.'

sanskrit_iast:
sanatkumāra uvāca /
ko 'yaṃ punnāmako deva narakāt trāti putrakaḥ /
kasmāccheṣaṃ tataḥ pāpaṃ harecchiṣyaśca tadvada //
meaning:
सनत्कुमार उवाच /
को ऽयं पुन्नामको देव नरकात् त्राति पुत्रकः /
कस्माच्छेषं ततः पापं हरेच्छिष्यश्च तद्वद //
text_mt: Sanatkumāra said: / 'What is this hell named Put, O god, from which a son saves? / And why does a disciple remove the remaining sin? Tell me that.'

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca /
etat purāṇaṃ paramaṃ maharṣe yogāṅgayuktaṃ ca sadaiva yacca /
tathaiva cograṃ bhayahāri mānavaṃ vadāmi te sādhya niśāmayainam //
iti śrīvāmanapurāṇe catustriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच /
एतत् पुराणं परमं महर्षे योगाङ्गयुक्तं च सदैव यच्च /
तथैव चोग्रं भयहारि मानवं वदामि ते साध्य निशामयैनम् //
इति श्रीवामनपुराणे चतुस्त्रिंशो ऽध्यायः
text_mt:
Brahmā said: / 'This supreme Purāṇa, O great sage, which is ever endowed with the limbs of yoga, / and likewise that which is fierce, removing fear for humankind, I tell you, O virtuous one; listen to it.'

Thus ends the thirty-fourth chapter in the glorious Vāmana Purāṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca /
paradārābhigamanaṃ pāpīyāṃsopasevanam /
pāruṣyaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ prathamaṃ narakaṃ smṛtam //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच /
परदाराभिगमनं पापीयांसोपसेवनम् /
पारुष्यं सर्वभूतानां प्रथमं नरकं स्मृतम् //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / 'Adultery with another's wife, consorting with the vile, / harshness toward all beings is traditionally remembered as the first hell.'

sanskrit_iast:
phalasteyaṃ mahāpāpaṃ phalahīnaṃ tathāṭanam /
chedanaṃ vṛkṣajātīnāṃ dvitīyaṃ narakaṃ smṛtam //
meaning:
फलस्तेयं महापापं फलहीनं तथाटनम् /
छेदनं वृक्षजातीनां द्वितीयं नरकं स्मृतम् //
text_mt: The theft of fruit—a great sin—and fruitlessly roaming about, / the felling of varieties of trees is remembered as the second hell.'

sanskrit_iast:
varjyādānaṃ tathā duṣṭamavadhyavadhabandhanam /
vivādamarthahetūtthaṃ tṛtīyaṃ narakaṃ smṛtam //
meaning:
वर्ज्यादानं तथा दुष्टमवध्यवधबन्धनम् /
विवादमर्थहेतूत्थं तृतीयं नरकं स्मृतम् //
text_mt: Taking what should be avoided, wicked slaughter and binding of what should not be killed, / [and] dispute arising from the motive of wealth is remembered as the third hell.'

sanskrit_iast:
bhayadaṃ sarvasattvānāṃ bhavabhūti vināśanam /
bhraṃśanaṃ nijadharmāṇāṃ caturthaṃ narakaṃ smṛtam //
meaning:
भयदं सर्वसत्त्वानां भवभूति विनाशनम् /
भ्रंशनं निजधर्माणां चतुर्थं नरकं स्मृतम् //
text_mt: Causing fear to all creatures, destroying prosperity and well-being, / [and] abandoning one's own duties is remembered as the fourth hell.'

sanskrit_iast:
māraṇaṃ mitrakauṭilyaṃ lithyābhiśapanaṃ ca yat /
miṣṭaukāśanamityuktaṃ pañcamaṃ tu nṛpācanam //
meaning:
मारणं मित्रकौटिल्यं लिथ्याभिशपनं च यत् /
मिष्टौकाशनमित्युक्तं पञ्चमं तु नृपाचनम् //
text_mt: Murder, crookedness toward friends, false accusation, / and eating sweet food alone is declared to be the fifth boiler of men.'

sanskrit_iast:
yantraḥ phalādiharaṇaṃ yamanaṃ yoganāśanam /
yānayugyasya haraṇaṃ ṣaṣṭhamuktaṃ nṛpācanam //
meaning:
यन्त्रः फलादिहरणं यमनं योगनाशनम् /
यानयुग्यस्य हरणं षष्ठमुक्तं नृपाचनम् //
text_mt: Stealing implements, fruit and the like, suppression, destruction of yoga, / [and] stealing a vehicle and draft animal is declared to be the sixth boiler of men.'

sanskrit_iast:
rājabhāgaharaṃ mūḍhaṃ rājajāyāniṣevaṇam /
rājye tvahitakāritvaṃ saptamaṃ nirayaṃ smṛtam //
meaning:
राजभागहरं मूढं राजजायानिषेवणम् /
राज्ये त्वहितकारित्वं सप्तमं निरयं स्मृतम् //
text_mt: Stealing the king's share, foolishly enjoying the king's wife, / and doing injury to the realm is remembered as the seventh hell.'

sanskrit_iast:
lubdhatvaṃ lolupatvaṃ ca labdhadharmārthanāśanam /
lālāsaṃkīrṇamevoktamaṣṭamaṃ narakaṃ smṛtam //
meaning:
लुब्धत्वं लोलुपत्वं च लब्धधर्मार्थनाशनम् /
लालासंकीर्णमेवोक्तमष्टमं नरकं स्मृतम् //
text_mt: Greed, covetousness, destruction of acquired virtue and wealth, / and being steeped in lust is declared to be the eighth hell.'

sanskrit_iast:
viproṣyaṃ brahmaharaṇaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ vinindanam /
virodhaṃ bandhubhiścoktaṃ navamaṃ narapācanam //
meaning:
विप्रोष्यं ब्रह्महरणं ब्राह्मणानां विनिन्दनम् /
विरोधं बन्धुभिश्चोक्तं नवमं नरपाचनम् //
text_mt: Dwelling abroad, stealing sacred knowledge, reviling Brahmins, / and conflict with kinsmen is declared to be the ninth boiler of men.'

sanskrit_iast:
śiṣṭācāravināśaṃ ca śiṣṭadveṣaṃ śiśorvadham /
śāstrasteyaṃ dharmanāśaṃ daśamaṃ parikīrtitam //
meaning:
शिष्टाचारविनाशं च शिष्टद्वेषं शिशोर्वधम् /
शास्त्रस्तेयं धर्मनाशं दशमं परिकीर्तितम् //
text_mt: The destruction of proper conduct, hatred toward the virtuous, slaying an infant, / theft of sacred texts, and destruction of righteousness is proclaimed as the tenth.'

sanskrit_iast:
ṣaḍaṅganidhanaṃ ghoraṃ ṣāṅguṇyapratiṣedhanam /
ekādaśamamevoktaṃ narakaṃ sadbhiruttamam //
meaning:
षडङ्गनिधनं घोरं षाङ्गुण्यप्रतिषेधनम् /
एकादशममेवोक्तं नरकं सद्भिरुत्तमम् //
text_mt: The dreadful destruction of the six limbs [of the Veda], rejection of the six royal policies / is declared by the good to be the prominent eleventh hell.'

sanskrit_iast:
satsu nityaṃ sadā vairamanācāramasatkriyā /
saṃskāraparihīnatvamidaṃ dvādaśamaṃ smṛtam //
meaning:
सत्सु नित्यं सदा वैरमनाचारमसत्क्रिया /
संस्कारपरिहीनत्वमिदं द्वादशमं स्मृतम् //
text_mt: Perpetual enmity toward the good, improper conduct, unrighteous acts, / [and] being destitute of the purificatory rites—this is remembered as the twelfth.'

sanskrit_iast:
hānirdharmārthakāmanāmapavargasya hāraṇam /
saṃbhedaḥ saṃvidāmetat trayodaśamamucyate //
meaning:
हानिर्धर्मार्थकामनामपवर्गस्य हारणम् /
संभेदः संविदामेतत् त्रयोदशममुच्यते //
text_mt: Loss of dharma, wealth, and desire, forfeiture of final emancipation, / and violation of agreements—this is spoken of as the thirteenth.'

sanskrit_iast:
kṛpaṇaṃ dharmahīnaṃ ca yad varjyaṃ yacca vahnidam /
catudrdaśamamovoktaṃ narakaṃ tad vigarhitam //
meaning:
कृपणं धर्महीनं च यद् वर्ज्यं यच्च वह्निदम् /
चतुद्र्दशममोवोक्तं नरकं तद् विगर्हितम् //
text_mt: Stinginess, being devoid of dharma, whatever should be shunned, and arson— / that is declared to be the reprehensible fourteenth hell.'

sanskrit_iast:
ajñānaṃ cāpyamuyatvamaśaucamaśubhāvaham /
smṛtaṃ tat pañcadaśamamastyavacanāni ca //
meaning:
अज्ञानं चाप्यमुयत्वमशौचमशुभावहम् /
स्मृतं तत् पञ्चदशममस्त्यवचनानि च //
text_mt: Ignorance, lack of restraint, impurity bringing misfortune, / and untrue words—that is remembered as the fifteenth.'

sanskrit_iast:
ālasyaṃ vai ṣoḍaśamamākrośaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ /
sarvasya cātatāyitvalamāvāseṣvagnidīpanam //
meaning:
आलस्यं वै षोडशममाक्रोशं च विशेषतः /
सर्वस्य चाततायित्वलमावासेष्वग्निदीपनम् //
text_mt: Laziness is indeed the sixteenth, especially reviling others, / behaving as an assassin toward everyone, and setting fire to dwellings.'

sanskrit_iast:
icchā ca paradāreṣu narakāya nigadyate /
īrṣaryābhāvaśca satyeṣu uddhṛttaṃ tu vigarhitam //
meaning:
इच्छा च परदारेषु नरकाय निगद्यते /
ईर्षर्याभावश्च सत्येषु उद्धृत्तं तु विगर्हितम् //
text_mt: And desire for another's wife is said to lead to hell; / also lack of jealousy toward truths, but haughtiness is condemned.

sanskrit_iast:
etaistu pāpaiḥ puruṣaḥ punnamādyairna saṃśayaḥ /
saṃyuktaḥ prīṇayed devaṃ saṃtatyā jagataḥ patim //
meaning:
एतैस्तु पापैः पुरुषः पुन्नमाद्यैर्न संशयः /
संयुक्तः प्रीणयेद् देवं संतत्या जगतः पतिम् //
text_mt: Endowed with these sins—such as the one called 'Pum' and the others, no doubt— / a man should please God, the Lord of the universe, through offspring.

sanskrit_iast:
prītaḥ sṛṣṭyā tu śubhayā sa pāpādyena mucyate /
puṃnāmanarakaṃ ghoraṃ vināśayati sarvataḥ //
meaning:
प्रीतः सृष्ट्या तु शुभया स पापाद्येन मुच्यते /
पुंनामनरकं घोरं विनाशयति सर्वतः //
text_mt: Pleosed by auspicious creation, he is liberated from that sin and the rest; / he completely destroys the dreadful hell named Pum.

sanskrit_iast:
etasmāt kāraṇāt sādhya sutaḥ putreti gadyate /
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi śeṣapāpasya lakṣaṇam //
meaning:
एतस्मात् कारणात् साध्य सुतः पुत्रेति गद्यते /
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि शेषपापस्य लक्षणम् //
text_mt: For this reason, O Sādhya, a son is called 'putra'. / Hereafter, I shall proclaim the characteristics of the remaining sins:

sanskrit_iast:
ṛmaṃ devarṣibhūtānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ viśeṣataḥ /
pitṛṇāṃ ca dvijaśreṣṭha sarvarvaṇeṣu caikatā //
meaning:
ऋमं देवर्षिभूतानां मनुष्याणां विशेषतः /
पितृणां च द्विजश्रेष्ठ सर्वर्वणेषु चैकता //
text_mt: The debt to the gods, ṛṣis, spirits, and especially to men / and to the ancestors, O best of the twice-born, and equality among all castes,

sanskrit_iast:
oṅkārādapi nirvṛttiḥ pāpakāryakṛtaśca yaḥ /
matsyādaśca mahāpāpamagamyāgamanaṃ tathā //
meaning:
ओङ्कारादपि निर्वृत्तिः पापकार्यकृतश्च यः /
मत्स्यादश्च महापापमगम्यागमनं तथा //
text_mt: turning away from the Praṇava, doing sinful deeds, / eating fish—a great sin—and having intercourse with forbidden women,

sanskrit_iast:
ghṛtādivikrayaṃ ghoraṃ caṇḍālādiparigrahaḥ /
svadoṣācchādanaṃ pāpaṃ paradoṣaprakāśanam //
meaning:
घृतादिविक्रयं घोरं चण्डालादिपरिग्रहः /
स्वदोषाच्छादनं पापं परदोषप्रकाशनम् //
text_mt: the dreadful selling of clarified butter and such, accepting gifts from Caṇḍālas and the like, / hiding one's own faults and exposing the faults of others,

sanskrit_iast:
matsaritvaṃ vāgduṣṭatvaṃ niṣṭuratvaṃ tathā param /
ṭākitvaṃ tālavāditvaṃ nāmnā vācāpyadharmajam //
meaning:
मत्सरित्वं वाग्दुष्टत्वं निष्टुरत्वं तथा परम् /
टाकित्वं तालवादित्वं नाम्ना वाचाप्यधर्मजम् //
text_mt: spitefulness, wickedness of speech, and great cruelty, / jugglery, insolence of rhythm, born of unrighteousness in name and speech,

sanskrit_iast:
dāruṇatvamadhārmikyaṃ narakāvahamucyate /
etaiśca pāpaiḥ saṃyuktaḥ prīṇayed yadi śaṅkaram //
meaning:
दारुणत्वमधार्मिक्यं नरकावहमुच्यते /
एतैश्च पापैः संयुक्तः प्रीणयेद् यदि शङ्करम् //
text_mt: ferocity, and unrighteousness—these are said to bring hell. / If, endowed with these sins, one pleases Śaṅkara,

sanskrit_iast:
jñānādhiramaśeṣeṇa śeṣapāpaṃ jayet tataḥ /
śārīraṃ vācikaṃ yat tu mānasaṃ kāyikaṃ tathā //
meaning:
ज्ञानाधिरमशेषेण शेषपापं जयेत् ततः /
शारीरं वाचिकं यत् तु मानसं कायिकं तथा //
text_mt: then through the supreme resting place of knowledge one overcomes the remaining sins entirely. / Whatever [sin] is bodily, verbal, or mental,

sanskrit_iast:
pitṛmātṛkṛtaṃ yacca kṛtaṃ yaccāśritairnaraiḥ /
bhrātṛbhirbāndhavaiścāpi tasmin janmani dharmaja //
meaning:
पितृमातृकृतं यच्च कृतं यच्चाश्रितैर्नरैः /
भ्रातृभिर्बान्धवैश्चापि तस्मिन् जन्मनि धर्मज //
text_mt: whatever was done by mother and father, or done by dependent men, / or by brothers and relatives in that birth, O Dharma-born,

sanskrit_iast:
tatsarvaṃ vilayaṃ yāti sa dharmaḥ sutaśiṣyayoḥ /
viparīte bhavet sādhya viparītaḥ padakramaḥ //
meaning:
तत्सर्वं विलयं याति स धर्मः सुतशिष्ययोः /
विपरीते भवेत् साध्य विपरीतः पदक्रमः //
text_mt: all that comes to dissolution; that is the dharma of a son and a disciple. / In the reverse case, O Sādhya, the reverse order of steps would occur.

sanskrit_iast:
tasmāt putraśca śiṣyaśca vidhātavyau vipaścitā /
etadarthamabhidhyāya śiṣyācchreṣṭhataraḥ sutaḥ /
seṣāt tārayate śiṣyaḥ sarvato 'pi hi putrakaḥ //
meaning:
तस्मात् पुत्रश्च शिष्यश्च विधातव्यौ विपश्चिता /
एतदर्थमभिध्याय शिष्याच्छ्रेष्ठतरः सुतः /
सेषात् तारयते शिष्यः सर्वतो ऽपि हि पुत्रकः //
text_mt: Therefore a son and a disciple should be produced by a wise man. / Considering this purpose, a son is superior to a disciple; / a disciple delivers from the remainder, but a son [delivers] from all.

sanskrit_iast:
pulastya uvāca /
pitāmahavacaḥ śrutvā sādhyaḥ prāha tapodhanaḥ /
triḥ satyaṃ tava putro 'haṃ deva yogaṃ vadasva me //
meaning:
पुलस्त्य उवाच /
पितामहवचः श्रुत्वा साध्यः प्राह तपोधनः /
त्रिः सत्यं तव पुत्रो ऽहं देव योगं वदस्व मे //
text_mt: Pulastya said: / Hearing the Grandfather's words, the ascetic Sādhya said: / 'Truly, thrice over, I am your son, O god; tell me yoga.'

sanskrit_iast:
tamuvāca mahāyogī tvanmātāpirarau yadi /
dāsyete ca tataḥ sūnurdāyādo me 'si putraka //
meaning:
तमुवाच महायोगी त्वन्मातापिररौ यदि /
दास्येते च ततः सूनुर्दायादो मे ऽसि पुत्रक //
text_mt: The great yogin said to him: 'If your mother and father / give you, then, O child, you are my son and heir.'

sanskrit_iast:
sanatkumāraḥ provāca dāyādaparikalpanā /
yeyaṃ hi bhavatā proktā tāṃ me vyākhyātumarhasi //
meaning:
सनत्कुमारः प्रोवाच दायादपरिकल्पना /
येयं हि भवता प्रोक्ता तां मे व्याख्यातुमर्हसि //
text_mt: Sanatkumāra said: 'This classification of heirs / which was spoken by you, you should explain to me.'

sanskrit_iast:
taduktaṃ sādhyamukhyena vākyaṃ śrutvā pitāmahaḥ /
prāha prahasya bhagavān kśruṇu vatseti nārada //
meaning:
तदुक्तं साध्यमुख्येन वाक्यं श्रुत्वा पितामहः /
प्राह प्रहस्य भगवान् क्श्रुणु वत्सेति नारद //
text_mt: Hearing that speech uttered by the foremost of the Sādhyas, the Grandfather, / the blessed lord, laughed and said: 'Listen, my child', O Nārada.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca /
aurasaḥ kṣetrajaścaiva dattaḥ kṛtrima eva ca /
guḍhotpanno 'paviddhaśca dāyādā bāndhavāstu ṣaṭ //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच /
औरसः क्षेत्रजश्चैव दत्तः कृत्रिम एव च /
गुढोत्पन्नो ऽपविद्धश्च दायादा बान्धवास्तु षट् //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / 'The body-born, the field-born, the given, and the artificially made, / the secretly born, and the abandoned: these six are heirs and kinsmen.

sanskrit_iast:
amīṣu ṣaṭpu putreṣu ṛmapiṇḍadhanakriyāḥ /
gotrasmyaṃ kule vṛttiḥ pratiṣṭha śāśvatī tathā //
meaning:
अमीषु षट्पु पुत्रेषु ऋमपिण्डधनक्रियाः /
गोत्रस्म्यं कुले वृत्तिः प्रतिष्ठ शाश्वती तथा //
text_mt: Among these six sons belong the rites of debt, funeral cake, and property, / equal caste-name, livelihood in the family, and everlasting establishment.

sanskrit_iast:
kānīnaśca sahoḍhaśca krītaḥ paunarbhavastathā /
svayedattaḥ pāraśavaḥ ṣaḍadāyādabandhavāḥ //
meaning:
कानीनश्च सहोढश्च क्रीतः पौनर्भवस्तथा /
स्वयेदत्तः पारशवः षडदायादबन्धवाः //
text_mt: The maiden-born, the carried-in-the-womb, the bought, and the twice-wedded's son, / the self-given, and the Pāraśava: these six are non-heir kinsmen.

sanskrit_iast:
amībhirṛṇapiṇḍādikathā naiveha vidyate /
nāmadhārakā eveha na gotrakulasaṃmatāḥ //
meaning:
अमीभिरृणपिण्डादिकथा नैवेह विद्यते /
नामधारका एवेह न गोत्रकुलसंमताः //
text_mt: Among these, there is no discussion of debt, funeral cakes, and so forth; / they are merely name-bearers here, not acknowledged in family and clan.'

sanskrit_iast:
tat tasya vacanaṃ śrutvā brahmaṇaḥ sanakāgrajaḥ /
uvācaiṣāṃ viśeṣaṃ me brahman vyākhyātumahasi //
meaning:
तत् तस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा ब्रह्मणः सनकाग्रजः /
उवाचैषां विशेषं मे ब्रह्मन् व्याख्यातुमहसि //
text_mt: Hearing that speech of Brahmā, the elder brother of Sanaka / said: 'O Brahman, you should explain to me the distinctions among these.'

sanskrit_iast:
tato 'bravīt surapatirviśeṣaṃ śṛṇu putraka /
auraso yaḥ svayaṃ jātaḥ pratibimbamivātmanaḥ //
meaning:
ततो ऽब्रवीत् सुरपतिर्विशेषं शृणु पुत्रक /
औरसो यः स्वयं जातः प्रतिबिम्बमिवात्मनः //
text_mt: Then the Lord of gods said: 'Listen to the distinction, my child. / The body-born is he who is born from oneself, like one's own reflection.

sanskrit_iast:
klībonmatte vyasanini patyau tasyājñayā tu yā /
bhāryā hyanāturā putraṃ janayet kṣetrajastu saḥ //
meaning:
क्लीबोन्मत्ते व्यसनिनि पत्यौ तस्याज्ञया तु या /
भार्या ह्यनातुरा पुत्रं जनयेत् क्षेत्रजस्तु सः //
text_mt: When a husband is impotent, mad, or addicted, by his order a wife / who is not in distress bears a son—he is the field-born.

sanskrit_iast:
mātāpitṛbhyāṃ yo dattaḥ sa dattaḥ parigīyate /
mitraputraṃ mitradattaṃ kṛtrimaṃ prāhuruttamāḥ //
meaning:
मातापितृभ्यां यो दत्तः स दत्तः परिगीयते /
मित्रपुत्रं मित्रदत्तं कृत्रिमं प्राहुरुत्तमाः //
text_mt: He who is given by mother and father is celebrated as the given. / A friend's son given by a friend, the excellent call the artificially made.

sanskrit_iast:
na jñāyate gṛhe kena jātastviti sa gūñakaḥ /
bāhmataḥ svayamānītaḥ so 'paviddhaḥ prakīrtitaḥ //
meaning:
न ज्ञायते गृहे केन जातस्त्विति स गूञकः /
बाह्मतः स्वयमानीतः सो ऽपविद्धः प्रकीर्तितः //
text_mt: He who is born in the house, it not being known by whom, is the secretly born. / He who is brought in by oneself from outside is declared to be the abandoned.

sanskrit_iast:
kanyājātastu kānīnaḥ sagarbhoḍhaḥ sahokaḥ /
mūlyairgṛhītaḥ krītaḥ syād dvividhaḥ syāt punarbhavaḥ //
meaning:
कन्याजातस्तु कानीनः सगर्भोढः सहोकः /
मूल्यैर्गृहीतः क्रीतः स्याद् द्विविधः स्यात् पुनर्भवः //
text_mt: The one born of an unmarried maiden is the maiden-born; he who is carried in the womb [at marriage] is the carried; / he who is acquired with money is the bought; the twice-wedded's son is of two kinds:

sanskrit_iast:
dattvaikasya ca yā kanyā hṛtvānyasya pradīyate /
tajjālastanayo jñeyo loke paunarbhavo mune //
meaning:
दत्त्वैकस्य च या कन्या हृत्वान्यस्य प्रदीयते /
तज्जालस्तनयो ज्ञेयो लोके पौनर्भवो मुने //
text_mt: the maiden who, having been given to one, is taken back and given to another— / a son born of her is to be known in the world as the twice-wedded's son, O sage.

sanskrit_iast:
durbhikṣe vyasane cāpi yenātmā viniveditaḥ /
sa svayandatta ityustathānyaḥ kāraṇāntaraiḥ //
meaning:
दुर्भिक्षे व्यसने चापि येनात्मा विनिवेदितः /
स स्वयन्दत्त इत्युस्तथान्यः कारणान्तरैः //
text_mt: He who has offered himself during a famine or distress / is said to be the self-given; likewise another for other reasons.

sanskrit_iast:
brāhmaṇasya sutaḥ śūdrayāṃ jāyate yastu suvrata /
ūḍhāyāṃ vāpyanūḍhāyāṃ sa pāraśava ucyate //
meaning:
ब्राह्मणस्य सुतः शूद्रयां जायते यस्तु सुव्रत /
ऊढायां वाप्यनूढायां स पारशव उच्यते //
text_mt: A Brahmin's son who is born of a Śūdra woman, O one of good vows, / whether married or unmarried, is called a Pāraśava.

sanskrit_iast:
etasmāt kāraṇāt putra na svayaṃ dātumarhasi /
svamātmānaṃ gaccha śīghraṃ pitarau samupāhvaya //
meaning:
एतस्मात् कारणात् पुत्र न स्वयं दातुमर्हसि /
स्वमात्मानं गच्छ शीघ्रं पितरौ समुपाह्वय //
text_mt: For this reason, O son, you ought not give yourself / of your own accord; go quickly and summon your parents.'

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥsa mātāpitarau sasmāra vacanād vibhoḥ /
tāvājagmaturīśānaṃ draṣṭuṃ vai dampatī mune //
meaning:
ततःस मातापितरौ सस्मार वचनाद् विभोः /
तावाजग्मतुरीशानं द्रष्टुं वै दम्पती मुने //
text_mt: Then, at the word of the Lord, he remembered his mother and father; / the couple came to see the Lord, O sage.

sanskrit_iast:
dharmo 'hiṃsā ca deveśaṃ praṇipatya nyaṣīdatām /
upaviṣṭau sukhāsīnau sādhyo vacanamabravīt //
meaning:
धर्मो ऽहिंसा च देवेशं प्रणिपत्य न्यषीदताम् /
उपविष्टौ सुखासीनौ साध्यो वचनमब्रवीत् //
text_mt: Dharma and Ahiṃsā bowed down to the Lord of gods and sat down; / as they were seated comfortably, the Sādhya spoke these words:

sanskrit_iast:
sanatkumāra uvāca /
yogaṃ jigamiṣustāta vrahmāṇaṃ samacūcudam /
sa coktavān māṃ putrārthe tasmāt tvaṃ dātumarhasi //
meaning:
सनत्कुमार उवाच /
योगं जिगमिषुस्तात व्रह्माणं समचूचुदम् /
स चोक्तवान् मां पुत्रार्थे तस्मात् त्वं दातुमर्हसि //
text_mt: Sanatkumāra said: / 'Father, wishing to attain yoga, I urged Brahmā; / and he told me [to ask] for a son; therefore you should give me.'

sanskrit_iast:
tāvevamuktau putreṇa yogācāryaṃ pitāmaham /
uktavantau prabho 'yaṃ hi āvayostanayastava //
meaning:
तावेवमुक्तौ पुत्रेण योगाचार्यं पितामहम् /
उक्तवन्तौ प्रभो ऽयं हि आवयोस्तनयस्तव //
text_mt: Being addressed thus by their son, the two said to the Grandfather, the teacher of yoga: / 'O Lord, this son of ours is yours.

sanskrit_iast:
adyaprabhṛtyayaṃ putrastava brahman bhaviṣyati /
ityuktvā jagmatursūrṇa yenaivābyāgatau yathā //
meaning:
अद्यप्रभृत्ययं पुत्रस्तव ब्रह्मन् भविष्यति /
इत्युक्त्वा जग्मतुर्सूर्ण येनैवाब्यागतौ यथा //
text_mt: From today onward, O Brahman, this one will be your son.' / Having spoken thus, they quickly went away by the path they had come.

sanskrit_iast:
pitāmaho 'pi taṃ putraṃ sādhyaṃ saddhinayānvitam /
sanatkumāraṃ provāca yogaṃ dvādaśapatrakam //
meaning:
पितामहो ऽपि तं पुत्रं साध्यं सद्धिनयान्वितम् /
सनत्कुमारं प्रोवाच योगं द्वादशपत्रकम् //
text_mt: The Grandfather then taught that son, the Sādhya endowed with true humility, / Sanatkumāra, the twelve-petaled yoga:

sanskrit_iast:
śikhāsaṃśthaṃ tu oṅkāraṃ meṣo 'sya śirasi sthitaḥ /
māso vaiśākhanāmā ca prathamaṃ patrakaṃ smṛtam //
meaning:
शिखासंश्थं तु ओङ्कारं मेषो ऽस्य शिरसि स्थितः /
मासो वैशाखनामा च प्रथमं पत्रकं स्मृतम् //
text_mt: The syllable 'Oṃ' resides in the crest, Aries is situated on his head, / and the month named Vaiśākha is remembered as the first petal.

sanskrit_iast:
nakāro mukhasaṃstho hi vṛṣastatra prakīrtitaḥ /
jyeṣṭhamāsāśca tatpatraṃ dvitīyaṃ parikīrtitam //
meaning:
नकारो मुखसंस्थो हि वृषस्तत्र प्रकीर्तितः /
ज्येष्ठमासाश्च तत्पत्रं द्वितीयं परिकीर्तितम् //
text_mt: The syllable 'Na' resides in the mouth, Taurus is proclaimed to be there, / and the month of Jyeṣṭha is proclaimed as the second petal.

sanskrit_iast:
mokāro bhujayoryugmaṃ mithunastatra saṃsthitaḥ /
māso āṣāḍhanāmā ca tṛtīyaṃ patrakaṃ smṛtam //
meaning:
मोकारो भुजयोर्युग्मं मिथुनस्तत्र संस्थितः /
मासो आषाढनामा च तृतीयं पत्रकं स्मृतम् //
text_mt: The syllable 'Mo' is the pair of arms, Gemini resides there, / and the month named Āṣāḍha is remembered as the third petal.

sanskrit_iast:
bhakāraṃ netrayugalaṃ tatra karkaṭakaḥ sthitaḥ /
māsaḥ śrāvaṇa ityuktaścaturthaṃ patrakaṃ smṛtam //
meaning:
भकारं नेत्रयुगलं तत्र कर्कटकः स्थितः /
मासः श्रावण इत्युक्तश्चतुर्थं पत्रकं स्मृतम् //
text_mt: The syllable 'Bha' is the pair of eyes, Cancer resides there, / the month is said to be Śrāvaṇa, remembered as the fourth petal.

sanskrit_iast:
gakāraṃ hṛdayaṃ proktaṃ siṃho vasati tatra ca /
māso bhādrastathā proktaḥ pañcamaṃ patrakaṃ smṛtam //
meaning:
गकारं हृदयं प्रोक्तं सिंहो वसति तत्र च /
मासो भाद्रस्तथा प्रोक्तः पञ्चमं पत्रकं स्मृतम् //
text_mt: The syllable 'Ga' is declared to be the heart, and Leo dwells there, / and the month is declared to be Bhādra, remembered as the fifth petal.

sanskrit_iast:
vakāraṃ kavacaṃ vidyāt kanyā tatra pratiṣiṭhatā /
māsaścāśvayujo nāma ṣṣṭhaṃ tat patrakaṃ smṛtam //
meaning:
वकारं कवचं विद्यात् कन्या तत्र प्रतिषिठता /
मासश्चाश्वयुजो नाम ष्ष्ठं तत् पत्रकं स्मृतम् //
text_mt: One should know the syllable 'Va' as the armor, Virgo is situated there, / and the month named Āśvayuja is remembered as that sixth petal.

sanskrit_iast:
tekāramastragrāmaṃ ca tulārāśiḥ kṛtāśrayaḥ /
māsaśca kārtiko nāma saptamaṃ patrakaṃ smṛtam //
meaning:
तेकारमस्त्रग्रामं च तुलाराशिः कृताश्रयः /
मासश्च कार्तिको नाम सप्तमं पत्रकं स्मृतम् //
text_mt: The syllable 'Te' is the array of weapons, the sign Libra takes its abode there, / and the month named Kārtika is remembered as the seventh petal.

sanskrit_iast:
vākāraṃ nābhisaṃyuktaṃ sthitastatra tu vṛścikaḥ /
māso mārgaśiro nāma tvaṣṭamaṃ patrakaṃ smṛtam //
meaning:
वाकारं नाभिसंयुक्तं स्थितस्तत्र तु वृश्चिकः /
मासो मार्गशिरो नाम त्वष्टमं पत्रकं स्मृतम् //
text_mt: The syllable 'Vā' is joined with the navel, Scorpio resides there, / and the month named Mārgaśira is remembered as the eighth petal.

sanskrit_iast:
sukāraṃ jaghanaṃ proktaṃ tatrasthaśca dhanurdharaḥ /
pauṣati gadito māso navamaṃ parikīrtitam //
meaning:
सुकारं जघनं प्रोक्तं तत्रस्थश्च धनुर्धरः /
पौषति गदितो मासो नवमं परिकीर्तितम् //
text_mt: The syllable 'Su' is declared to be the hips, and Sagittarius resides there, / the month is declared to be Pauṣa, proclaimed as the ninth.

sanskrit_iast:
dekāraścoruyugalaṃ makaro 'pyatra saṃsthitaḥ /
māgho nigadito māsaḥ patrakaṃ daśamaṃ smṛtam //
meaning:
देकारश्चोरुयुगलं मकरो ऽप्यत्र संस्थितः /
माघो निगदितो मासः पत्रकं दशमं स्मृतम् //
text_mt: The syllable 'de' is the pair of thighs, and Capricorn is stationed there; / the month is declared to be Māgha, and it is traditionally known as the tenth petal.

sanskrit_iast:
vākāro januyugmaṃ ca kumbhastatrādisaṃsthitaḥ /
patrakaṃ phālgunaṃ proktaṃ tadekādaśamuttamam //
meaning:
वाकारो जनुयुग्मं च कुम्भस्तत्रादिसंस्थितः /
पत्रकं फाल्गुनं प्रोक्तं तदेकादशमुत्तमम् //
text_mt: The syllable 'vā' is the pair of knees, and Aquarius is situated there from the beginning; / the month is said to be Phālguna, and that is the excellent eleventh petal.

sanskrit_iast:
pādau yakāro mīno 'pi sa caitre vasate mune /
idaṃ dvādaśamaṃ proktaṃ patraṃ vai keśavasya hi //
meaning:
पादौ यकारो मीनो ऽपि स चैत्रे वसते मुने /
इदं द्वादशमं प्रोक्तं पत्रं वै केशवस्य हि //
text_mt: The syllable 'ya' is the two feet, and Pisces resides in Caitra, O sage; / this is indeed declared to be the twelfth petal of Keśava.

sanskrit_iast:
dvādaśāraṃ tathā cakraṃ ṣaṣṇābhi dviyutaṃ tathā /
trivyūhamekamūrtiśca tathoktaḥ parameśvaraḥ //
meaning:
द्वादशारं तथा चक्रं षष्णाभि द्वियुतं तथा /
त्रिव्यूहमेकमूर्तिश्च तथोक्तः परमेश्वरः //
text_mt: Likewise, the wheel has twelve spokes and six navels, along with the two; / and the Supreme Lord is thus spoken of as having three manifestations and a single form.

sanskrit_iast:
etat tavoktaṃ devasya rūpaṃ dvādaśapatrakam /
yasmin jñāte muniśreṣṭha na bhūyo maraṇaṃ bhavet //
meaning:
एतत् तवोक्तं देवस्य रूपं द्वादशपत्रकम् /
यस्मिन् ज्ञाते मुनिश्रेष्ठ न भूयो मरणं भवेत् //
text_mt: This twelve-petaled form of the Lord has been described to you; / once it is known, O best of sages, there is no death again.

sanskrit_iast:
dvitīyamuktaṃ sattvāḍhyaṃ caturvarṇaṃ caturmukham /
caturbāhumudārāṅgaṃ śrīvatsadharamavyayam //
meaning:
द्वितीयमुक्तं सत्त्वाढ्यं चतुर्वर्णं चतुर्मुखम् /
चतुर्बाहुमुदाराङ्गं श्रीवत्सधरमव्ययम् //
text_mt: The second [form] is said to abound in sattva, possessing four colors, four faces, / four arms, noble limbs, bearing the śrīvatsa mark, and imperishable.

sanskrit_iast:
tṛtīyastamaso māma śeṣamūrtiḥ sahasrapāt /
sahasravadanaḥ śrīmān prajāpralayakārakaḥ //
meaning:
तृतीयस्तमसो माम शेषमूर्तिः सहस्रपात् /
सहस्रवदनः श्रीमान् प्रजाप्रलयकारकः //
text_mt: The third form is of tamas, the form of Śeṣa with a thousand feet, / a thousand faces, glorious, the causer of the dissolution of creatures.

sanskrit_iast:
caturtho rājaso nāma raktavarṇaścaturmukhaḥ /
dvibhujo dhārayan mālaṃ sṛṣṭikṛccādipūruṣaḥ //
meaning:
चतुर्थो राजसो नाम रक्तवर्णश्चतुर्मुखः /
द्विभुजो धारयन् मालं सृष्टिकृच्चादिपूरुषः //
text_mt: The fourth is named rājasa, red in color, four-faced, / two-armed, holding a garland, the creator of the world, and the primeval person.

sanskrit_iast:
avyāktāt mabhavantyete trayo vyaktā mahāmune /
ato marīcipramukhāstathānye 'pi sahasraśaḥ //
meaning:
अव्याक्तात् मभवन्त्येते त्रयो व्यक्ता महामुने /
अतो मरीचिप्रमुखास्तथान्ये ऽपि सहस्रशः //
text_mt: From the Unmanifest these three manifest forms arise, O great sage; / from this also come Marīci and the foremost [sages], as well as thousands of others.

sanskrit_iast:
etat tavoktaṃ munivarya rūpaṃ vibhoḥ purāṇaṃ matipuṣṭivardhanam /
cuturbhujaṃ taṃ sa mururdurātmā kṛtāntavākyāt punarāsasāda //
meaning:
एतत् तवोक्तं मुनिवर्य रूपं विभोः पुराणं मतिपुष्टिवर्धनम् /
चुतुर्भुजं तं स मुरुर्दुरात्मा कृतान्तवाक्यात् पुनराससाद //
text_mt: This ancient form of the omnipresent Lord, which increases the vigor of intellect, has been told to you, O best of sages; / and that wicked Mura, following the words of Death, approached that four-armed Lord again.

sanskrit_iast:
tamāgataṃ prāha mune madhughnaḥ prāpto 'si kenāsura kāraṇena /
sa prāha yoddhuṃ saha vai tvayādya taṃ prāha bhūyaḥ suraśatruhantā //
yadīha māṃ yoddhumupāgato 'si tat kampeta te hṛdayaṃ kimartham /
jvarāturasyeva muhurmuhurvai tannāsmi yotsye saha kātareṇa / /
meaning:
तमागतं प्राह मुने मधुघ्नः प्राप्तो ऽसि केनासुर कारणेन /
स प्राह योद्धुं सह वै त्वयाद्य तं प्राह भूयः सुरशत्रुहन्ता //
यदीह मां योद्धुमुपागतो ऽसि तत् कम्पेत ते हृदयं किमर्थम् /
ज्वरातुरस्येव मुहुर्मुहुर्वै तन्नास्मि योत्स्ये सह कातरेण / /
text_mt:
When he arrived, the slayer of Madhu said to him, 'For what purpose have you come, O asura?' / He replied, 'Indeed to fight with you today.' Then the slayer of the enemies of the gods spoke to him again:

'If you have come here to fight me, why then should your heart tremble
again and again like that of one stricken with fever? Therefore I shall not fight with a coward.'

sanskrit_iast:
35.74 ityevamukto madhusūdanena murustadā sve hṛdaye svahastam /
kathaṃ kva kasyeti muhustathoktvā nipātayāmāsa vipannabuddhiḥ //
meaning:
35.74 इत्येवमुक्तो मधुसूदनेन मुरुस्तदा स्वे हृदये स्वहस्तम् /
कथं क्व कस्येति मुहुस्तथोक्त्वा निपातयामास विपन्नबुद्धिः //
text_mt:
Addressed thus by Madhusūdana, Mura then placed his hand upon his own heart,
and repeatedly saying, 'How? Where? Whose?', his mind perplexed, he let it fall.

sanskrit_iast:
hariśca cakraṃ mṛdulāghavena mumoca taddhatakamalasya śatroḥ /
ciccheda devāstu gatavyathābhavan devaṃ prasaṃsanti ca padmanābham //
meaning:
हरिश्च चक्रं मृदुलाघवेन मुमोच तद्धतकमलस्य शत्रोः /
चिच्छेद देवास्तु गतव्यथाभवन् देवं प्रसंसन्ति च पद्मनाभम् //
text_mt: And Hari released his discus with gentle swiftness against the heart of that wretch of an enemy; / he severed it, and the gods became free from distress and praised the lotus-navel god.

sanskrit_iast:
etat tavoktaṃ muradaityanāśanaṃ kṛtaṃ hi yuktyā śitacakrapāṇinā /
ataḥ prasiddhiṃ samupājagāma murārirityeva vibhurnṛsiṃhaḥ //
iti śrīvāmanapurāṇe pañcatriṃśo
meaning:
एतत् तवोक्तं मुरदैत्यनाशनं कृतं हि युक्त्या शितचक्रपाणिना /
अतः प्रसिद्धिं समुपाजगाम मुरारिरित्येव विभुर्नृसिंहः //
इति श्रीवामनपुराणे पञ्चत्रिंशो
text_mt:
This destruction of the daitya Mura, accomplished indeed by stratagem by the one with the sharp discus in his hand, has been related to you; / therefore the omnipresent Lord Nṛsiṃha attained fame by the very name Murāri.

Thus [ends] the thirty-fifth [chapter] in the glorious Vāmana Purāṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
pulastya uvāca /
tato murāribhavanaṃ samabhyetya surāstataḥ /
ūcurdevaṃ namaskṛtya jagatsaṃkṣubdhikāraṇam //
meaning:
पुलस्त्य उवाच /
ततो मुरारिभवनं समभ्येत्य सुरास्ततः /
ऊचुर्देवं नमस्कृत्य जगत्संक्षुब्धिकारणम् //
text_mt: Pulastya said: / Then the gods, having approached the abode of Murāri, / bowed down to the god and spoke of the cause of the agitation of the world.

sanskrit_iast:
tacchrutvā bhagavān prāha gacchāmo haramandiram /
sa tavtsyati mahājñānī jagatkṣubdhaṃ caracaram //
meaning:
तच्छ्रुत्वा भगवान् प्राह गच्छामो हरमन्दिरम् /
स तव्त्स्यति महाज्ञानी जगत्क्षुब्धं चरचरम् //
text_mt: Hearing that, the Blessed Lord said, 'Let us go to the abode of Hara; / he, possessing great knowledge, will pacify the agitated world, moving and unmoving.'

sanskrit_iast:
tayoktā vāsudevenana devāḥ śakrapurogamāḥ /
janārdanaṃ puraskṛtya prajāgmurmandaraṃ girim /
na tatra devaṃ na vṛṣaṃ na devīṃ na ca nandinam //
meaning:
तयोक्ता वासुदेवेनन देवाः शक्रपुरोगमाः /
जनार्दनं पुरस्कृत्य प्रजाग्मुर्मन्दरं गिरिम् /
न तत्र देवं न वृषं न देवीं न च नन्दिनम् //
text_mt: Addressed thus by Vāsudeva, the gods, led by Indra, / went to Mount Mandara, placing Janārdana at their head; / [but] they saw neither the god nor the bull nor the goddess nor Nandin there.

sanskrit_iast:
śūnyaṃ girimapaśyanta ajñānatimirāvṛtāḥ /
tān mūḍhadṛṣṭīn saṃprokṣya devān viṣṇurmahādyutiḥ //
meaning:
शून्यं गिरिमपश्यन्त अज्ञानतिमिरावृताः /
तान् मूढदृष्टीन् संप्रोक्ष्य देवान् विष्णुर्महाद्युतिः //
text_mt: Covered by the darkness of ignorance, they saw the mountain empty; / beholding those gods whose vision was bewildered, Viṣṇu of great splendor

sanskrit_iast:
provāca kiṃ na paśyadhvaṃ maheśaṃ purataḥ sthitam /
tamūcurnaiva deveśaṃ paśyāmo girijāpatim //
meaning:
प्रोवाच किं न पश्यध्वं महेशं पुरतः स्थितम् /
तमूचुर्नैव देवेशं पश्यामो गिरिजापतिम् //
text_mt: spoke, 'Why do you not see Maheśa standing before you?' / They said to him, 'We do not see the lord of gods, the husband of Girijā, at all.

sanskrit_iast:
na vidmaḥ kāraṇaṃ tacca yena dṛṣṭirhatā hi naḥ /
tānuvāca jaganmūrtiryūyaṃ devasya sāgasaḥ //
meaning:
न विद्मः कारणं तच्च येन दृष्टिर्हता हि नः /
तानुवाच जगन्मूर्तिर्यूयं देवस्य सागसः //
text_mt: Nor do we know that reason whereby our sight has indeed been destroyed.' / The embodiment of the universe said to them, 'You have committed a transgression against the god,

sanskrit_iast:
pāpiṣṭhā garbhahantāro mṛḍānyāḥ svārthatatparāḥ /
tena jñānaviveko vai hṛto devevana śūlinā //
meaning:
पापिष्ठा गर्भहन्तारो मृडान्याः स्वार्थतत्पराः /
तेन ज्ञानविवेको वै हृतो देवेवन शूलिना //
text_mt: being sinful, slayers of Mṛḍānī's embryo, intent only on your own selfish ends; / therefore wisdom and discrimination have been taken away by the spear-bearing god,

sanskrit_iast:
yenāgrataḥ sthitamapi paśyanto 'pi na paśyatha /
tasmāt kāyaviśuddhyarthaṃ devadṛṣṭyarthamādarāt //
meaning:
येनाग्रतः स्थितमपि पश्यन्तो ऽपि न पश्यथ /
तस्मात् कायविशुद्ध्यर्थं देवदृष्ट्यर्थमादरात् //
text_mt: because of which, even though looking, you do not see him standing right in front of you. / Therefore, for the purification of your bodies and to see the god, with devotion

sanskrit_iast:
taptakṛcchrema saṃśuddhāḥ kurudhvaṃ snānamīśvare /
kṣīrasnāne prayuñjīta sārddha kumbhaśataṃ surāḥ //
meaning:
तप्तकृच्छ्रेम संशुद्धाः कुरुध्वं स्नानमीश्वरे /
क्षीरस्नाने प्रयुञ्जीत सार्द्ध कुम्भशतं सुराः //
text_mt: purified by the taptakṛcchra penance, perform a bath for the Lord. / In the milk-bath, one should employ a hundred and fifty jars, O gods;

sanskrit_iast:
dadhisnāne cutaḥṣaṣṭirdvātriṃśaddhaviṣor'haṇe /
pañcagavyasya śuddhasya kumbhāḥ ṣoḍaśa kīrtitāḥ //
meaning:
दधिस्नाने चुतःषष्टिर्द्वात्रिंशद्धविषोर्ऽहणे /
पञ्चगव्यस्य शुद्धस्य कुम्भाः षोडश कीर्तिताः //
text_mt: in the curd-bath, sixty-four; thirty-two in the offering of clarified butter; / sixteen jars of pure pañcagavya are prescribed;

sanskrit_iast:
maduno 'ṣṭau jalasyoktāḥ sarve te dviguṇāḥ surāḥ /
tato rocanayā devamaṣṭottaraśatena hi //
meaning:
मदुनो ऽष्टौ जलस्योक्ताः सर्वे ते द्विगुणाः सुराः /
ततो रोचनया देवमष्टोत्तरशतेन हि //
text_mt: eight of honey, and double all of those are prescribed of water, O gods. / Then, with rocanā and a hundred and eight [recitations], for the god,

sanskrit_iast:
anulimpet kuṅkumena candanena ca bhaktitaḥ /
bilvapatraiḥ sakamalaiḥ dhattūrasuracandanaiḥ //
meaning:
अनुलिम्पेत् कुङ्कुमेन चन्दनेन च भक्तितः /
बिल्वपत्रैः सकमलैः धत्तूरसुरचन्दनैः //
text_mt: one should anoint [him] with saffron and sandalwood paste with devotion; / with bilva leaves and lotuses, dhattūra, and divine sandalwood,

sanskrit_iast:
mandāraiḥ pārijātaiśca atimuktaistathār'cayet /
aguruṃ saha kāleyaṃ candanenāpi dhūpayet //
meaning:
मन्दारैः पारिजातैश्च अतिमुक्तैस्तथार्ऽचयेत् /
अगुरुं सह कालेयं चन्दनेनापि धूपयेत् //
text_mt: with mandāras, pārijātas, and likewise atimuktas, one should worship; / one should incense [him] with agallochum along with kāleya and sandalwood.

sanskrit_iast:
japtavyaṃ śatarūdrīyaṃ ṛgvedoktaiḥ padakramaiḥ /
evaṃ kṛte tu deveśaṃ paśyadhvaṃ netareṇa ca //
meaning:
जप्तव्यं शतरूद्रीयं ऋग्वेदोक्तैः पदक्रमैः /
एवं कृते तु देवेशं पश्यध्वं नेतरेण च //
text_mt: The Śatarudrīya hymn is to be muttered with the word-sequences prescribed in the Ṛgveda; / when this is done, you will see the lord of the gods, and by no other means.'

sanskrit_iast:
ityuktā vāsudevena devāḥ keśavamabruvan /
vidhānaṃ taptakṛcchrasya kathyatāṃ madhusūdana /
yasmiścirṇe kāyaśuddhirbhavate sārvakālikī //
meaning:
इत्युक्ता वासुदेवेन देवाः केशवमब्रुवन् /
विधानं तप्तकृच्छ्रस्य कथ्यतां मधुसूदन /
यस्मिश्चिर्णे कायशुद्धिर्भवते सार्वकालिकी //
text_mt: Addressed thus by Vāsudeva, the gods said to Keśava: / 'Let the rite of the taptakṛcchra be told, O Madhusūdana, / by performing which permanent bodily purification takes place.'

sanskrit_iast:
vāsudeva uvāca /
tryahamuṣṇaṃ pibedāpaḥ tryahamuṣṇaṃ payaḥ pivet /
tryahamuṣṇaṃ pibetsarpirvāyubhakṣo dinatrayam //
meaning:
वासुदेव उवाच /
त्र्यहमुष्णं पिबेदापः त्र्यहमुष्णं पयः पिवेत् /
त्र्यहमुष्णं पिबेत्सर्पिर्वायुभक्षो दिनत्रयम् //
text_mt: Vāsudeva said: / 'For three days one should drink hot water; for three days one should drink hot milk; / for three days one should drink hot clarified butter; and consume only air for three days.

sanskrit_iast:
palā dvādaśa toyasya palāṣṭau payasaḥ surāḥ /
ṣaṭpalaṃ sarpiṣaḥ proktaṃ divase divase pibet //
meaning:
पला द्वादश तोयस्य पलाष्टौ पयसः सुराः /
षट्पलं सर्पिषः प्रोक्तं दिवसे दिवसे पिबेत् //
text_mt: Twelve palas of water, eight palas of milk, O gods, / and six palas of clarified butter are prescribed to be drunk day by day.'

sanskrit_iast:
pulastya uvāca /
ityevamukte vacane surāḥ kāyaviśuddhaye /
taptakṛcchrarahasyaṃ vai cakruḥ śakrapurogamāḥ //
meaning:
पुलस्त्य उवाच /
इत्येवमुक्ते वचने सुराः कायविशुद्धये /
तप्तकृच्छ्ररहस्यं वै चक्रुः शक्रपुरोगमाः //
text_mt: Pulastya said: / When these words had thus been spoken, the gods, led by Indra, / performed the esoteric rite of taptakṛcchra for the purification of their bodies.

sanskrit_iast:
tato vrate surāścīrṇe vimuktāḥ pāpato 'bhavan /
vimuktapāpā deveśaṃ vāsudevamathābruvan //
meaning:
ततो व्रते सुराश्चीर्णे विमुक्ताः पापतो ऽभवन् /
विमुक्तपापा देवेशं वासुदेवमथाब्रुवन् //
text_mt: Then, having observed the rite, the gods became freed from sin; / freed from sin, they then spoke to Vāsudeva, the lord of gods:

sanskrit_iast:
kvāsau vada jagannātha śaṃbhustiṣṭhati keśava /
yaṃ kṣīrādyabhiṣekeṇa snāpayāmo vidhānataḥ //
meaning:
क्वासौ वद जगन्नाथ शंभुस्तिष्ठति केशव /
यं क्षीराद्यभिषेकेण स्नापयामो विधानतः //
text_mt: 'Tell us, O Lord of the World, O Keśava, where does that Śambhu abide, / whom we may bathe with milk and other [substances] according to the injunction?'

sanskrit_iast:
athovāca surānviṣṇureva tiṣṭhati śaṅkaraḥ /
maddehe kiṃ na paśyadhvaṃ yogāścāyaṃ pratiṣṭhitaḥ //
meaning:
अथोवाच सुरान्विष्णुरेव तिष्ठति शङ्करः /
मद्देहे किं न पश्यध्वं योगाश्चायं प्रतिष्ठितः //
text_mt: Then Viṣṇu said to the gods, 'Śaṅkara abides right here; / do you not see him established in my body, a master of yoga?'

sanskrit_iast:
tamūcurnaiva paśyāmastvatto vai tripurāntakam /
satyaṃ vada sureśāna maheśānaḥ kva tiṣṭhati //
meaning:
तमूचुर्नैव पश्यामस्त्वत्तो वै त्रिपुरान्तकम् /
सत्यं वद सुरेशान महेशानः क्व तिष्ठति //
text_mt: They said to him, 'We do not see the destroyer of Tripura in you at all; / speak the truth, O lord of gods, where does Maheśāna abide?'

sanskrit_iast:
tato 'vyayātmā sa hariḥ svahṛtpaṅkajaśāyinam /
darśayāmāsa devānāṃ murārirliṅgamaiśvaram //
meaning:
ततो ऽव्ययात्मा स हरिः स्वहृत्पङ्कजशायिनम् /
दर्शयामास देवानां मुरारिर्लिङ्गमैश्वरम् //
text_mt: Then that imperishable Hari, Murāri, revealed to the gods / the divine liṅga resting in the lotus of his own heart.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ surāḥ krameṇaiva kṣīrādibhiranantaram /
snāpayāñcakrire liṅgaṃ śāśvataṃ dhruvamavyayam //
meaning:
ततः सुराः क्रमेणैव क्षीरादिभिरनन्तरम् /
स्नापयाञ्चक्रिरे लिङ्गं शाश्वतं ध्रुवमव्ययम् //
text_mt: Then the gods subsequently bathed the eternal, steadfast, imperishable liṅga / in due order with milk and the other [substances].

sanskrit_iast:
gorocanayā tvālipya candanena sugandhinā /
bilvapatrāmbujairdevaṃ pūjayāmāsurañjasā //
meaning:
गोरोचनया त्वालिप्य चन्दनेन सुगन्धिना /
बिल्वपत्राम्बुजैर्देवं पूजयामासुरञ्जसा //
text_mt: Having anointed the god with gorocanā and fragrant sandalwood, / they worshipped him straightway with bilva leaves and lotuses.

sanskrit_iast:
pradhūpyāguruṇā bhaktyā nivedya paramaiṣadhīḥ /
japtvāṣṭaśatanāmānaṃ praṇāmaṃ cakrire tataḥ //
meaning:
प्रधूप्यागुरुणा भक्त्या निवेद्य परमैषधीः /
जप्त्वाष्टशतनामानं प्रणामं चक्रिरे ततः //
text_mt: Having fumigated him with agallochum with devotion and offered supreme medicinal herbs, / and having muttered the eight-hundred names, they then bowed down.

sanskrit_iast:
ityevaṃ cintayantaśca devāvetau harīśvarau /
kathaṃ yogatvamāpannau sattvāndhatamasodbhavau //
meaning:
इत्येवं चिन्तयन्तश्च देवावेतौ हरीश्वरौ /
कथं योगत्वमापन्नौ सत्त्वान्धतमसोद्भवौ //
text_mt: And as they were reflecting thus: 'How have these two gods, Hari and Īśvara, / born from sattva and blind darkness, attained oneness?'—

sanskrit_iast:
surāṇāṃ cintitaṃ jñātvā viśvamūrtibhūdvibhuḥ /
sarvalakṣaṇasaṃyuktaḥ sarvāyudhadharo 'vyayaḥ //
meaning:
सुराणां चिन्तितं ज्ञात्वा विश्वमूर्तिभूद्विभुः /
सर्वलक्षणसंयुक्तः सर्वायुधधरो ऽव्ययः //
text_mt: Knowing what the gods were thinking, the omnipresent, imperishable Lord, / endowed with all auspicious marks and bearing all weapons, became the universal form.

sanskrit_iast:
sārddhaṃ trinetraṃ kamalāhikuṇḍalaṃ jaṭāguḍākeśakhagarṣabhadhvajam /
samādhavaṃ hārabhujaṅgavakṣasaṃ pītājinācchannakaṭipradeśam //
meaning:
सार्द्धं त्रिनेत्रं कमलाहिकुण्डलं जटागुडाकेशखगर्षभध्वजम् /
समाधवं हारभुजङ्गवक्षसं पीताजिनाच्छन्नकटिप्रदेशम् //
text_mt:
With half three-eyed, with lotus and serpent earrings, with matted hair, curly locks, and the bull and bird standards,
associated with Mādhava, with a necklace and a serpent on the chest, his waist area covered with yellow cloth and a deerskin,

sanskrit_iast:
cakrāsihastaṃ halaśārṅgapāṇiṃ pinākaśūlājagavānvitaṃ ca /
kapardakhaṭvāṅgakapālaghaṇṭāsaśaṅkhaṭaṅkāraravaṃ maharṣe //
meaning:
चक्रासिहस्तं हलशार्ङ्गपाणिं पिनाकशूलाजगवान्वितं च /
कपर्दखट्वाङ्गकपालघण्टासशङ्खटङ्काररवं महर्षे //
text_mt:
holding a discus and sword in hand, holding a plough and the Śārṅga bow, equipped with the Pināka bow, trident, and Ajagava bow,
with matted hair, a skull-topped staff, skull, and bell, accompanied by the clanging sound of a conch, O great sage.

sanskrit_iast:
dṛṣṭvaiva devā hariśaṅkaraṃ taṃ namo 'stu te sarvagatāvyayeti /
proktvā praṇāmaṃ kamalāsanādyāścakrurmatiṃ caikatarāṃ niyujya //
meaning:
दृष्ट्वैव देवा हरिशङ्करं तं नमो ऽस्तु ते सर्वगताव्ययेति /
प्रोक्त्वा प्रणामं कमलासनाद्याश्चक्रुर्मतिं चैकतरां नियुज्य //
text_mt:
Upon merely seeing that Hari-Śaṅkara, the gods, beginning with the lotus-seated Brahmā,
said, "Praise be to you, omnipresent, imperishable one," and making obeisance, united their minds into one.

sanskrit_iast:
tānekacittān vijñāya devān devapatirhariḥ /
pragṛhyābhyadravattūrṇaṃ kurukṣetraṃ svamāśramama //
meaning:
तानेकचित्तान् विज्ञाय देवान् देवपतिर्हरिः /
प्रगृह्याभ्यद्रवत्तूर्णं कुरुक्षेत्रं स्वमाश्रमम //
text_mt:
Knowing the gods to be single-minded, Hari, the lord of gods,
went quickly, taking them along, to Kurukṣetra, to his own hermitage.

sanskrit_iast:
tato 'paśyanta deveśaṃ sthāṇubhūtaṃ jale śucim /
dṛṣṭvānamaḥ sthāṇaveti proktvā sarvehyupāviśan //
meaning:
ततो ऽपश्यन्त देवेशं स्थाणुभूतं जले शुचिम् /
दृष्ट्वानमः स्थाणवेति प्रोक्त्वा सर्वेह्युपाविशन् //
text_mt:
Then they saw the pure lord of the gods, standing motionless like a pillar in the water;
seeing him, they said, "Praise to the pillar!" and all sat down.

sanskrit_iast:
tato 'bravīt surapatirehyehi dīyatāṃ varaḥ /
kṣubdhaṃ jagajjagannātha unmajjasva priyātithe //
meaning:
ततो ऽब्रवीत् सुरपतिरेह्येहि दीयतां वरः /
क्षुब्धं जगज्जगन्नाथ उन्मज्जस्व प्रियातिथे //
text_mt:
Then the lord of gods said: "Come, come! Grant a boon!
The world is agitated, O lord of the world! Emerge, O beloved guest!"

sanskrit_iast:
tatastāṃ madhurāṃ vāṇīṃ śuśrāva vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ /
śrutvottasthau ca vaigena sarvavyāpī nirañjanaḥ //
meaning:
ततस्तां मधुरां वाणीं शुश्राव वृषभध्वजः /
श्रुत्वोत्तस्थौ च वैगेन सर्वव्यापी निरञ्जनः //
text_mt:
Then the bull-bannered [god] heard that sweet voice;
having heard it, the all-pervading, unstained one rose up with speed.

sanskrit_iast:
namo 'stu srvadebhyaḥ provāca prahasan haraḥ /
sa cāgataḥ suraiḥ sendraḥ praṇato vinayānvitaiḥ //
meaning:
नमो ऽस्तु स्र्वदेभ्यः प्रोवाच प्रहसन् हरः /
स चागतः सुरैः सेन्द्रः प्रणतो विनयान्वितैः //
text_mt:
Laughing gently, Hara said, "Praise be to all the gods!"
And he approached, bowed to by the humble gods accompanied by Indra.

sanskrit_iast:
tamūcurdevatāḥ sarvastyajyatāṃ śaṅkaradratm /
mahāvrataṃ trayo lokāḥ kṣubdhāstvattesāvṛtāḥ //
meaning:
तमूचुर्देवताः सर्वस्त्यज्यतां शङ्करद्रत्म् /
महाव्रतं त्रयो लोकाः क्षुब्धास्त्वत्तेसावृताः //
text_mt:
All the deities said to him: "O Śaṅkara, quickly abandon
this great observance! The three worlds are agitated, surrounded by your fiery splendour."

sanskrit_iast:
athovāca mahādevo mayā tyakto mahāvrataḥ /
tataḥ surā divaṃ jagmurhṛṣṭāḥ prayatamānasāḥ //
meaning:
अथोवाच महादेवो मया त्यक्तो महाव्रतः /
ततः सुरा दिवं जग्मुर्हृष्टाः प्रयतमानसाः //
text_mt:
Then Mahādeva said: "I have abandoned the great observance."
Thereupon the gods went to heaven, rejoiced and disciplined in mind.

sanskrit_iast:
tato 'pi kampate pṛthvī sābdhidvīpācalā mune /
tato 'bhicintayadrudraḥ kimarthaṃ kṣubhitā mahī //
meaning:
ततो ऽपि कम्पते पृथ्वी साब्धिद्वीपाचला मुने /
ततो ऽभिचिन्तयद्रुद्रः किमर्थं क्षुभिता मही //
text_mt:
Even then, O sage, the earth shook, together with its oceans, islands, and mountains.
Then Rudra pondered: "For what reason is the earth agitated?"

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ paryacaracchūlī kurukṣetraṃ samantataḥ /
dadarśoghavatītīre uśanasaṃ taponidhim //
meaning:
ततः पर्यचरच्छूली कुरुक्षेत्रं समन्ततः /
ददर्शोघवतीतीरे उशनसं तपोनिधिम् //
text_mt:
Then the trident-bearer wandered all around Kurukṣetra;
he saw Uśanas, the treasure of asceticism, on the bank of the Oghavatī.

sanskrit_iast:
tato 'bravītsurapatiḥ kimarthaṃ tapyate tapaḥ /
jagatkṣobhakaraṃ vipra tacchīghraṃ kathyatāṃ mama //
meaning:
ततो ऽब्रवीत्सुरपतिः किमर्थं तप्यते तपः /
जगत्क्षोभकरं विप्र तच्छीघ्रं कथ्यतां मम //
text_mt:
Then the lord of gods said: "Why is this asceticism being performed,
which causes turmoil in the world, O Brahmin? Tell me that quickly."

sanskrit_iast:
uśanā uvāca /
tavārādhanakāmārthaṃ tapyate hi mahattapaḥ /
saṃjīvanīṃ śubhāṃ vidyāṃ jñātumicche trilocana //
meaning:
उशना उवाच /
तवाराधनकामार्थं तप्यते हि महत्तपः /
संजीवनीं शुभां विद्यां ज्ञातुमिच्छे त्रिलोचन //
text_mt:
Uśanas said:
"Indeed, great asceticism is being performed with the desire to worship you.
I wish to know the auspicious Saṃjīvanī lore, O three-eyed one!"

sanskrit_iast:
hara uvāca /
tapasā parituṣṭo 'smi sutaptena tapodhana /
tasmāt saṃjīvanīṃvidyāṃ bhavān jñāsyati tattavattaḥ //
meaning:
हर उवाच /
तपसा परितुष्टो ऽस्मि सुतप्तेन तपोधन /
तस्मात् संजीवनींविद्यां भवान् ज्ञास्यति तत्तवत्तः //
text_mt:
Hara said:
"I am well-pleased by your asceticism, well-performed, O you whose wealth is asceticism!
Therefore you shall know the Saṃjīvanī lore in its true essence."

sanskrit_iast:
varaṃ labdhvā tataḥ śukrastapasaḥ saṃnyavarttata /
tathāpi calate pṛthvī sābdhibhūbhṛnnagāvṛtā //
meaning:
वरं लब्ध्वा ततः शुक्रस्तपसः संन्यवर्त्तत /
तथापि चलते पृथ्वी साब्धिभूभृन्नगावृता //
text_mt:
Then, having obtained the boon, Śukra ceased from his asceticism.
Even so, the earth moved, encompassed by oceans, earth-bearers, and mountains.

sanskrit_iast:
tato 'gamanmahādevaḥ saptasārasvataṃ śuciḥ /
dadarśa nṛtyamānaṃ ca ṛṣiṃ maṅkaṇasaṃjñitam //
meaning:
ततो ऽगमन्महादेवः सप्तसारस्वतं शुचिः /
ददर्श नृत्यमानं च ऋषिं मङ्कणसंज्ञितम् //
text_mt:
Then the pure Mahādeva went to Saptasārasvata;
and he saw the sage named Maṅkaṇa dancing.

sanskrit_iast:
bhāvena poplūyati bālavat sa bhujau prasāryaiva nanartta vegāt /
tasyaiva vegena samāhatā tu cacāla bhūrbhūmidharaiḥ sahaiva //
meaning:
भावेन पोप्लूयति बालवत् स भुजौ प्रसार्यैव ननर्त्त वेगात् /
तस्यैव वेगेन समाहता तु चचाल भूर्भूमिधरैः सहैव //
text_mt:
He kept leaping up like a child out of emotion, stretching out his arms, and danced with speed;
struck by his very momentum, the earth trembled together with the mountains.

sanskrit_iast:
taṃ śaṅgaro 'bhyetya kare nigṛhya provāca vākyaṃ prahasan maharṣe /
kiṃ bhāvito nṛtyasi kena hetunā vadasva māmetya kimatra tuṣṭiḥ //
meaning:
तं शङ्गरो ऽभ्येत्य करे निगृह्य प्रोवाच वाक्यं प्रहसन् महर्षे /
किं भावितो नृत्यसि केन हेतुना वदस्व मामेत्य किमत्र तुष्टिः //
text_mt:
Śaṅkara, approaching him and grasping his hand, spoke these words with a laugh, O great sage:
"Feeling what do you dance? For what reason? Speak to me as I approach: what is the joy here?"

sanskrit_iast:
sa brāhmaṇaḥ prāha mamādya tuṣṭiryeneha jātā śṛṇu tad dvijendra /
bahūn gaṇān vai mama tapyatastapaḥ saṃvatsarān kāyaviśoṣaṇārtham //
meaning:
स ब्राह्मणः प्राह ममाद्य तुष्टिर्येनेह जाता शृणु तद् द्विजेन्द्र /
बहून् गणान् वै मम तप्यतस्तपः संवत्सरान् कायविशोषणार्थम् //
text_mt:
That Brahmin said: "Hear that by which my joy has arisen today, O foremost of the twice-born!
While I was performing asceticism for many hosts of years to desiccate the body,

sanskrit_iast:
tato 'nupaśyāmi karāt kṣatotthaṃ nirgacchate śākarasaṃ mameha /
tenādya tuṣṭo 'smi bhṛśaṃ dvijendra yenāsmi nṛtyāmi subhāvitātmā //
meaning:
ततो ऽनुपश्यामि करात् क्षतोत्थं निर्गच्छते शाकरसं ममेह /
तेनाद्य तुष्टो ऽस्मि भृशं द्विजेन्द्र येनास्मि नृत्यामि सुभावितात्मा //
text_mt:
I then saw vegetable sap issuing here from a wound on my hand.
By that I am greatly pleased today, O foremost of the twice-born, by which I dance, my mind deeply stirred."

sanskrit_iast:
taṃ prāha śaṃbhurdvija paśya mahyaṃ bhasma pravṛtto 'ṅgulito 'tiśuklam /
saṃtāḍanādeva na ca praharṣo mamāsti nṛnaṃ hi bhavān pramattaḥ //
meaning:
तं प्राह शंभुर्द्विज पश्य मह्यं भस्म प्रवृत्तो ऽङ्गुलितो ऽतिशुक्लम् /
संताडनादेव न च प्रहर्षो ममास्ति नृनं हि भवान् प्रमत्तः //
text_mt:
Śambhu said to him: "O twice-born, look at me! From my finger, exceedingly white ashes
flow out merely from striking it, and there is no joy in me; surely you are out of your senses!"

sanskrit_iast:
śrutvātha vākyaṃ vṛṣabhadhvajasya matvā munirmaṅkaṇako maharṣe /
nṛtyaṃ parityajya suvismito 'tha vavanda pādau vinayāvanamraḥ //
meaning:
श्रुत्वाथ वाक्यं वृषभध्वजस्य मत्वा मुनिर्मङ्कणको महर्षे /
नृत्यं परित्यज्य सुविस्मितो ऽथ ववन्द पादौ विनयावनम्रः //
text_mt:
Then, hearing the words of the bull-bannered god, the sage Maṅkaṇaka realized, O great sage,
and abandoning his dance, exceedingly astonished, bowed down at his feet, bent low with modesty.

sanskrit_iast:
tamāha śaṃbhurdvija gaccha lokaṃ taṃ brahmaṇo durgamamavyayasya /
idaṃ ca tīrthaṃ pravaraṃ pṛthivyāṃ pṛthūdakasyāstu samaṃ phalena //
meaning:
तमाह शंभुर्द्विज गच्छ लोकं तं ब्रह्मणो दुर्गममव्ययस्य /
इदं च तीर्थं प्रवरं पृथिव्यां पृथूदकस्यास्तु समं फलेन //
text_mt:
Śambhu said to him: "O twice-born, go to that world of imperishable Brahmā, difficult of access.
And let this tīrtha, the best on earth, be equal in fruit to Pṛthūdaka.

sanskrit_iast:
sāṃnidhyamatraiva surāsurāṇāṃ gandharvavidyādharakinnarāṇām /
sadāstu dharmasya nidhānamagryaṃ sārasvataṃ pāpamalāpahāri //
meaning:
सांनिध्यमत्रैव सुरासुराणां गन्धर्वविद्याधरकिन्नराणाम् /
सदास्तु धर्मस्य निधानमग्र्यं सारस्वतं पापमलापहारि //
text_mt:
Let there always be the presence right here of gods, asuras,
gandharvas, vidyādharas, and kinnaras; let this Sārasvata [tīrtha] be the foremost repository of righteousness, removing the taint of sin.

sanskrit_iast:
suprabhā kāñcānākṣī ca suveṇurvimalodakā /
manoharā caughavatī viśālā ca sarasvatī //
meaning:
सुप्रभा काञ्चानाक्षी च सुवेणुर्विमलोदका /
मनोहरा चौघवती विशाला च सरस्वती //
text_mt:
Suprabhā, Kāñcanākṣī, Suveṇu, Vimalodakā,
Manoharā, Oghavatī, and the wide Sarasvatī—

sanskrit_iast:
etāḥ sapta sarasvatyo nivisiṣyanti nityaśaḥ /
somapālaphalaṃ sarvāḥ prayacchanti supuṇyadāḥ //
meaning:
एताः सप्त सरस्वत्यो निविसिष्यन्ति नित्यशः /
सोमपालफलं सर्वाः प्रयच्छन्ति सुपुण्यदाः //
text_mt:
these seven Sarasvatīs will dwell [here] constantly;
bestowing great merit, they all grant the fruit of the Somapāna.

sanskrit_iast:
bhavānapi kurukṣetre mūrtiṃ sthāpya garīyasīm /
gamiṣyati mahāpuṇyaṃ brahmalokaṃ sudurgamam //
meaning:
भवानपि कुरुक्षेत्रे मूर्तिं स्थाप्य गरीयसीम् /
गमिष्यति महापुण्यं ब्रह्मलोकं सुदुर्गमम् //
text_mt:
You too, having established a weighty image in Kurukṣetra,
will go to the greatly meritorious Brahmaloka, exceedingly difficult to reach."

sanskrit_iast:
ityevamukto devena śaṅkarema tapodhanaḥ /
mūrtti sthāpya kurukṣetre brahmalokamagād vaśī //
meaning:
इत्येवमुक्तो देवेन शङ्करेम तपोधनः /
मूर्त्ति स्थाप्य कुरुक्षेत्रे ब्रह्मलोकमगाद् वशी //
text_mt:
Thus addressed by the god Śaṅkara, the self-controlled ascetic,
having installed an image in Kurukṣetra, went to Brahmaloka.

sanskrit_iast:
gate maṅkaṇake pṛthvī niścalā samajāyata /
athāgānmandaraṃ śaṃbhurnijamāvasathaṃ śuciḥ //
meaning:
गते मङ्कणके पृथ्वी निश्चला समजायत /
अथागान्मन्दरं शंभुर्निजमावसथं शुचिः //
text_mt:
When Maṅkaṇaka had gone, the earth became motionless.
Then the pure Śambhu went to Mandara, his own abode.

sanskrit_iast:
etat tavoktaṃ dvija śaṅkarastu gatastadāsīt tapase 'tha śaile /
śūnye 'bhyagād dṛṣṭamatirhi devyā saṃyodhito yena hi kāraṇena //
iti śrīvāmanapurāṇe ṣaṭtriśodhyāyaḥ
meaning:
एतत् तवोक्तं द्विज शङ्करस्तु गतस्तदासीत् तपसे ऽथ शैले /
शून्ये ऽभ्यगाद् दृष्टमतिर्हि देव्या संयोधितो येन हि कारणेन //
इति श्रीवामनपुराणे षट्त्रिशोध्यायः
text_mt:
This has been told to you, O twice-born: that Śaṅkara then went to the desolate
mountain for asceticism, and arrived with his mind resolved; for which reason he was fought by the goddess.

Thus ends the thirty-sixth chapter in the glorious Vāmana Purāṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
nārāda uvāca /
gato 'ndhakastu pātāle kimaceṣṭata dānavaḥ /
śaṅkaro mandarastho 'pi yaccākāra taducyatām //
meaning:
नाराद उवाच /
गतो ऽन्धकस्तु पाताले किमचेष्टत दानवः /
शङ्करो मन्दरस्थो ऽपि यच्चाकार तदुच्यताम् //
text_mt:
Nārada said:
"When the Dānava Andhaka had gone to Pātāla, what did he do?
And what Śaṅkara did while staying on Mandara, let that be told!"

sanskrit_iast:
pulāstya uvāca /
pātālastho 'ndhako brahman bādhyate madanāgninā /
saṃtpatavigrahaḥ sarvān dānavānidamabravīt //
meaning:
पुलास्त्य उवाच /
पातालस्थो ऽन्धको ब्रह्मन् बाध्यते मदनाग्निना /
संत्पतविग्रहः सर्वान् दानवानिदमब्रवीत् //

sanskrit_iast:
sa me suhṛtsa me bandhuḥ sa bhrāta sa pitā mama /
yastāmadrisutāṃ śīghnaṃ mamānti kamupānayet //
meaning:
स मे सुहृत्स मे बन्धुः स भ्रात स पिता मम /
यस्तामद्रिसुतां शीघ्नं ममान्ति कमुपानयेत् //
text_mt:
'He is my friend, he is my kinsman, he is my brother, he is my father,
who would quickly bring that daughter of the mountain to my presence!'

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ bruvati daityende andhake madanāndhake /
meghagambhīranirghoṣaṃ prahalādo vākyamabravīt //
meaning:
एवं ब्रुवति दैत्येन्दे अन्धके मदनान्धके /
मेघगम्भीरनिर्घोषं प्रहलादो वाक्यमब्रवीत् //
text_mt:
When Andhaka, the lord of the Daityas, blinded by love, spoke thus,
Prahlāda spoke these words with a sound deep as a raincloud:

sanskrit_iast:
yeyaṃ girisutā vīra sā mātā dharmatastava /
pitā trinayano devaḥ śrūyatāmatra kāraṇam //
meaning:
येयं गिरिसुता वीर सा माता धर्मतस्तव /
पिता त्रिनयनो देवः श्रूयतामत्र कारणम् //
text_mt:
'She who is the mountain's daughter, O hero, is by duty your mother;
your father is the three-eyed god. Hear the reason for this!

sanskrit_iast:
tava pitrā hyaputrema dharmanityena dānava /
ārādhito mahādevaḥ putrārthāya purā kila //
meaning:
तव पित्रा ह्यपुत्रेम धर्मनित्येन दानव /
आराधितो महादेवः पुत्रार्थाय पुरा किल //
text_mt:
Formerly indeed, O Dānava, Mahādeva was worshipped for the sake of a son
by your father, who was childless and constantly devoted to dharma.

sanskrit_iast:
tasmai trilocananāsīd datto 'ndho 'pyeva dānava /
putrakaḥ putrakāmāsya proktvetyaṃ vacanaṃ vibho //
meaning:
तस्मै त्रिलोचननासीद् दत्तो ऽन्धो ऽप्येव दानव /
पुत्रकः पुत्रकामास्य प्रोक्त्वेत्यं वचनं विभो //
text_mt:
To him, desiring a son, a blind little boy was given by the three-eyed one,
O Dānava, having spoken these words, O lord:

sanskrit_iast:
netratrayaṃ hiraṇyākṣa narmārthamumayā mama /
pihitaṃ yogasaṃsthasya tato 'ndhamabhavattamaḥ //
meaning:
नेत्रत्रयं हिरण्याक्ष नर्मार्थमुमया मम /
पिहितं योगसंस्थस्य ततो ऽन्धमभवत्तमः //
text_mt:
“O Hiraṇyākṣa, my three eyes were covered by Umā in jest
while I was engaged in yoga, and from that blinding darkness arose.

sanskrit_iast:
tasmācca tamaso jāto bhūto nīlaghanasvanaḥ /
taditaṃ gṛhyatāṃ daitya tavopayikamātmajam //
meaning:
तस्माच्च तमसो जातो भूतो नीलघनस्वनः /
तदितं गृह्यतां दैत्य तवोपयिकमात्मजम् //
text_mt:
And from that darkness a being was born, roaring like a dark cloud.
Therefore, take this suitable son of yours, O Daitya!

sanskrit_iast:
yadā tu lokavidviṣṭaṃ duṣṭaṃ karma kariṣyati /
trailokyajananīṃ cāpi abhīvāñchiṣyate 'dhamaḥ //
meaning:
यदा तु लोकविद्विष्टं दुष्टं कर्म करिष्यति /
त्रैलोक्यजननीं चापि अभीवाञ्छिष्यते ऽधमः //
text_mt:
When, however, he performs wicked deeds hated by the world,
and the base wretch lusts after the mother of the three worlds,

sanskrit_iast:
ghātayiṣyati vā vipraṃ yadā prakṣipta cāsurān /
tadāsya svayamevāhaṃ kariṣye kāyaśodhanam //
meaning:
घातयिष्यति वा विप्रं यदा प्रक्षिप्त चासुरान् /
तदास्य स्वयमेवाहं करिष्ये कायशोधनम् //
text_mt:
or slays a Brahmin, casting down the asuras,
then I myself will purge his body.”

sanskrit_iast:
evamuktvā gataḥ śaṃbhuṃ svasthānaṃ mandarācalam /
tvatpitāpi samabhyāgāt tvāmādāya rasātalam //
meaning:
एवमुक्त्वा गतः शंभुं स्वस्थानं मन्दराचलम् /
त्वत्पितापि समभ्यागात् त्वामादाय रसातलम् //
text_mt:
Having spoken thus, Śambhu departed for his own abode, Mount Mandara;
and your father, taking you with him, also returned to Rasātala.

sanskrit_iast:
etena kāraṇenāmbā śaileyī bhavitā tava /
sarvasyāpīha jagato guruḥ śaṃbhuḥ pitā dhruvam //
meaning:
एतेन कारणेनाम्बा शैलेयी भविता तव /
सर्वस्यापीह जगतो गुरुः शंभुः पिता ध्रुवम् //
text_mt:
For this reason, the daughter of the mountain is your mother;
and Śambhu is truly the father and guru of this entire universe.

sanskrit_iast:
bhavānapi tapoyuktaḥ śāstravettā guṇāplutaḥ /
nedṛśe pāpasaṃkalpe matiṃ kuryād bhavadvidhaḥ //
meaning:
भवानपि तपोयुक्तः शास्त्रवेत्ता गुणाप्लुतः /
नेदृशे पापसंकल्पे मतिं कुर्याद् भवद्विधः //
text_mt:
You too are endowed with austerities, learned in the scriptures, and rich in virtues;
someone like you should not set his mind on such a sinful resolution.

sanskrit_iast:
trailokyaprabhuravyakto bhavaḥ sarvairnamaskṛtaḥ /
ajeyastasya bhāryeyaṃ na tvamarhe 'marārdana //
meaning:
त्रैलोक्यप्रभुरव्यक्तो भवः सर्वैर्नमस्कृतः /
अजेयस्तस्य भार्येयं न त्वमर्हे ऽमरार्दन //
text_mt:
The unmanifest Bhava, lord of the three worlds, is bowed to by all;
he is unconquerable, and she is his wife—you are not worthy [of her], O tormentor of the gods!

sanskrit_iast:
na cāpi śaktaḥ prāptuṃ tāṃ bhavāñśailanṛpātmajām /
ajitvā sagaṇaṃ rudraṃ sa ca kāmo 'dya durlabhaḥ //
meaning:
न चापि शक्तः प्राप्तुं तां भवाञ्शैलनृपात्मजाम् /
अजित्वा सगणं रुद्रं स च कामो ऽद्य दुर्लभः //
text_mt:
Nor are you capable of winning that daughter of the mountain king
without conquering Rudra along with his hosts—and today that desire is unattainable.

sanskrit_iast:
yastaret sāgaraṃ dorbhyā pātayed bhuvi bhāskaram /
merumutpāṭayed vāpi sa jayecchūlapāṇinam //
meaning:
यस्तरेत् सागरं दोर्भ्या पातयेद् भुवि भास्करम् /
मेरुमुत्पाटयेद् वापि स जयेच्छूलपाणिनम् //
text_mt:
One who could cross the ocean with his arms, cast down the sun to earth,
or tear up Mount Meru, might conquer the trident-bearer.

sanskrit_iast:
utāhosvidimāḥ śakyāḥ kriyāḥ kartuṃ narerbalāt /
na ca śakyo haro jetuṃ satyaṃ satyaṃ mayoditam //
meaning:
उताहोस्विदिमाः शक्याः क्रियाः कर्तुं नरेर्बलात् /
न च शक्यो हरो जेतुं सत्यं सत्यं मयोदितम् //
text_mt:
Even if these deeds could be performed by men through force,
Hara cannot be conquered: what I have spoken is the absolute truth.

sanskrit_iast:
kiṃ tvayā na śrutaṃ daitya yathā daṇḍo mahīpaliḥ /
parastrīkāmavān mūḍhaḥ sarāṣṭro nāśamāptavān //
meaning:
किं त्वया न श्रुतं दैत्य यथा दण्डो महीपलिः /
परस्त्रीकामवान् मूढः सराष्ट्रो नाशमाप्तवान् //
text_mt:
Have you not heard, O Daitya, how King Daṇḍa,
a fool lusting for another’s wife, met destruction along with his kingdom?

sanskrit_iast:
āsīd daṇḍo nāma nṛpaḥ prabhūtabalavāhanaḥ /
sa ca vavre mahātejāḥ paurohityāya bhārgavam //
meaning:
आसीद् दण्डो नाम नृपः प्रभूतबलवाहनः /
स च वव्रे महातेजाः पौरोहित्याय भार्गवम् //
text_mt:
There was a king named Daṇḍa of immense forces and mounts;
and that king of great splendor chose Bhārgava as his royal priest.

sanskrit_iast:
īje ca vividhairyajñairnṛpatiḥ śukrapāvalitaḥ /
sukrasyāsīcca duhitā arajā nāma nāmataḥ //
meaning:
ईजे च विविधैर्यज्ञैर्नृपतिः शुक्रपावलितः /
सुक्रस्यासीच्च दुहिता अरजा नाम नामतः //
text_mt:
Protected by Śukra, the king sacrificed with various sacrifices;
and Śukra had a daughter named Arajā.

sanskrit_iast:
śukraḥ kadācidagamad vṛṣuparvāṇamāsuram /
tenārcitaściraṃ tatra tasthau bhārgavasattmaḥ //
meaning:
शुक्रः कदाचिदगमद् वृषुपर्वाणमासुरम् /
तेनार्चितश्चिरं तत्र तस्थौ भार्गवसत्त्मः //
text_mt:
Once Śukra went to the asura Vṛṣaparvan;
worshiped by him, the best of the Bhārgavas stayed there for a long time.

sanskrit_iast:
arajā svagṛhe vahniṃ śuśruṣantī mahāsura /
atiṣṭhata sucārvaṅgī tato 'byāgānnarādhipaḥ //
meaning:
अरजा स्वगृहे वह्निं शुश्रुषन्ती महासुर /
अतिष्ठत सुचार्वङ्गी ततो ऽब्यागान्नराधिपः //
text_mt:
Arajā, beautiful in every limb, stayed in her own home
tending the sacred fire, O great asura; then the king arrived.

sanskrit_iast:
sa papraccha kva śukroti tamūcuḥ paricārikāḥ /
gataḥ sa bhagavān śukro yājanāya danoḥ sutam //
meaning:
स पप्रच्छ क्व शुक्रोति तमूचुः परिचारिकाः /
गतः स भगवान् शुक्रो याजनाय दनोः सुतम् //
text_mt:
He asked, “Where is Śukra?” The maidservants answered him,
“Lord Śukra has gone to conduct a sacrifice for the son of Danu.”

sanskrit_iast:
papraccha nṛpatiḥ kā tu tiṣṭhate bhārgavāśrame /
tāstamūcurguroḥ putrī saṃtiṣṭhatyarajā nṛpa //
meaning:
पप्रच्छ नृपतिः का तु तिष्ठते भार्गवाश्रमे /
तास्तमूचुर्गुरोः पुत्री संतिष्ठत्यरजा नृप //
text_mt:
The king asked, “Who then remains in the hermitage of Bhārgava?”
They answered him, “The guru’s daughter, Arajā, resides [here], O king.”

sanskrit_iast:
tāmāśrame śukrasutāṃ draṣṭumikṣvākunandanaḥ /
praviveśa mahābāhurdadarśārajasaṃ tataḥ //
meaning:
तामाश्रमे शुक्रसुतां द्रष्टुमिक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः /
प्रविवेश महाबाहुर्ददर्शारजसं ततः //
text_mt:
Wishing to see the daughter of Śukra in the hermitage, the descendant of Ikṣvāku,
mighty-armed, entered and then beheld Arajā.

sanskrit_iast:
tāṃ tṛṣṭvā kāmasaṃtaptastatkṣaṇādeva pārthivaḥ /
saṃjāto 'ndhaka daṇḍastu kṛtāntabalacoditaḥ //
meaning:
तां तृष्ट्वा कामसंतप्तस्तत्क्षणादेव पार्थिवः /
संजातो ऽन्धक दण्डस्तु कृतान्तबलचोदितः //
text_mt:
Having seen her, King Daṇḍa was immediately inflamed by desire,
impelled by the force of Death, O Andhaka.

sanskrit_iast:
tato visarjayāmāsa bhṛtyān bhrātṛn suhṛttamān /
śukraśiṣyānapi balī ekākī nṛpa āvrajat //
meaning:
ततो विसर्जयामास भृत्यान् भ्रातृन् सुहृत्तमान् /
शुक्रशिष्यानपि बली एकाकी नृप आव्रजत् //
text_mt:
Then the powerful king dismissed his servants, brothers, dearest friends,
and even Śukra’s disciples, and went forward alone.

sanskrit_iast:
tamāgataṃ śukrasutā pratyutthāya yaśasvinī /
pūjayāmāsa saṃhṛṣṭā bhrātṛbhāvena dānava //
meaning:
तमागतं शुक्रसुता प्रत्युत्थाय यशस्विनी /
पूजयामास संहृष्टा भ्रातृभावेन दानव //
text_mt:
As he arrived, the illustrious daughter of Śukra stood up
and welcomed him joyfully with sisterly affection, O Dānava.

sanskrit_iast:
tatastāmāha nṛpatirbāle kāmāgnivāriṇā /
māṃ samāhlādayasvādya svapariṣvaṅgavāriṇā //
meaning:
ततस्तामाह नृपतिर्बाले कामाग्निवारिणा /
मां समाह्लादयस्वाद्य स्वपरिष्वङ्गवारिणा //
text_mt:
Then the king said to her: “O young girl,
delight me today with the water of your embrace against the fire of love!”

sanskrit_iast:
sāpi prāha nṛpaśreṣṭha mā vinīnasa āturaḥ /
pitā mama mahākrodhāt tridaśānapi nirdahet //
meaning:
सापि प्राह नृपश्रेष्ठ मा विनीनस आतुरः /
पिता मम महाक्रोधात् त्रिदशानपि निर्दहेत् //
text_mt:
She said: “O best of kings, do not perish in your affliction!
Out of his great wrath, my father would burn even the gods.

sanskrit_iast:
mūḍhabuddhe bhavān bhrātā mamāsi tvanayāplutaḥ /
bhaginī dharmataste 'haṃ bhavāñśiṣyaḥ piturmama //
meaning:
मूढबुद्धे भवान् भ्राता ममासि त्वनयाप्लुतः /
भगिनी धर्मतस्ते ऽहं भवाञ्शिष्यः पितुर्मम //
text_mt:
O foolish-minded one, you are my brother, yet you are overwhelmed by improper conduct!
By right I am your sister, and you are my father’s disciple.”

sanskrit_iast:
so 'brovīd bhīru māṃ śukraḥ kālena paridhakṣyati /
kāmāgnirnirdahati māmadyaiva tanumadhyame //
meaning:
सो ऽब्रोवीद् भीरु मां शुक्रः कालेन परिधक्ष्यति /
कामाग्निर्निर्दहति मामद्यैव तनुमध्यमे //
text_mt:
He replied: “O timid one, Śukra might burn me in time,
[but] the fire of desire burns me this very day, O slender-waisted girl!”

sanskrit_iast:
sā prāha daṇḍaṃ nṛpātiṃ muhūrta paripālaya /
tameva yācasva guruṃ sa te dāsyatyasaṃśayam //
meaning:
सा प्राह दण्डं नृपातिं मुहूर्त परिपालय /
तमेव याचस्व गुरुं स ते दास्यत्यसंशयम् //
text_mt:
She said to King Daṇḍa: “Wait for a moment;
ask the guru himself, and he will undoubtedly give me to you.”

sanskrit_iast:
daṇḍo 'bravīt sutanvaṅgi kālakṣepo na me kṣamaḥ /
cyutāvasarakartṛtve vighno jāyeta sundari //
meaning:
दण्डो ऽब्रवीत् सुतन्वङ्गि कालक्षेपो न मे क्षमः /
च्युतावसरकर्तृत्वे विघ्नो जायेत सुन्दरि //
text_mt:
Daṇḍa said: “O slender-limbed girl, delaying is not suitable for me;
an obstacle arises when one acts having missed the right moment, O beautiful one.”

sanskrit_iast:
tato 'bravīcca virajā nāhaṃ tvāṃ pārthivātmaja /
dātuṃ śaktā svamātmānaṃ svatantrā na hi yoṣitaḥ //
meaning:
ततो ऽब्रवीच्च विरजा नाहं त्वां पार्थिवात्मज /
दातुं शक्ता स्वमात्मानं स्वतन्त्रा न हि योषितः //
text_mt:
Then Arajā said: “O prince, I am not able
to give myself to you, for women are not independent.

sanskrit_iast:
kiṃ vā te bahunoktena mā tvaṃ nāśaṃ narādhipa /
gacchasva śukraśāpena sabhṛtyajñātibāndhavaḥ //
meaning:
किं वा ते बहुनोक्तेन मा त्वं नाशं नराधिप /
गच्छस्व शुक्रशापेन सभृत्यज्ञातिबान्धवः //
text_mt:
What is the use of speaking much to you? Do not go to destruction,
O ruler of men, together with your servants, kin, and relatives, by Śukra’s curse!”

sanskrit_iast:
tato ''bravīnnarapatiḥ sutanu śṛṇu ceṣṭitam /
citrāṅgadāyā yad vṛttaṃ purā devayuge śubhe //
meaning:
ततो 'ऽब्रवीन्नरपतिः सुतनु शृणु चेष्टितम् /
चित्राङ्गदाया यद् वृत्तं पुरा देवयुगे शुभे //
text_mt:
Then the king said: “O slender-waisted girl, hear the deed
of Citrāṅgadā that happened long ago in the auspicious age of the gods.

sanskrit_iast:
viśvakarṇasutā sādhvī nāmnā citrāṅgadābhavat /
rūpayauvanasaṃpannā padmahīneva padminī //
meaning:
विश्वकर्णसुता साध्वी नाम्ना चित्राङ्गदाभवत् /
रूपयौवनसंपन्ना पद्महीनेव पद्मिनी //
text_mt:
The virtuous daughter of Viśvakarman was named Citrāṅgadā;
she was endowed with beauty and youth, like a lotus-pond without lotuses.

sanskrit_iast:
sā kadācinmahāraṇyaṃ sakhībhiḥ parivāritā /
jagāma nemiṣaṃ nāma snātuṃ kamalalocanā //
sā snātumavatīrṇā ca athābhyāgānnareśvaraḥ /
sudevatanayo dhīmān suratho nāma nāmataḥ /
//
meaning:
सा कदाचिन्महारण्यं सखीभिः परिवारिता /
जगाम नेमिषं नाम स्नातुं कमललोचना //
सा स्नातुमवतीर्णा च अथाभ्यागान्नरेश्वरः /
सुदेवतनयो धीमान् सुरथो नाम नामतः /
//
text_mt:
Surrounded by her friends, that lotus-eyed girl once went
to the great forest named Naimiṣa to bathe.

As she stepped down to bathe, a ruler of men arrived,
the wise son of Sudeva named Suratha.

sanskrit_iast: tāṃ dadarśa ca tanvaṅgīṃ śubhāṅgo madanāturaḥ //
meaning: तां ददर्श च तन्वङ्गीं शुभाङ्गो मदनातुरः //
text_mt: Afflicted with love, the handsome [prince] beheld that slender-limbed girl.

sanskrit_iast:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā sā sakhīrāha vacanaṃ satyasaṃyutam /
asau narādhipasuto madanena sadarthyate //
meaning:
तं दृष्ट्वा सा सखीराह वचनं सत्यसंयुतम् /
असौ नराधिपसुतो मदनेन सदर्थ्यते //
text_mt:
Seeing him, she spoke truthful words to her friends:
‘That prince is tormented by desire for my sake,

sanskrit_iast:
madarthe ca kṣamaṃ me 'sya svapradānaṃ surūpiṇaḥ /
sakhyastāmabruvan bālā na pragalbha'si sundari //
meaning:
मदर्थे च क्षमं मे ऽस्य स्वप्रदानं सुरूपिणः /
सख्यस्तामब्रुवन् बाला न प्रगल्भऽसि सुन्दरि //
text_mt:
and it is fitting for me to give myself to this handsome man.’
Her friends said to her: ‘O girl, you are not bold, O beautiful one!

sanskrit_iast:
asvātantryaṃ tavāstīha pradāne svatmano 'naghe /
pitā tavāsti dharmiṣṭhaḥ sarvaśilpaviśāradaḥ //
meaning:
अस्वातन्त्र्यं तवास्तीह प्रदाने स्वत्मनो ऽनघे /
पिता तवास्ति धर्मिष्ठः सर्वशिल्पविशारदः //
text_mt:
You have no independence here in giving yourself away, O sinless one;
your father is most righteous and skilled in all crafts.

sanskrit_iast:
na te yuktamihātmānaṃ dātuṃ narapateḥ svayam /
etasminnantare rājā surathaḥ satyavāt sudhī //
meaning:
न ते युक्तमिहात्मानं दातुं नरपतेः स्वयम् /
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे राजा सुरथः सत्यवात् सुधी //
text_mt:
It is not proper for you to give yourself to the king on your own.’
In the meantime, the wise King Suratha, truthful in speech,

sanskrit_iast:
samabhyetyābrabīdenāṃ kandarpaśarapīḍitaḥ /
tvaṃ mugdhe mohayasi māṃ dṛṣṭyaiva madirekṣaṇe //
meaning:
समभ्येत्याब्रबीदेनां कन्दर्पशरपीडितः /
त्वं मुग्धे मोहयसि मां दृष्ट्यैव मदिरेक्षणे //
text_mt:
approached, tormented by Kandarpa’s arrows, and said to her:
‘O charming girl, you enchant me with your very gaze, O wine-eyed one!

sanskrit_iast:
tvaddṛṣṭirapātena smareṇābhyetya tāḍitaḥ /
tanmāṃ kucatale talpe abhiśāyitumarhasi //
meaning:
त्वद्दृष्टिरपातेन स्मरेणाभ्येत्य ताडितः /
तन्मां कुचतले तल्पे अभिशायितुमर्हसि //
text_mt:
Struck by Love who approached by the glance of your eyes,
you ought to let me lie upon the couch of your breast.

sanskrit_iast:
nocet pradhakṣyate kāmo bhūyo bhūyo 'tidarśanāt /
tataḥ sā cārusarvāṅgī rājño rājīvalocanā //
meaning:
नोचेत् प्रधक्ष्यते कामो भूयो भूयो ऽतिदर्शनात् /
ततः सा चारुसर्वाङ्गी राज्ञो राजीवलोचना //
text_mt:
Otherwise, desire will burn me again and again through intense gaze.’
Then that lotus-eyed girl of beautiful limbs,

sanskrit_iast:
vāryamāṇā sakhībhistu prādādātmānamātmanā /
evaṃ purā tayā tainvyā paritrātaḥ sa bhūpatiḥ //
meaning:
वार्यमाणा सखीभिस्तु प्रादादात्मानमात्मना /
एवं पुरा तया तैन्व्या परित्रातः स भूपतिः //
text_mt:
though restrained by her friends, gave herself on her own accord.
Thus was that king rescued long ago by that slender maiden.
